name.zh: 日常生活中的人工智能

description.zh: 发现日常生活中的人工智能：手机的人脸解锁、视频推荐、拼写自动纠错、能感应到人的自动门；这些技术看起来好像能“知道”一些事情。
description.en: Spotting AI in daily life: face unlock on a phone, video recommendations, spelling auto-correct, automatic doors that detect people; technology that seems to 'know' things

evidence.zh: 能列举至少五个日常生活中的人工智能应用实例
evidence.en: Identify at least five examples of AI in their daily life

evidence.zh: 说明这些技术是基于模式和数据运行的，而非魔法或真正的思考。
evidence.en: Explain that these technologies use patterns and data, not magic or real thinking

evidence.zh: 能举例说明AI为生活带来便利的一个方面，以及AI可能无法完美运作的一种情形。
evidence.en: Describe one way AI makes their life easier and one time it might not work perfectly

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否举出几件他们每天都会用到的东西——比如自动纠错或人脸解锁——并说明这些都是人工智能的例子？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} point out several things they use every day — like auto-correct or face unlock — and explain that these are examples of AI?

description.zh: 认识日常生活中的计算机——不只是笔记本电脑，还有手机、平板电脑、智能音箱、交通信号灯、洗衣机；了解是什么让一件物品成为计算机。
description.en: Identifying computers in everyday life — not just laptops but phones, tablets, smart speakers, traffic lights, washing machines; what makes something a computer

evidence.zh: 能列举至少五种含有计算机的日常物品
evidence.en: Point out at least five everyday objects that contain computers

evidence.zh: 解释所有计算机的共同特征（即它们都遵循指令并处理信息）
evidence.en: Explain what all computers have in common (they follow instructions and process information)

evidence.zh: 能按“含计算机”和“不含计算机”对一组物品进行分类。
evidence.en: Sort a set of objects into 'contains a computer' and 'does not contain a computer'

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否在家中四处观察，找出至少五样内含电脑的物品，包括那些看起来不像传统电脑的东西？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} look around your home and point out at least five things that have a computer inside them, including ones that don't look like traditional computers?

description.zh: 了解机器人到底是什么——不是科幻故事里的样子；认识工厂里的机器人、扫地机器人、手术机械臂；知道机器人会按照人们给出的指令行动。
description.en: What a robot really is — not the sci-fi version; robots in factories, robot vacuum cleaners, robot arms in surgery; that robots follow instructions given by people

evidence.zh: 描述机器人的定义（一种按指令执行任务的机器）
evidence.en: Describe what a robot is (a machine that follows instructions to do a task)

evidence.zh: 能列举至少三种现实中的机器人并说明其功能。
evidence.en: Name at least three real robots and what they do

evidence.zh: 能说明机器人没有生命和情感，只是按人类编写的程序指令运行。
evidence.en: Explain that robots are not alive and do not have feelings — they follow instructions people wrote

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到一台扫地机器人，能不能说出它和真人打扫有什么不同——它是按照指令行事，而不是自己会思考？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} saw a robot vacuum cleaner, could they explain how it's different from a person cleaning — that it follows instructions rather than thinking for itself?

name.zh: 智能设备与非智能设备

description.zh: 把物品分成“智能”（能感知并做出反应）和“非智能”（只会固定地工作）两类，比如烤面包机和智能音箱；初步了解有些机器能够感知周围世界并做出反应。
description.en: Sorting objects into 'smart' (can sense and respond) and 'not smart' (just sits there); a toaster vs a smart speaker; introduction to the idea that some machines can sense and respond to the world

evidence.zh: 将物体分为“智能”（能对输入作出反应）和“非智能”（每次执行相同操作）两类。
evidence.en: Sort a set of objects into 'smart' (responds to input) and 'not smart' (does the same thing every time)

evidence.zh: 能说出智能音箱与普通收音机的区别
evidence.en: Explain what makes a smart speaker different from a regular radio

evidence.zh: 能举例说明一种能感知并做出反应的机器（如自动门、感应灯）。
evidence.en: Give an example of a machine that senses something and responds (automatic door, motion-sensor light)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释普通电灯开关与走进房间就自动亮起的开关之间的区别？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} explain the difference between a normal light switch and one that turns on automatically when you walk into a room?

description.zh: 为日常任务编写一步步的指令，比如做三明治、刷牙；了解如果指令错了或少了一步，事情就会出问题；知道计算机会严格按照指令执行。
description.en: Step-by-step instructions for everyday tasks (making a sandwich, brushing teeth); that if instructions are wrong or missing, things go wrong; computers follow instructions exactly

evidence.zh: 能编写或口述简单的日常任务分步指令
evidence.en: Write or describe step-by-step instructions for a simple everyday task

evidence.zh: 预测步骤遗漏或顺序错误可能导致的后果
evidence.en: Predict what goes wrong if a step is missing or in the wrong order

evidence.zh: 能说明计算机严格按指令执行——它无法猜测你的意图
evidence.en: Explain that a computer follows instructions exactly — it cannot guess what you meant

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果让{{name}}写一份制作果酱三明治的说明，精确到连机器人都能照着做，他能把每一个步骤都写进去吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} had to write instructions for making a jam sandwich so precise that even a robot could follow them, could they include every single step?

name.zh: 语音助手及其工作原理
name.en: Voice Assistants and How They Work

description.zh: 当你和Alexa、Siri或谷歌助手说话时会发生什么：它们会听、试着理解、查找答案；有时也会出错；它们是工具，不是有生命的。
description.en: What happens when you talk to Alexa, Siri, or Google Assistant; they listen, try to understand, look up answers; sometimes they get it wrong; they are tools, not alive

evidence.zh: 描述向语音助手提问的过程（倾听、处理词语、查找答案、语音回复）。
evidence.en: Describe the steps that happen when you ask a voice assistant a question (it listens, processes words, finds an answer, speaks back)

evidence.zh: 能举例说明语音助手可能出错的情况。
evidence.en: Give an example of a time a voice assistant might get something wrong

evidence.zh: 能指出语音助手是计算机程序而非真人——它没有理解能力，也没有情感。
evidence.en: Explain that a voice assistant is a computer program, not a person — it doesn't understand or feel

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}向Alexa或Siri提问却得到了错误答案，他们能解释为什么语音助手有时会出错吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} asked Alexa or Siri a question and got a wrong answer, could they explain why the voice assistant sometimes makes mistakes?

name.zh: 电脑游戏中的人工智能

description.zh: 电脑游戏角色如何“决定”做什么；简单的基于规则的AI和会学习的AI；非玩家角色（NPC）、难度调节；国际象棋或棋类游戏中作为对手的AI。
description.en: How computer game characters 'decide' what to do; simple rule-based AI vs learning AI; NPCs, difficulty adjustment; AI as the opponent in chess or board games

evidence.zh: 说明游戏中电脑对手的决策机制
evidence.en: Explain how a computer opponent in a game decides its moves

evidence.zh: 描述遵循固定规则的游戏角色与从玩家行为中学习的游戏角色之间的区别
evidence.en: Describe the difference between a game character that follows fixed rules and one that learns from the player

evidence.zh: 能举例说明AI如何提升游戏趣味性（如动态调整难度、自动生成关卡）。
evidence.en: Give an example of AI making a game more fun (adjusting difficulty, generating levels)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}在电脑上玩电子游戏时，他们能否解释游戏角色是如何“决定”做什么的？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} plays a video game against the computer, could they explain how the game's characters 'decide' what to do?

name.zh: 人工智能的错误与局限

description.zh: 机器也会出错；它们只知道被展示过的内容；不好的训练数据会导致不好的结果；AI不是魔法——只是对数据进行数学运算；展示边缘情况和失败案例。
description.en: Machines make mistakes; they only know what they've been shown; bad training data leads to bad results; AI is not magic — just maths on data; showing edge cases and failures

evidence.zh: 能举例说明AI出错的情况（如语音助手听错、自动纠错出错、推荐错误）
evidence.en: Give an example of AI making a mistake (voice assistant mishearing, auto-correct error, wrong recommendation)

evidence.zh: 能指出AI的错误源于训练数据的缺失或错误
evidence.en: Explain that AI mistakes happen because of gaps or errors in training data

evidence.zh: 能说明AI并非魔法——它遵循应用于数据的数学规则
evidence.en: Describe why AI is not magic — it follows mathematical rules applied to data

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果AI把一张玛芬蛋糕的图片错认成吉娃娃，{{name}}能解释为什么会发生这种错误吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If an AI incorrectly identified a picture of a muffin as a chihuahua, could {{name}} explain why that kind of mistake happens?

description.zh: 什么是数据：计算机使用的信息——数字、文字、图片、声音；计算机知道的一切都来自人们提供的数据。
description.en: What data is: information that computers use — numbers, words, pictures, sounds; everything a computer knows comes from data that people give it

evidence.zh: 能将数据定义为存储在计算机中的信息（数字、文本、图像、声音）
evidence.en: Define data as information stored in a computer (numbers, text, images, sounds)

evidence.zh: 能列举至少三个自己每天产生的数据实例（如照片、消息、搜索记录）
evidence.en: Give at least three examples of data they create every day (photos, messages, search queries)

evidence.zh: 能说明计算机只能处理输入的信息，本身不具备知识。
evidence.en: Explain that a computer only knows what it has been given — it has no knowledge of its own

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释“数据”的含义，并举例说明他们每次使用手机或电脑时会产生哪些数据？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} explain what 'data' means and give examples of data they create every time they use a phone or computer?

description.zh: 比较人类和机器的能力：创造力、共情力、常识与速度、记忆、重复劳动；简单介绍图灵测试；人类有什么独特之处。
description.en: Comparing human and machine capabilities: creativity, empathy, common sense vs speed, memory, repetition; the Turing Test (simplified); what makes humans unique

evidence.zh: 至少能列举三项人类优于计算机的能力（创造力、同理心、常识）。
evidence.en: Name at least three things humans are better at than computers (creativity, empathy, common sense)

evidence.zh: 能列举计算机优于人类的至少三个方面（运算速度、存储容量、重复性任务）。
evidence.en: Name at least three things computers are better at than humans (speed, memory, repetitive tasks)

evidence.zh: 能用通俗语言解释图灵测试（即计算机能否让人误以为它是人类）。
evidence.en: Describe the Turing Test in simple terms (can a computer fool a person into thinking it's human?)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释一下，人类在哪些方面仍然优于计算机，而计算机又能做哪些人类无法做到的事情？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} explain what humans are still better at than computers and what computers can do that humans can't?

description.zh: 从概念层面了解机器学习的运作原理：给计算机展示很多示例，它会从中找到规律，之后就能对新事物做出预测；可以借助可教机器（Teachable Machine）或同类工具获得动手实操的体验
description.en: How machine learning works at a conceptual level: show the computer many examples, it finds patterns, then it makes predictions about new things; hands-on experience with Teachable Machine or similar tool

evidence.zh: 能用自己的话简单说明机器学习的三个步骤（举例、找规律、做预测）。
evidence.en: Describe the three steps of machine learning in simple terms (give examples, find patterns, make predictions)

evidence.zh: 能使用Teachable Machine等工具训练简单模型，并描述训练结果。
evidence.en: Train a simple model using a tool like Teachable Machine and describe what happened

evidence.zh: 解释为何提供更多更好的示例能提高模型的准确性
evidence.en: Explain why showing more and better examples makes the model more accurate

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能不能讲一讲，你是怎么教计算机识别东西的——是不是给它看很多例子，直到它发现规律？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} describe how you teach a computer to recognise something — by showing it lots of examples until it spots the pattern?

description.zh: 人类非常擅长发现模式，计算机也可以学习识别模式，但它们需要大量的示例才能做到；归类和分类活动是机器学习的基础。
description.en: Humans are great at spotting patterns; computers can learn to spot patterns too, but they need lots of examples; sorting and classification activities as the basis of machine learning

evidence.zh: 能根据某一标准对一组物品进行分类，并说明分类的依据。
evidence.en: Sort a set of items into categories and explain the rules they used

evidence.zh: 能说明计算机是通过观察大量样本来学习模式的
evidence.en: Explain that computers learn patterns by looking at many examples

evidence.zh: 解释为什么计算机需要比人类更多的示例才能学会相同的模式
evidence.en: Describe why a computer needs more examples than a human to learn the same pattern

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果你给{{name}}看猫和狗的图片，他们能否解释计算机是如何学会区分猫和狗的——以及为什么计算机需要比人多得多的图片才能学会？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you showed {{name}} pictures of cats and dogs, could they explain how a computer could learn to tell them apart — and why it would need many more pictures than a person would?

description.zh: 学习推荐系统的工作原理：YouTube、网飞、购物网站等平台会追踪你点击过的内容，从中总结规律；认识什么是信息茧房；学会区分有用的推荐和恶意操纵的区别
description.en: How recommendation systems work: YouTube, Netflix, and shop websites track what you click and find patterns; filter bubbles; the difference between helpful suggestions and manipulation

evidence.zh: 解释YouTube或Netflix如何决定下一步推荐内容
evidence.en: Explain how YouTube or Netflix decides what to suggest next

evidence.zh: 描述“过滤气泡”的概念（即仅接触与自身既有偏好相似的内容）
evidence.en: Describe what a 'filter bubble' is (only seeing things similar to what you already like)

evidence.zh: 说出推荐系统的一个优点和一个风险
evidence.en: Give one benefit and one risk of recommendation systems

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否理解YouTube为何会持续推荐与已观看视频相似的内容，并能解释推荐系统的工作原理？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} understand why YouTube keeps suggesting similar videos to ones they've watched, and could they explain how the recommendation system works?

description.zh: 探讨人工智能是否可以做出与人们切身利益相关的重要决策，例如招聘、贷款审批、司法判定等；了解人工智能做出不公平决策时的责任归属；初步认识算法公平的概念。
description.en: Whether AI should make important decisions about people: jobs, loans, justice; who is responsible when AI makes unfair decisions; introduction to algorithmic fairness

evidence.zh: 能举例说明AI可能参与的重要决策（如招聘、医疗诊断、贷款审批）。
evidence.en: Give an example of an important decision that AI might help make (hiring, medical diagnosis, loan approval)

evidence.zh: 解释在系统存在偏见的情况下，用AI替代人类决策为何会带来风险
evidence.en: Explain why letting AI make decisions about people can be risky if the system is biased

evidence.zh: 能识别AI系统作出不公正决策时的责任主体。
evidence.en: Suggest who should be responsible if an AI system makes an unfair decision

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}知道是计算机程序在决定谁获得面试机会，他们能否解释为什么这可能不公平，以及谁应该为此负责？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} learned that a computer program was deciding who gets a job interview, could they explain why that might be unfair and who should be responsible?

description.zh: 训练人工智能模型需要消耗大量能源与水资源，数据中心也会产生相应的环境成本；同时人工智能也能助力环境保护，例如预测天气、监测森林砍伐、优化能源利用等；需要客观看待其中的利弊权衡。
description.en: AI needs huge amounts of energy and water to train; data centres and their environmental cost; but AI can also help — predicting weather, monitoring deforestation, optimising energy; trade-offs

evidence.zh: 能说明训练AI模型会消耗大量电力和水资源
evidence.en: Explain that training AI models uses a lot of electricity and water

evidence.zh: 至少能列举两个AI在环保领域的应用实例
evidence.en: Give at least two examples of AI being used to help the environment

evidence.zh: 描述人工智能环境成本与环境效益之间的权衡
evidence.en: Describe the trade-off between AI's environmental cost and its environmental benefits

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释人工智能既需要消耗大量能源才能运行，又可以用于帮助保护环境，并讨论这种权衡是否值得？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} explain that AI needs a lot of energy to work but can also be used to help protect the environment, and discuss whether the trade-off is worth it?

name.en: AI and the Future of Work

description.zh: 人工智能如何改变职场：一些工作会消失，新的工作会出现，许多工作会发生变化；人工智能（暂时）还不能做的工作；在人工智能时代哪些技能很重要。
description.en: How AI is changing the world of work: some jobs disappear, new ones are created, many change; jobs AI can't do (yet); what skills matter in an AI world

evidence.zh: 至少列举两个AI正在改变或取代的职业，以及两个AI催生的新职业。
evidence.en: Name at least two jobs that AI is changing or replacing and two new jobs AI has created

evidence.zh: 解释创造力、共情力和问题解决能力在人工智能时代日益重要的原因
evidence.en: Explain why creativity, empathy, and problem-solving are skills that matter more in an AI world

evidence.zh: 能举例说明AI如何改变某一具体职业（如教师、医生、农民），但不替代该职业。
evidence.en: Describe how AI might change a specific job they know about (teacher, doctor, farmer) without replacing it

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释人工智能可能如何改变人们未来的工作方式，以及哪些人类技能仍将重要？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} explain how AI might change the way people work in the future and which human skills will still be important?

name.zh: 人工智能数据收集与隐私

description.zh: 人工智能系统会收集哪些关于你的数据；谁拥有这些数据，以及为什么这很重要；Cookie、网络跟踪、智能音箱一直在收音；你的数据很有价值。
description.en: What data AI systems collect about you; who has it and why it matters; cookies, tracking, smart speakers always listening; your data is valuable

evidence.zh: 至少列举出AI系统收集的三类个人数据。
evidence.en: Name at least three types of personal data that AI systems collect

evidence.zh: 说明个人数据对公司的价值
evidence.en: Explain why personal data is valuable to companies

evidence.zh: 描述一种可采取的在线隐私保护措施
evidence.en: Describe one step they can take to protect their privacy online

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否理解应用程序和网站会收集其在线行为信息，并能解释为什么这一点很重要？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} understand that apps and websites collect information about what they do online, and could they explain why that matters?

name.zh: 人工智能系统中的偏见

description.zh: 如果训练数据存在偏见，人工智能也会产生偏见；例子包括人脸识别对某些肤色识别效果更好、翻译会默认某种性别；偏见从何而来，以及我们能否解决它。
description.en: If training data is biased, AI will be biased; examples: facial recognition working better for some skin tones, translation assuming gender; where bias comes from and whether we can fix it

evidence.zh: 能结合生活实例解释AI偏见。
evidence.en: Explain what bias in AI means using a real-world example

evidence.zh: 描述训练数据偏差如何导致AI结果偏差
evidence.en: Describe how biased training data leads to biased AI results

evidence.zh: 能提出减少AI系统偏见的方法（如使用更多样化的数据、在不同群体中进行测试）
evidence.en: Suggest one way to reduce bias in an AI system (use more diverse data, test with different groups)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释一下，为什么主要用浅肤色人脸照片训练出来的人工智能，在深肤色人群身上可能效果不佳？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} explain why an AI trained mostly on photos of light-skinned faces might not work as well for people with darker skin?

name.zh: 深度伪造与人工智能生成内容

description.zh: 深度伪造、人工智能生成的图片和文本；如何辨别它们以及它们为什么重要；核查信息来源的重要性；网络上的内容并不都是真实的。
description.en: Deepfakes, AI-generated images and text; how to spot them and why they matter; the importance of checking sources; not everything online is real

evidence.zh: 能解释深度伪造的定义，并能举例说明AI生成内容。
evidence.en: Explain what a deepfake is and give an example of AI-generated content

evidence.zh: 至少列举两条可能表明图像或文本由AI生成的线索
evidence.en: Describe at least two clues that might reveal an image or text was AI-generated

evidence.zh: 解释AI能生成逼真虚假内容为何重要
evidence.en: Explain why it matters that AI can create realistic fake content

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在网上看到一张令人惊叹的照片，他们会想到去质疑这张照片可能是由AI生成的，而不是用相机拍摄的吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} saw an amazing photo online, would they think to question whether it might have been created by AI rather than captured by a camera?

name.zh: 设计公平的人工智能规则

description.zh: 将设计思维应用于人工智能伦理：如果你要设计一个人工智能系统，你会给它制定什么规则？它应该帮助谁？哪些事情是不允许它做的？
description.en: Design thinking applied to AI ethics: if you were designing an AI system, what rules would you give it? Who should it help? What should it not be allowed to do?

evidence.zh: 能为自主设计的AI系统假设提出至少三条规则
evidence.en: Propose at least three rules for a hypothetical AI system they are designing

evidence.zh: 说明AI设计者为何要考虑可能受影响的群体，而不只是关注受益方。
evidence.en: Explain why AI designers need to think about who might be harmed, not just who benefits

evidence.zh: 能分别举例说明AI被负责任使用和未被负责任使用的真实案例。
evidence.en: Describe one real example of AI being used responsibly and one where it was not

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}正在为学校设计一个AI助手，他们能想到哪些规则来确保它对每个人都公平且有帮助？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was designing an AI assistant for their school, could they think of rules to make sure it was fair and helpful for everyone?

description.zh: 了解十年后人工智能可能的发展方向与应用场景；探讨人们对人工智能的期待与担忧；认识到儿童是未来人工智能的设计者与决策参与者，建立充满信心、主动参与的正向认知。
description.en: What AI might do in 10 years; what we want it to do and what we're worried about; children as future designers and decision-makers about AI; hopeful, empowered framing

evidence.zh: 至少描述两种未来可能实现但目前尚不存在的AI应用方式
evidence.en: Describe at least two ways AI might be used in the future that don't exist yet

evidence.zh: 说出希望AI做的一件事和希望AI不做的一件事
evidence.en: Explain one thing they would want AI to do and one thing they would want it not to do

evidence.zh: 阐明为何青少年理解人工智能至关重要——因为他们将决定人工智能的使用方式。
evidence.en: Describe why it matters that young people understand AI — because they will shape how it is used

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否就他们希望未来AI做什么以及他们担心什么进行深思熟虑的对话？
assessmentPrompt.en: Could {{name}} have a thoughtful conversation about what they'd want AI to do in the future and what they'd be worried about?

description.zh: 要明白阅读的核心是读懂内容含义，可不只是把单词读准就可以哦。如果只会拼读文本内容却完全不懂其中的意思，那不叫真正的阅读哦。
description.en: Understand that reading is about making meaning, not just saying words correctly — a text that can be decoded but not understood has not been read

evidence.zh: 掌握简单阅读观（Gough & Tunmer）
evidence.en: Simple View of Reading (Gough & Tunmer)

evidence.zh: 阅读理解研究中理解与解码的分离
evidence.en: reading comprehension research on comprehension-decoding separation

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}能正确朗读一段内容，但读完后却说不出它讲了什么，他是否意识到阅读意味着理解——而不仅仅是把字念出来？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} reads something aloud correctly but then can't tell you what it was about, do they recognise that reading means understanding — not just saying the words?

description.zh: 你要留意认读单词和真正读懂内容的区别哦——如果发现自己读完了所有单词，却没弄懂内容讲的是什么，就要主动想办法搞明白~
description.en: Notice the difference between decoding words and actually understanding them — recognise when you've read the words but not grasped the meaning, and do something about it

evidence.zh: 理解监控研究
evidence.en: comprehension monitoring research

evidence.zh: 阅读理解中的元认知监控（MDPI 2024）
evidence.en: Metacognitive Monitoring in Reading Comprehension (MDPI 2024)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在{{name}}读完一段文字或听完一段讲解后，他们是否能意识到自己其实并没有真正理解——而不是不懂装懂地继续下去？
assessmentPrompt.en: After {{name}} reads a paragraph or listens to an explanation, do they notice when they haven't really understood it — rather than just carrying on as if they had?

description.zh: 认识作者在遣词、文本结构、语气、叙事视角上的刻意安排，会对身为读者的你产生哪些特定影响
description.en: Recognise how an author's deliberate choices — of words, structure, tone, and perspective — create particular effects on you as a reader

evidence.zh: 分析作者意图
evidence.en: authorial awareness research

evidence.zh: 理解作者意图（菲尔金斯）
evidence.en: Understanding Author's Purpose (Firkins)

evidence.zh: 5-8岁儿童的合作式多层文本解读
evidence.en: collaborative multilayered text interpretation in 5-8 year olds

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}阅读一本书或一篇文章时，他们是否会关注并评价作者为何选择以某种方式写作——以及这对他们作为读者产生了什么影响？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} reads a book or article, do they ever notice and comment on why the author chose to write it a certain way — and what effect that has on them as a reader?

description.zh: 学会区分文本明确表述的内容，和你自己推断、假设或是脑补出的内容，分清二者的区别是做到对文本真实理解的基础。
description.en: Distinguish between what a text explicitly says and what you have inferred, assumed, or read in — knowing which is which is fundamental to honest comprehension

evidence.zh: 推理与字面理解发展研究
evidence.en: inference vs literal comprehension development research

evidence.zh: 在线推断与理解监控（PMC 2021）
evidence.en: online inference making and comprehension monitoring (PMC 2021)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在{{name}}读完一个故事或文章后，他们能否区分哪些内容是文本中实际读到的，哪些是自己推断或假设出来的？
assessmentPrompt.en: After {{name}} reads a story or article, can they tell you which parts they actually read in the text and which parts they worked out or assumed for themselves?

name.zh: 认识你尚未掌握的知识

description.zh: 主动排查自己的词汇缺口——留意那些你一知半解的单词，分清哪些是你已经熟练掌握的知识、哪些是你没有把握的内容，同时学习解决这类知识不确定性的实用方法
description.en: Monitor your own vocabulary gaps — notice words you half-know, distinguish confident from uncertain knowledge, and develop strategies to resolve the uncertainty

evidence.zh: 生词识别评估研究（二年级及以上）
evidence.en: Noticing Unfamiliar Words Assessment research (grade 2+)

evidence.zh: 词汇意识与词汇元认知研究
evidence.en: word consciousness and vocabulary metacognition research

evidence.zh: 能制作词汇知识电子书（PMC 2019）
evidence.en: Building Word Knowledge e-Book (PMC 2019)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}遇到一个似懂非懂的词——能猜出大致意思但不太确定——他们能否意识到这个知识缺口并主动采取措施，比如查词典或询问？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} comes across a word they half-know — where they can guess the meaning but aren't sure — do they notice that gap and do something about it, like looking it up or asking?

description.zh: 评估你自己写的英语作文是否能给读者传递你想要的效果，不要只检查拼写、语法是否正确，还要判断内容是不是真的达到了你预想的表达作用
description.en: Evaluate whether your own writing achieves the effect you intended on a reader — go beyond checking for correctness to asking whether it actually works

evidence.zh: 撰写自我评估报告（3-5年级）
evidence.en: writing self-evaluation research grades 3-5

evidence.zh: 写作元认知意识（《前沿》2025）
evidence.en: metacognitive awareness of writing (Frontiers 2025)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在{{name}}写完一篇故事、一封信或一篇议论文之后，他们是否会思考这篇文章能否对读者产生他们想要的效果，而不仅仅是拼写是否正确？
assessmentPrompt.en: After {{name}} writes something — a story, a letter, a persuasive piece — do they think about whether it would have the effect they wanted on a reader, not just whether the spelling is right?

description.zh: 站在语言使用者的角度进行自我反思：你的阅读、写作、口语表达是如何根据沟通对象、表达目的和场景灵活调整的，以及你想要进一步提升的方向
description.en: Reflect on yourself as a language user — how your reading, writing, and speaking shift across audiences, purposes, and contexts, and where you want to develop further

evidence.zh: 元语言意识发展
evidence.en: metalinguistic awareness development

evidence.zh: 读者意识与语域研究
evidence.en: register and audience awareness research

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否能意识到自己在不同情境下的沟通方式差异——比如写作业和给朋友发短信，或在辩论中发言和在家闲聊——并且能否解释这些差异为何重要？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} notice how they communicate differently in different situations — writing for school versus texting a friend, or speaking in a debate versus chatting at home — and can they explain why those differences matter?

description.zh: 明白单词组合在一起就能构成句子，句子可以表达完整的想法；会在说话和书写时使用完整句子，还能扩充句子让内容更丰富。
description.en: Understand that words combine to make sentences — a sentence expresses a complete thought; produce and expand complete sentences in speech and writing

evidence.zh: 区分完整句与残缺句
evidence.en: Distinguish between complete sentences and fragments

evidence.zh: 能写出主谓结构完整的句子
evidence.en: Compose a complete sentence with a subject and verb

evidence.zh: 通过添加细节扩展简单句
evidence.en: Expand a simple sentence by adding detail

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}说出“那只狗”这样的短语，他们能否识别出这不是一个完整的句子，并补充词语使其表达完整意思，例如“那只狗跑得很快”？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} says something like "The dog", can they tell you that's not a complete sentence — and add words to make it say something like "The dog ran fast"?

description.zh: 学习正确使用不定冠词：发音以辅音音素开头的单词前用「a」，发音以元音音素开头的单词前用「an」，示例：a rock（一块石头）、an open box（一个开着的盒子）、an hour（一小时）、a unicorn（一只独角兽）
description.en: Use the correct form of the indefinite article — 'a' before words beginning with a consonant sound and 'an' before words beginning with a vowel sound (e.g., a rock, an open box, an hour, a unicorn)

evidence.zh: 能正确使用不定冠词a/an：辅音音素前用a，元音音素前用an（如a ball、an egg、an umbrella）。
evidence.en: Choose 'a' or 'an' correctly before nouns beginning with consonant or vowel sounds (e.g., 'a ball', 'an egg', 'an umbrella')

evidence.zh: 能运用该规则判断拼写与发音不一致的疑难词（如“an hour”，因/h/不发音；“a uniform”，因/juː/以辅音音素开头）。
evidence.en: Apply the rule to tricky words where spelling and sound differ (e.g., 'an hour' because /h/ is silent, 'a uniform' because /juː/ starts with a consonant sound)

evidence.zh: 能纠正所给句子中a/an的用法错误（如将“a orange”改为“an orange”）。
evidence.en: Correct errors in a/an usage in given sentences (e.g., change 'a orange' to 'an orange')

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}写作时，他们是否能自动在辅音音素开头的单词前选用“a”，在元音音素开头的单词前选用“an”——比如“a cat”，但“an apple”或“an hour”？

description.zh: 学习使用连词（when、before、after、while、so、because）、副词（then、next、soon、therefore）和介词（before、after、during、in、because of），在单句内或句与句之间表达时间、地点和原因

evidence.zh: 能在短语中正确使用时间介词和原因介词（如“during the lesson”“before lunch”“because of the rain”）。

description.zh: 理解并会运用抽象名词，这类名词指代的是无法通过感官（看、听、闻、尝、摸）感知的想法、品质、状态类概念
description.en: Understand and use abstract nouns to name ideas, qualities, and states that cannot be perceived by the senses

evidence.zh: 能准确区分并归类“freedom、table、courage、pencil、childhood”等词为抽象名词或具体名词。
evidence.en: Sort words like 'freedom', 'table', 'courage', 'pencil', 'childhood' into abstract and concrete noun categories

evidence.zh: 能正确选用抽象名词填空：Her _____ (brave → bravery) inspired the whole team。
evidence.en: Complete sentences using appropriate abstract nouns: 'Her _____ (brave → bravery) inspired the whole team'

evidence.zh: 能写出三个句子，每句各含一个不同的抽象名词（如“诚实”“友谊”“幸福”）。
evidence.en: Write three sentences each containing a different abstract noun (e.g. 'honesty', 'friendship', 'happiness')

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否用“善良”“自由”或“快乐”这类抽象名词造句，并理解这些词虽然是名词，却看不见、摸不着？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} write a sentence using an abstract word like "kindness", "freedom", or "happiness" — knowing these are nouns even though you can't touch or see them?

description.zh: 掌握单句内部及句与句之间的主谓一致、代词与先行词一致规则
description.en: Ensure subject-verb agreement and pronoun-antecedent agreement within and across sentences

evidence.zh: 能识别并改正“The group of children were laughing”中的主谓一致错误（改为was），并能说明group为单数主语。
evidence.en: Correct 'The group of children were laughing' to 'The group of children was laughing' and explain the singular subject

evidence.zh: 能在“Each student must bring ____ (his or her / their) book”中选出正确代词，并解释其与先行词的指代关系。
evidence.en: Choose the correct pronoun in 'Each student must bring ____ (his or her / their) book' and explain the antecedent link

evidence.zh: 能识别并修改短段落中的三处一致性错误，并说明每处修改的理由。
evidence.en: Identify and fix three agreement errors in a short paragraph, explaining each correction

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}写下“Each of the players have their own locker”，他能否发现错误并将其改为“has their own locker”——确保动词与主语一致？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} writes "Each of the players have their own locker", can they spot the error and fix it to "has their own locker" — making sure the verb matches the subject?

evidence.zh: 能正确运用比较副词（如“more carefully”）和最高级形容词（如“tallest”）造句。

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}正在比较三样东西——比如他们读过的三本书——他们能否正确地说一本是“good”，另一本是“better”，而最好的一本是“the best”？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} is comparing three things — like three books they've read — can they correctly say one is "good", another is "better", and the best one is "the best"?

description.zh: 借助修饰性形容词、名词和介词短语对名词短语进行扩展，为表述补充更多细节
description.en: Expand noun phrases with modifying adjectives, nouns, and preposition phrases to add detail

evidence.zh: 运用形容词、名词和介词短语，将“the teacher”扩展为“the strict maths teacher with curly hair”。
evidence.en: Expand 'the teacher' to 'the strict maths teacher with curly hair' using adjective, noun, and preposition phrase

evidence.zh: 能写出包含至少三个修饰语的名词短语的句子，如“河上那座古老的石桥”。
evidence.en: Write a sentence containing a noun phrase with at least three modifiers, e.g. 'the old stone bridge over the river'

evidence.zh: 能识别“the tiny grey kitten under the table”中的中心词及其修饰语。
evidence.en: Identify the head noun and its modifiers in 'the tiny grey kitten under the table'

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}在写作中描述某样事物时，他们是否会进行丰富的描写——比如写“那个穿灰色大衣的高个子男人”，而不只是写“那个男人”？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} describes something in a piece of writing, do they build up a rich description — like "the tall man with the grey coat" rather than just "the man"?

description.zh: 学习使用前置状语丰富句子开头形式，掌握前置状语后的逗号使用规则
description.en: Use fronted adverbials to vary sentence openings and punctuate them with commas

evidence.zh: 能用以时间状语开头的句子造句，如“Later that day, the children ran home”。
evidence.en: Write a sentence beginning with a time adverbial, e.g. 'Later that day, the children ran home'

evidence.zh: 能将“The fox crept through the garden at midnight”改写为状语前置且逗号使用正确的句子。
evidence.en: Rewrite 'The fox crept through the garden at midnight' with the adverbial fronted and a comma placed correctly

evidence.zh: 识别并改正“Before breakfast she packed her bag”中前置状语后缺失的逗号。

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}写故事或报告时，他们有时会用“午饭后，”或“狐狸悄悄地靠近了，”这样的短语作为句子开头，并在开头短语后加逗号吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} writes a story or a report, do they sometimes start a sentence with a phrase like "After lunch," or "Quietly, the fox moved closer," — and put a comma after that opening phrase?

name.zh: 语法术语：代词与限定词

description.zh: 掌握并运用四年级要求的语法术语，包括限定词、代词、物主代词和状语
description.en: Know and use Year 4 grammar terminology including determiner, pronoun, possessive pronoun, and adverbial

evidence.zh: 准确标注“She quickly opened her present on the table”中的限定词、代词和状语。
evidence.en: Label the determiner, pronoun, and adverbial in 'She quickly opened her present on the table'

evidence.zh: 能说明名词性物主代词（如“mine”“theirs”）与主格代词（如“I”“they”）的区别。
evidence.en: Explain the difference between a possessive pronoun ('mine', 'theirs') and other pronouns ('I', 'they')

evidence.zh: 在讨论同学作文时，能正确使用“限定词”和“状语”两个术语。
evidence.en: Use the terms 'determiner' and 'adverbial' accurately when discussing a classmate's writing

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果你让{{name}}在一个句子里找出“限定词”或“物主代词”，他们能指出来并解释它的作用吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you ask {{name}} to find a "determiner" or a "possessive pronoun" in a sentence, can they point one out and explain what job it does?

name.zh: 名词的复数与所有格辨析

description.zh: 学会区分名词的复数后缀-s和所有格后缀-'s的不同用法
description.en: Distinguish between the plural -s suffix and the possessive -'s suffix in nouns

evidence.zh: 能区分并归类“dogs”“dog's”“dogs'”等词为复数、单数所有格和复数所有格。
evidence.en: Sort words like 'dogs', 'dog's', and 'dogs'' into plural, singular possessive, and plural possessive categories

evidence.zh: 能解释“the cats bowl”的错误原因，并根据给定含义写出正确形式（“the cat's bowl”或“the cats' bowl”）。
evidence.en: Explain why 'the cats bowl' is incorrect and supply the correct form ('the cat's bowl' or 'the cats' bowl') for a given meaning

evidence.zh: 用同一名词写两个句子——一句用复数形式，一句用所有格形式。
evidence.en: Write two sentences using the same noun — one as a plural and one as a possessive

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否区分“the girls' coats”（表示多个女孩的）和“the girls are coming”（仅表示复数）——并正确写出两者，不混淆撇号？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} tell the difference between "the girls' coats" (belonging to many girls) and "the girls are coming" (just a plural) — and write each one correctly without mixing up the apostrophe?

name.zh: 一般过去时、一般现在时和一般将来时

description.zh: 写作时能够正确构造并连贯使用一般过去时、一般现在时和一般将来时三种动词时态，保持全文时态统一
description.en: Form and use the simple past, present, and future verb tenses consistently in writing

evidence.zh: 能将“I walk to school”改写为过去时（“I walked”）和将来时（“I will walk”）。
evidence.en: Rewrite 'I walk to school' in past tense ('I walked') and future tense ('I will walk')

evidence.zh: 识别并改正“Yesterday she walks to the shop and bought milk”中时态不一致的错误。
evidence.en: Identify and correct inconsistent tense in 'Yesterday she walks to the shop and bought milk'

evidence.zh: 写一个三句话的段落，全段保持将来时态一致。
evidence.en: Write a three-sentence paragraph maintaining consistent future tense throughout

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}描述昨天发生的事、现在正在发生的事以及明天将要发生的事时，他们能否针对不同时间正确变化动词——比如“I walked”、“I walk”和“I will walk”？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} writes about something that happened yesterday, something happening now, and something that will happen tomorrow, do they change the verb correctly for each time — like "I walked", "I walk", and "I will walk"?

description.zh: 学习使用标准英语的动词变形，替换不规范的地域性动词表达
description.en: Use Standard English verb inflections in place of non-standard local forms

evidence.zh: 能识别并纠正“we was playing”为“we were playing”，并说明书面表达中需使用标准形式的理由。
evidence.en: Correct 'we was playing' to 'we were playing' and explain why the standard form is needed in writing

evidence.zh: 能在“I did / I done”“she has / she have”“they were / they was”等成对形式中选出标准形式。
evidence.en: Choose the standard form in pairs such as 'I did / I done', 'she has / she have', 'they were / they was'

evidence.zh: 改写短文，将其中的三处非标准动词形式改为标准英语形式。
evidence.en: Rewrite a short passage replacing three non-standard verb forms with their Standard English equivalents

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在对话中有时会说“we was”或“they done it”，那么他们在学校作业中是否知道要写成“we were”和“they did it”——使用标准书面英语？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sometimes says "we was" or "they done it" in conversation, do they know to write "we were" and "they did it" in their schoolwork — using standard written English?

description.zh: 学习按照英语通用规则排列句子中的形容词，常规排序逻辑为：观点→大小→年龄/新旧→形状→颜色→来源/产地→材质→用途，让描述读起来更自然通顺
description.en: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional English patterns (opinion-size-age-shape-colour-origin-material-purpose) to produce natural-sounding descriptions

evidence.zh: 能在名词前按基本顺序排列多个形容词，如课堂示例中能说“a small red bag”而非“a red small bag”。
evidence.en: Arrange multiple adjectives before a noun in conventional order, e.g. 'a lovely little old rectangular green French silver whittling knife' simplified to classroom examples like 'a small red bag' not 'a red small bag'

evidence.zh: 能识别形容词顺序不当的表达，并按英语习惯调整语序，如将“the wooden big table”改为“the big wooden table”。
evidence.en: Identify when adjective order sounds unnatural and rearrange to match English conventions, e.g. correct 'the wooden big table' to 'the big wooden table'

evidence.zh: 在描写性写作中，能按“大小—颜色—材料”的顺序排列形容词，如“一座高大的灰色石堡”，而非“一座石质灰色高大的城堡”。
evidence.en: Apply the size-before-colour-before-material pattern in descriptive writing, e.g. 'a tall grey stone castle' rather than 'a stone grey tall castle'

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}把几个描述词连用时——比如“一个又小又旧的木盒子”——这个顺序听起来自然吗，还是会把形容词顺序弄混，听起来别扭？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} uses several describing words together — like "a tiny old wooden box" — does the order sound natural, or do they mix up the adjectives so it sounds odd?

name.zh: 用于插入语的括号和破折号

description.zh: 学习使用括号、破折号和逗号标注插入语：插入语是加入句子中的补充信息，就算删掉这部分内容，也不会改变句子的核心含义
description.en: Use brackets, dashes, and commas to indicate parenthesis — additional information inserted into a sentence that could be removed without changing the sentence's core meaning

evidence.zh: 能使用成对括号插入补充说明，如“最古老的建筑（建于1642年）坐落在城镇广场上”。
evidence.en: Insert a parenthetical phrase using paired brackets, e.g. 'The oldest building (built in 1642) stands in the town square'

evidence.zh: 掌握破折号的用法：用双破折号在句中插入题外话或补充说明，如“My brother — who is older than me — lives in London”。
evidence.en: Use paired dashes to add an aside or extra detail within a sentence, e.g. 'My brother — who is older than me — lives in London'

evidence.zh: 能根据插入语强调程度的不同，在括号、破折号和逗号中作出选择，明确破折号强调意味最强，括号最弱。
evidence.en: Choose between brackets, dashes, and commas for parenthesis based on how much emphasis the aside should receive, recognising that dashes give most prominence and brackets give least

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}在句子中补充额外细节时——例如“那位老师，非常严格，给我们布置了作业”——他们能否正确使用括号、破折号或逗号来标示这部分补充内容？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} adds a little extra detail inside a sentence — like "The teacher, who is very strict, gave us homework" — do they correctly use brackets, dashes, or commas around that added bit?

evidence.zh: 能修改作文，在并列句的并列连词前补上遗漏的逗号。
evidence.en: Edit writing to insert missing commas before coordinating conjunctions in compound sentences

evidence.zh: 能借助逗号消除歧义，如区分“Let's eat, Grandma”和“Let's eat Grandma”，或理解“Most of the time, travellers worry about their bags”中逗号的作用。

evidence.zh: 能识别因缺少逗号而导致歧义的句子，并说明两种不同的句意理解。
evidence.en: Identify sentences where a missing comma changes the meaning and explain the two possible readings

evidence.zh: 在引导性成分（状语短语、从句）后使用逗号，以避免主句被误读。
evidence.en: Use commas after introductory elements (adverbial phrases, subordinate clauses) to prevent misreading of the main clause

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么“Let's eat, Grandma”和“Let's eat Grandma”意思截然不同——并能在自己的写作中运用这类逗号来避免歧义？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why "Let's eat, Grandma" and "Let's eat Grandma" mean very different things — and use that kind of comma in their own writing to avoid confusion?

description.zh: 学习构造并使用介词短语（即「介词+名词短语」结构），为句子补充时间、地点、方向类的细节，同时能够识别介词短语在句中是充当形容词性短语还是副词性短语
description.en: Form and use prepositional phrases (preposition + noun phrase) to add detail about time, location, or direction within sentences, recognising how they function as adjective or adverb phrases

description.zh: 学会识别并修改两类错误句子：一类是残缺句，也就是缺少主语或谓语的不完整句子；另一类是连写句，也就是没有使用正确标点或连词，就把两个及以上可以独立成句的分句拼接在一起的错误句子

description.zh: 你可以使用时间状语（比如稍后、与此同时、过了一会儿）、地点状语（比如在附近、在远处、墙的另一边）、列举类状语（比如第二、最后、除此之外）衔接不同段落的观点，引导读者顺畅读懂多段落文本。
description.en: Link ideas across paragraphs using adverbials of time (later, meanwhile, after a while), place (nearby, far away, beyond the wall), and number (secondly, finally, in addition) to guide the reader through a multi-paragraph text

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}在写多段故事或报告时，是否会使用过渡短语——例如“与此同时，在远方……”或“到了第二天早上……”——来引导读者顺畅地从一段过渡到下一段？

description.zh: 掌握动词进行时态的构成与用法，包含过去进行时（例：was walking 当时正在走路）、现在进行时（例：am walking 正在走路）、将来进行时（例：will be walking 届时正在走路），能够用这三类时态表述不同时间节点上正在持续进行的动作。

description.en: Read common high-frequency and exception words automatically by sight, including words with irregular spelling patterns

evidence.zh: 能直接识别常见例外词，无需拼读（如“the”“said”“was”“you”）。
evidence.en: Read common exception words instantly without sounding out (e.g. 'the', 'said', 'was', 'you')

evidence.zh: 能识别例外单词中拼写与读音的不规则对应。
evidence.en: Note unusual correspondences between spelling and sound in exception words

evidence.zh: 在连贯文本中认读至少20-30个高频词
evidence.en: Recognise at least 20-30 high-frequency words in connected text

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否不假思索地认读“said”、“was”、“they”、“come”、“because”等常见词，而无需每次都进行拼读？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} instantly recognise everyday words like 'said', 'was', 'they', 'come', and 'because' without needing to sound them out every time?

name.zh: 带屈折词尾的单词认读

description.zh: 认读符合已学字素音素对应规则、带有常见屈折词尾（-s、-es、-ing、-ed、-er、-est）以及带前缀un-的单词，同时能认读符合已学拼读规律的多音节单词
description.en: Read words containing taught GPCs with common inflectional endings (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) and the prefix un-; read multi-syllable words with taught patterns

evidence.zh: 能流利朗读带后缀的单词（如“jumping”“wanted”“faster”）。
evidence.en: Read suffixed words fluently (e.g. 'jumping', 'wanted', 'faster')

evidence.zh: 能识别添加后缀后的词根。
evidence.en: Identify the root word when a suffix is added

evidence.zh: 能认读含前缀 un- 的单词（如 unhappy、undo）。
evidence.en: Read words with prefix un- (e.g. 'unhappy', 'undo')

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}看到带有不同词尾的熟悉单词时——比如“jumped”“running”“biggest”或“unhappy”——他/她能识别出词根并正确读出整个单词吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} sees familiar words with different endings — like 'jumped', 'running', 'biggest', or 'unhappy' — can they spot the root word and read the whole thing correctly?

description.zh: 认读并拼写包含拆分元音组合（a-e、e-e、i-e、o-e、u-e）的单词，这类单词末尾的「e」不发音，会让它前面的元音发长音。
description.en: Read and spell words containing split digraphs (a-e, e-e, i-e, o-e, u-e) where a final 'e' makes the preceding vowel long

evidence.zh: 能拼读含有分离二合字母的单词（如cake、bike、home、cube）。
evidence.en: Read words with split digraphs (e.g. 'cake', 'bike', 'home', 'cube')

evidence.zh: 能通过最小对立词对（如cap与cape）对比并拆分字母组合的发音。
evidence.en: Compare minimal pairs showing the effect of the split digraph (e.g. 'cap' vs 'cape')

evidence.zh: 正确拼写含有分离二合字母的单词
evidence.en: Spell words with split digraphs correctly

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否知道，像“cake”、“bike”或“home”这类词末尾的“e”会改变中间元音的音——让它发字母本身的音，而不是短元音？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know that the 'e' at the end of words like 'cake', 'bike', or 'home' changes the vowel sound in the middle — making it say its name instead of its short sound?

description.zh: 能够提炼故事、寓言或民间故事的核心主旨、道理与寓意，说出故事带给读者的启示，并结合文本中的关键细节支撑自己的理解。
description.en: Determine the central message, lesson, or moral of a story, fable, or folktale, explaining what the story teaches the reader and supporting the interpretation with key details from the text

evidence.zh: 能一句话概括寓言的寓意或道理（如《龟兔赛跑》告诉我们：稳扎稳打，终能取胜）。
evidence.en: State the lesson or moral of a fable in one sentence (e.g. 'The Tortoise and the Hare teaches that slow and steady wins the race')

evidence.zh: 能结合文中至少两处细节，概括故事的中心思想。
evidence.en: Explain what a story's central message is using at least two details from the text as support

evidence.zh: 区分主题与情节概要——阐释故事的深层含义，而非仅复述事件。
evidence.en: Distinguish the central message from a summary of events — explain what the story means, not just what happens

assessmentPrompt.zh: 读完《龟兔赛跑》这类寓言后，{{name}}能否说出这个故事所讲的道理，并指出故事中体现这个道理的一个情节？
assessmentPrompt.en: After reading a fable like "The Tortoise and the Hare", can {{name}} tell you the lesson the story is teaching — and point to a moment in the story that shows that lesson?

description.zh: 能够识别语言选择、文本结构以及各类呈现特征（插图、示意图、粗体字、排版布局）对文本整体含义和表达效果的作用
description.en: Identify how language choices, text structure and presentational features (illustrations, diagrams, bold print, layout) contribute to the overall meaning and effect of a text

evidence.zh: 解释作者选词如何营造特定效果（如：“作者用‘蹑手蹑脚’而非‘走’，营造出鬼祟紧张的氛围”）。
evidence.en: Explain how an author's word choices create a particular effect (e.g., 'The author uses "crept" instead of "walked" to make it feel sneaky and tense')

evidence.zh: 能指出文本结构对读者的作用（如“标题有助于快速查找信息”“故事在结尾前制造悬念”）。
evidence.en: Identify how a text's structure helps the reader (e.g., 'The headings help you find information quickly', 'The story builds suspense before the ending')

evidence.zh: 解释文本特征如何促进内容理解（如“加粗词为关键词”“该图展示了水循环过程”）。

assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} reads a page with headings, diagrams, or bold words, can they explain how those features help — like "the diagram shows the water cycle because the words alone are hard to picture"?

description.zh: 结合文本依据分析故事人物的特点、行为动机和情绪感受，学会区分自身观点与叙述者或故事人物的观点
description.en: Analyse character traits, motivations, and feelings using text evidence, and distinguish one's own point of view from that of the narrator or characters

evidence.zh: 能识别故事中两个人物的性格特征，并引用体现各自特征的具体行为或对话。
evidence.en: Identify two character traits from a story and cite the specific actions or dialogue that reveal each trait

evidence.zh: 能结合文本中的事件，联系人物动机，解释人物做出某一决定的原因。
evidence.en: Explain why a character made a particular decision by linking their motivation to events in the text

evidence.zh: 能指出自己对某个人物的看法与叙述者刻画的不同之处，并说明理由。
evidence.en: Describe where one's own opinion about a character differs from the narrator's portrayal and explain why

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}阅读一个故事时，他们能否描述某个角色为什么做出某个特定选择——解释其动机——并说明他们个人是否认同该角色的行为？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} reads a story, can they describe why a character made a particular choice — explaining their motivations — and also say whether they personally agree with what the character did?

name.zh: 梳理文本内容间的关联

description.zh: 能够运用表时间、先后顺序、因果、比较的表达，描述信息类文本中事件、观点或概念之间的关联，识别句子与段落之间的逻辑联系
description.en: Describe connections between events, ideas, or concepts in informational text using time, sequence, cause-and-effect, and comparison language, and identify logical connections between sentences and paragraphs

evidence.zh: 阅读科学文本，借助“因为”“因此”等信号词，识别出三组因果关系。
evidence.en: Read a science text and identify three cause-and-effect relationships using signal words like 'because', 'as a result'

evidence.zh: 能运用“首先”“接着”“最后”等表示时间先后的词语，说清楚技术流程的步骤顺序。
evidence.en: Explain the sequence of steps in a technical procedure using time-order language ('first', 'next', 'finally')

evidence.zh: 描述文中两个段落之间的关系（如比较、因果或顺序）。
evidence.en: Describe how two paragraphs in a text are connected (e.g. comparison, cause/effect, or sequence)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 读完一篇非虚构类文章后——比如关于气候或历史的文章——{{name}}能否解释某件事的起因、结果，以及作者是如何将这些观点联系在一起的？
assessmentPrompt.en: After reading a non-fiction passage — like one about climate or history — can {{name}} explain what caused something to happen, what the effect was, and how the author linked those ideas together?

name.zh: 寓言、民间故事与神话中的寓意
name.en: Morals in Fables, Folktales and Myths

description.zh: 能够说明寓言、民间故事、神话等不同类型故事中的核心主旨、经验教训或寓意是如何通过关键细节传递出来的
description.en: Explain how the central message, lesson, or moral of a story is conveyed through key details across diverse text types including fables, folktales, and myths

evidence.zh: 能复述寓言故事并概括寓意，能列举三个体现寓意的关键细节。
evidence.en: Retell a fable and identify the moral, citing three key details that convey it

evidence.zh: 比较不同文化中的两则神话如何通过不同事件传达相似的中心思想
evidence.en: Compare how two myths from different cultures convey a similar central message through different events

evidence.zh: 阐明故事主题与中心思想的区别
evidence.en: Explain the difference between the topic of a story and its central message or lesson

assessmentPrompt.zh: 阅读完来自另一种文化的神话或民间故事后，{{name}}能否解释它传递了什么道理或价值观——并说出故事中哪些细节体现了这一点？
assessmentPrompt.en: After reading a myth or folktale from another culture, can {{name}} explain what lesson or value it was teaching — and say which details in the story showed that?

description.zh: 运用结构术语（章节、戏剧场景、诗节）指代文学文本的各个组成部分，能够说明每一个后续部分是如何在前文内容的基础上逐步展开的
description.en: Use structural terminology (chapter, scene, stanza) to refer to parts of literary texts and describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections

evidence.zh: 能识别段落、场景或诗节，并正确使用相关术语。
evidence.en: Identify chapters, scenes, or stanzas in a given text and use the correct term for each

evidence.zh: 阐释诗歌第二节如何在第一节点明的情感基调上进一步发展。
evidence.en: Explain how the second stanza of a poem builds on the mood established in the first

evidence.zh: 能结合前几章的事件，说明某一章如何推动情节发展。
evidence.en: Describe how a specific chapter advances the plot by referring to events in earlier chapters

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}谈论自己正在读的书时，能否正确使用“章节”“诗节”或“场景”等词，并解释后面的章节如何在前文基础上展开？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} talks about a book they're reading, do they use words like "chapter", "stanza", or "scene" correctly — and can they explain how a later chapter builds on what happened earlier?

name.zh: 作者为什么写这篇文章

description.zh: 能够区分个人观点与信息类文本作者的观点，判断作者的写作目的
description.en: Distinguish one's own point of view from that of the author of an informational text and identify the author's purpose

evidence.zh: 阅读观点性文章，能概括作者观点，表达个人观点，并阐释二者异同。
evidence.en: Read an opinion article and state the author's point of view, then state one's own and explain how they differ

evidence.zh: 能判断作者的意图是告知、说服还是娱乐，并能从文中找出依据。
evidence.en: Identify whether an author's purpose is to inform, persuade, or entertain, citing evidence from the text

evidence.zh: 解释说明性文本中的措辞如何体现作者对主题的态度
evidence.en: Explain how word choices in an informational text reveal the author's attitude toward the topic

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}阅读一本知识类书籍或一篇文章时，能否说出作者的写作目的是什么——比如是为了告知、说服还是娱乐——以及他们是否同意作者的观点？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} reads a fact book or an article, can they tell you what the author's purpose was — like whether they were trying to inform, persuade, or entertain — and whether they agree with the author's viewpoint?

description.zh: 整合两篇同主题文本的信息，结合、比对两篇材料各自提供的内容要点，从而能够有理有据、内容充实地围绕该主题进行写作或口头表达
description.en: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably, combining and comparing what each source contributes

evidence.zh: 阅读同一主题的两篇信息类文本，能提取两篇文本的共同信息、各自独有信息及相互矛盾之处。
evidence.en: Read two informational texts on the same topic and identify information that appears in both, information unique to each, and any contradictions between them

evidence.zh: 整合两篇文本的关键细节，写出一篇连贯的摘要或简短报告。
evidence.en: Combine key details from two sources into a coherent summary or short report that draws on both texts

evidence.zh: 阐释阅读同一主题的第二篇文本如何补充、印证或挑战从第一篇文本中获得的理解
evidence.en: Explain how reading a second text on the same topic added to, confirmed, or challenged understanding gained from the first text

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}正在通过两本不同的书或文章研究同一主题，他们能否整合从两个来源中获取的信息，从而比仅依据其中任一来源更全面地讨论或撰写该主题？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} is researching a topic using two different books or articles, can they combine the information they've gathered from both to talk or write about the subject more fully than either source alone?

description.zh:
认识信息类文本的四类常见整体结构：时间顺序、比较对照、因果关系、问题解决，能够解释作者选用的结构对传递信息与观点的作用。具体掌握要求：
1. 能判断信息类文本使用的组织结构类型，并举出文中提示该结构的文本特征；
2. 能理解各类标志词对文本结构的提示作用：时间顺序的标志词有first（首先）、then（接着）、finally（最后）；比较对照的标志词有however（然而）、similarly（同样）；因果关系的标志词有because（因为）、as a result（因此）；问题解决的标志词有the solution was（解决方法是）；
3. 能对比同主题、使用不同结构的两篇信息类文本，解释不同结构对信息呈现方式的影响。
description.en: Describe the overall structure of an informational text (chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) and explain how the author's chosen structure helps convey information and ideas

evidence.zh: 能识别信息类文本的结构组织方式（时间顺序、比较与对比、因果、问题与解决），并能引用体现该结构的文本特征。
evidence.en: Identify which organisational structure an informational text uses (chronological order, compare/contrast, cause/effect, or problem/solution) and cite textual features that signal it

evidence.zh: 解释信号词（如时间顺序的first、then、finally；比较的however、similarly；因果的because、as a result；问题解决的the solution was）如何揭示文本结构
evidence.en: Explain how signal words (first, then, finally for chronology; however, similarly for comparison; because, as a result for cause/effect; the solution was for problem/solution) reveal text structure

evidence.zh: 比较同一主题下不同结构的两篇信息类文本，并解释各自的结构如何影响信息的呈现方式。
evidence.en: Compare two informational texts on the same topic that use different structures and explain how each structure affects the way information is presented to the reader

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}阅读非虚构文本时，他们能否识别文本的组织结构——例如，“这篇采用的是问题与解决方案结构”或“这篇按时间顺序叙述事件”——并解释为什么这种结构有效？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} reads a non-fiction text, can they identify how it's organised — for example, "this one is structured as a problem and solution" or "this one goes through events in time order" — and explain why that structure works?

description.zh: 即兴创作、排练并表演戏剧剧本与诗歌，学会运用角色塑造、语调、语气、音量、情绪、静默、静态姿态与肢体动作，丰富语言表达、探究内容含义、提升表演感染力

evidence.zh: 运用即兴表演，探索角色在新情境中可能作出的反应。

evidence.zh: 朗诵并表演一首诗，通过节奏和重音传达诗意。
evidence.en: Rehearse and perform a poem aloud, using pace and emphasis to bring out the meaning

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}参与戏剧表演或朗读剧本时，他们是否能运用声音——音量、节奏和表达——让角色或诗歌栩栩如生？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} performs in a play or reads aloud from a script, do they use their voice — volume, pace, and expression — to bring the character or poem to life?

description.zh: 能够在正式与非正式口语场景中自信使用标准英语，完成简短发言与演讲展示，清晰表达个人观点、紧扣主题，并根据听众调整语域与用词。
description.en: Use Standard English confidently in formal and informal spoken contexts — give short speeches and presentations expressing own ideas clearly, keeping to the point, and adapting register and vocabulary to the audience

evidence.zh: 能围绕一个主题进行2-3分钟的口头表达，做到开篇点题、条理清晰、结尾总结到位。
evidence.en: Deliver a 2-3 minute presentation on a topic with a clear opening, organised points, and a conclusion

evidence.zh: 能在正式与非正式语言之间根据语境和对象灵活切换。
evidence.en: Adapt language between formal and informal registers depending on the context and audience

evidence.zh: 面向群体发言时，能保持眼神交流，语速适中，吐字清晰。
evidence.en: Maintain eye contact, appropriate pace, and clear articulation when speaking to a group

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否用标准英语进行简短的备稿演讲或展示——紧扣主题并根据听众调整用词？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} give a short prepared speech or presentation in Standard English — staying on point and adjusting their vocabulary to suit the audience?

description.zh: 参与正式辩论和结构化讨论：提出有论据支撑的个人立场，回应他人观点，总结已有发言并在此基础上进行拓展，同时遵守讨论规则
description.en: Participate in formal debates and structured discussions — presenting a position with supporting evidence, responding to others’ points, summarising and building on what has been said, and following rules of discussion

evidence.zh: 在辩论中提出明确论点，并用证据加以支持。
evidence.en: Present an argument in a debate with a clear claim supported by evidence

evidence.zh: 在反驳之前，先准确复述对方观点，再进行回应。
evidence.en: Respond to an opposing point by summarising it fairly before offering a counterargument

evidence.zh: 能对他人的观点进行建设性补充、质疑或反驳。
evidence.en: Build on a previous speaker’s idea by extending, questioning, or challenging it constructively

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否参加过学校辩论，在辩论中需要用证据支持自己的立场、回应对方的观点，并遵守正式讨论的规则？
assessmentPrompt.en: Has {{name}} taken part in a school debate where they had to argue a position with evidence, respond to the other side's points, and keep to the rules of formal discussion?

description.zh: 认识并会使用自然拼读与字词结构相关的词汇，具体包括音素、字素、字素-音素对应规则（简称GPC，即字素与音素的对应关系）、拼合、拆分、二合字母、辅元辅结构（简称CVC）、元音、辅音、音节、词根、后缀、前缀、同音异形词；明白这些词汇所指代的概念是自然拼读学习的基础构成模块。
description.en: Know and use the vocabulary of phonics and word structure — phoneme, grapheme, GPC (grapheme-phoneme correspondence), blend, segment, digraph, CVC, vowel, consonant, syllable, root word, suffix, prefix, and homophone — and understand that these words describe the building blocks that phonics instruction is built on

evidence.zh: 能正确发音常见字素（如sh、ch、th、ee、igh），并在教学中正确使用“音素”和“字素”两个术语。
evidence.en: Say the sounds for common graphemes (e.g. 'sh', 'ch', 'th', 'ee', 'igh') and use 'phoneme' and 'grapheme' correctly when explaining

evidence.zh: 能拼读生词，并能用“拼读”一词说明拼读过程。
evidence.en: Blend sounds together to read an unfamiliar word and explain what they are doing using the word 'blend'

evidence.zh: 能通过切分单词中的单个音素进行拼写，并能用“切分”这一术语描述该过程。
evidence.en: Segment a word into its individual sounds for spelling and use the term 'segment' to describe the process

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}的老师让他们“把一个词切分成音素”或找出“二合字母”时，他们明白这些词的意思吗？能顺利完成而不显得困惑吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}}'s teacher asks them to 'segment a word into phonemes' or spot a 'digraph', do they understand what those words mean and can they do the task without looking confused?

name.zh: 将单词拆分为单个发音

description.zh: 将听到的口语单词拆分为单个音素，为每个发音匹配对应的一个或多个字母，以此拼写CVC（辅音-元音-辅音结构）单词和简单的规则发音单词

evidence.zh: 能根据听写拼写CVC单词（如“cat”“bed”“hot”）
evidence.en: Write CVC words from dictation (e.g. 'cat', 'bed', 'hot')

evidence.zh: 在书写字母之前，先将单词拆分为单个音素。
evidence.en: Segment words into individual sounds before choosing letters to write

evidence.zh: 能根据读音规则拼写简单单词。
evidence.en: Spell simple words phonetically drawing on sound-letter knowledge

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否听辨“cat”或“ship”这类简单单词，并写出所听到的每个音对应的字母？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} listen to a simple word like "cat" or "ship" and write down the letters for each sound they hear?

description.zh: 运用已学音素对应的不同字素拼写单词，学习已接触过的发音的其他拼写规则，例如/ɔ:/音在ll前由字母a发出、/ʌ/音可由字母o发出、-tion结尾的单词拼写规律，同时掌握常见同音词的区分方法。

evidence.zh: 能拼写含替代音/ɔː/（在ll前发/a/）的单词ball、call、walk。

evidence.zh: 在写作中能正确区分同音词：there/their/they’re、here/hear、quite/quiet。
evidence.en: Distinguish homophones in writing: 'there/their/they’re', 'here/hear', 'quite/quiet'

evidence.zh: 正确拼写以-tion结尾的单词：station、fiction、motion
evidence.en: Spell words ending in -tion correctly: 'station', 'fiction', 'motion'

description.zh: 学会在单数名词后使用所有格撇号来表示所属关系，例如：the girl's book（女孩的书）、the dog's bone（小狗的骨头）
description.en: Use the possessive apostrophe with singular nouns to show ownership (e.g., the girl's book, the dog's bone)

evidence.zh: 能写出“the cat's tail”，表明尾巴属于猫。
evidence.en: Write 'the cat's tail' to show the tail belongs to the cat

evidence.zh: 在书写中区分复数-s（如“the cats ran”）与所有格's（如“the cat's bed”）。
evidence.en: Distinguish plural -s ('the cats ran') from possessive 's ('the cat's bed') in writing

evidence.zh: 在听写句子中为单数名词添加所有格撇号
evidence.en: Add a possessive apostrophe to a singular noun in a dictated sentence

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}书写表示单个人或事物的所属关系时——比如“the dog's lead”或“the girl's bag”——他们能否把撇号放在正确的位置？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} writes something belonging to one person or thing — like "the dog's lead" or "the girl's bag" — do they put the apostrophe in the right place?

description.zh: 正确拼写单词的缩写形式，将撇号写在省略字母的位置（例如can't、didn't、I'll、it's等）
description.en: Spell contracted forms correctly by placing the apostrophe where letters are omitted (can't, didn't, I'll, it's, etc.)

evidence.zh: 能正确使用撇号，将cannot缩写为can't，将did not缩写为didn't。
evidence.en: Write 'can't' for 'cannot', 'didn't' for 'did not' with apostrophe correctly placed

evidence.zh: 能在句子中区分“it's”（it is）与“its”（所有格）。
evidence.en: Distinguish 'it's' (it is) from 'its' (possessive) in a sentence

evidence.zh: 能还原缩写为完整形式，并指出省略的字母。
evidence.en: Expand a contraction back to its full form and explain which letters are missing

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}书写“can't”或“didn't”这类缩写形式时，他们能否在正确位置加上撇号，以表示省略了哪些字母？

description.zh: 能够区分并正确拼写小学三至四年级常见的同音异形词和近音词（例如accept/except、affect/effect、brake/break、grate/great），掌握发/eɪ/音、拼作ei、eigh或ey的单词拼写规则
description.en: Distinguish and correctly spell common homophones and near-homophones encountered at Y3-4 level (e.g., accept/except, affect/effect, brake/break, grate/great), including using the /eɪ/ sound spelt ei, eigh, or ey

evidence.zh: 能在语境中正确拼写同音异形词（如“there/their/they're”“brake/break”“grate/great”）。
evidence.en: Spell pairs of homophones correctly in context (e.g., 'there/their/they're', 'brake/break', 'grate/great')

evidence.zh: 能根据句意选择正确的同音词填空（如“The dog wagged its/it's tail”）。
evidence.en: Choose the correct homophone to complete a sentence (e.g., 'The dog wagged its/it's tail')

evidence.zh: 能拼写发/eɪ/音、以ei、eigh或ey拼写的单词（如vein、eight、they、neighbour）。
evidence.en: Spell words with the /eɪ/ sound as ei, eigh, or ey (e.g., vein, eight, they, neighbour)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}写作时，他们能否正确拼写同音异义词——比如“brake”（自行车上的刹车）和“break”（折断某物）？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} writes, do they use the right spelling for words that sound the same but mean different things — like "brake" (on a bike) and "break" (snap something)?

description.zh: 能拼写带有dis-、mis-、un-、re-、pre-、anti-、auto-、super-等多种前缀的单词，理解每个前缀会改变词根的含义，但不会改变词根本身的拼写
description.en: Spell words with a range of prefixes (dis-, mis-, un-, re-, pre-, anti-, auto-, super-) understanding how each prefix modifies the root word's meaning without changing its spelling

evidence.zh: 能正确拼写加前缀dis-、mis-、re-且词根不变的单词（如disappoint、misspell、return）。
evidence.en: Spell words with prefixes dis-, mis-, re- correctly without altering the root (e.g., disappoint, misspell, return)

evidence.zh: 能通过给词根加前缀 un-、pre-、anti-、auto-、super- 构成新词，并会用新词造句（如 unhappy、preview、autograph）。
evidence.en: Add prefixes un-, pre-, anti-, auto-, super- to root words and use the new word in a sentence (e.g., unhappy, preview, autograph)

evidence.zh: 解释前缀如何改变词根含义（如“dis-”表示“不”或“相反”）。
evidence.en: Explain how a prefix changes the meaning of a root word (e.g., 'dis-' means 'not' or 'opposite of')

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到一个以“dis-”、“mis-”或“pre-”开头的单词，他们能否通过思考前缀来推断出这个词的意思并正确拼写？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a word starting with "dis-," "mis-," or "pre-," can they work out what the word means and spell it correctly by thinking about the prefix?

name.zh: 拼写单词表（7岁及以上适用）

description.zh: 需掌握三、四年级课标规定必修单词表中的单词拼写，涵盖不符合常规拼写规律的高频易拼错单词。
description.en: Spell words from the statutory word list for Years 3 and 4, including commonly misspelt words that do not follow regular patterns

evidence.zh: 准确拼写Y3-4法定词表中的至少20个单词（如accident、believe、different、favourite、imagine）。

evidence.zh: 在各学科写作中准确运用法定词汇表词汇
evidence.en: Use statutory list words accurately in own writing across subjects

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}在写作时能否凭记忆正确拼写出小学三、四年级单词表中的易错词——例如“enough”“believe”或“separate”？

description.zh: 运用小学三至四年级课程中引入的常用后缀（-ation、-ly、-ous）及次常见音形对应规则拼写单词，涉及的音形对应规则包括：元音/ɪ/对应字母y、元音/ʌ/对应字母组合ou，以及发音为/ʒə/、/tʃə/、/ʒən/、/ʃən/的词尾拼写规则。
description.en: Spell words using productive suffixes (-ation, -ly, -ous) and less common sound-spelling correspondences (/ɪ/ as y, /ʌ/ as ou, endings sounding like /ʒə/, /tʃə/, /ʒən/, /ʃən/) introduced in the Year 3-4 programme

evidence.zh: 掌握 -ation（如 information、sensation）、-ly（如 sadly、gently、happily）和 -ous（如 famous、enormous、various）后缀单词的拼写。
evidence.en: Spell words with suffixes -ation (e.g., information, sensation), -ly (e.g., sadly, gently, happily), and -ous (e.g., famous, enormous, various)

evidence.zh: 掌握不常见元音字母组合的拼写规则：/ɪ/ 拼作 y（如 myth、gym），/ʌ/ 拼作 ou（如 young、touch、double）
evidence.en: Spell words with less common vowel patterns: /ɪ/ as y (e.g., myth, gym), /ʌ/ as ou (e.g., young, touch, double)

evidence.zh: 能根据词尾发音拼写单词：以 /ʒə/ 结尾的拼作 -sure（如 measure、treasure），以 /tʃə/ 结尾的拼作 -ture（如 creature、furniture），以 /ʒən/ 结尾的拼作 -sion（如 division、television）。
evidence.en: Spell words with endings /ʒə/ as -sure (e.g., measure, treasure), /tʃə/ as -ture (e.g., creature, furniture), /ʒən/ as -sion (e.g., division, television)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否在不查词典的情况下，正确拼写以“-tion”“-ous”或“-ly”结尾的单词——例如“nation”“famous”或“quietly”？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} spell words with endings like "-tion," "-ous," or "-ly" correctly — for example, "nation," "famous," or "quietly" — without needing to look them up?

name.en: Using a Dictionary to Check Spellings

description.zh: 利用单词的前两到三个字母在词典中核对拼写；查阅包括入门词典在内的参考资料，确认并改正拼写错误

evidence.zh: 能借助词汇表或初级词典检查并确认自己作文中单词的拼写。

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}不确定某个单词的拼写，他们能否利用该词的前两三个字母在字典中快速查找？

name.en: Spellings from Greek, French and Latin

description.zh: 学习源自希腊语、法语、拉丁语的英语单词拼写，掌握不同语言来源对应的特殊字母组合规律：希腊语来源的单词中ch发/k/音；法语来源的单词中ch发/ʃ/音，常见词尾为-gue、-que；拉丁语来源的单词中sc发/s/音。
description.en: Spell words with etymological letter patterns from Greek (ch = /k/), French (ch = /ʃ/, -gue, -que), and Latin (sc = /s/) origins

evidence.zh: 能拼写含希腊词根ch的单词（如scheme、chorus、chemist、echo），并解释ch发/k/音的规律。
evidence.en: Spell words with Greek ch such as 'scheme', 'chorus', 'chemist', 'echo' and explain the /k/ sound pattern

evidence.zh: 正确拼写含法语ch的单词（如chef、chalet、machine）及以-gue/-que结尾的单词（如league、unique）。
evidence.en: Spell words with French ch such as 'chef', 'chalet', 'machine' and -gue/-que endings like 'league', 'unique'

evidence.zh: 准确拼写含拉丁词根sc的单词（如science、scene、discipline），并识别其中不发音字母的规律。
evidence.en: Spell words with Latin sc such as 'science', 'scene', 'discipline' and identify the silent letter pattern

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否知道有些单词包含源自其他语言的字母组合模式——比如“ch”在“school”或“chorus”中发“k”音——并且能否正确拼写这些单词？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know that some words have letter patterns from other languages — like "ch" making a "k" sound in "school" or "chorus" — and can they spell those words correctly?

description.zh: 运用5-6年级要求掌握的各类拼写规则拼写单词，具体规则包括：重音保持不变时，-fer结尾的单词变形需双写字母r（如referring需双写，reference无需双写）；使用连字符连接前缀与词根（例词：co-ordinate、re-enter）；字母c后发/iː/音时拼写为ei（例词：receive、ceiling）；字母组合ough可对应多种不同发音（例词：though、through、thought、thorough、plough）
description.en: Spell words using assorted Y5-6 conventions: doubling after -fer when the stress remains (referring but reference), using hyphens to join prefixes to root words (co-ordinate, re-enter), the /iː/ sound spelt ei after c (receive, ceiling), and the letter string ough representing different sounds (though, through, thought, thorough, plough)

evidence.zh: 掌握-fer双写规则：重读闭音节双写r（referring、preferred、transferred），重音转移不双写（reference、preference）。
evidence.en: Apply the -fer doubling rule: double the r when the syllable is stressed (referring, preferred, transferred) but not when stress shifts (reference, preference)

evidence.zh: 能在前缀与词根首尾字母相同（如 re-enter、co-own）或为避免歧义（如 re-cover 与 recover）时正确使用连字符。
evidence.en: Use hyphens correctly when a prefix ends with the same letter the root begins with (re-enter, co-own) or to avoid ambiguity (re-cover vs recover)

evidence.zh: 能认读并拼写含ough的单词，识别其多种发音：/oʊ/（though）、/uː/（through）、/ɔː/（thought）、/ʌf/（rough）、/aʊ/（plough）。
evidence.en: Read and spell words containing ough by recognising its multiple pronunciations: /oʊ/ (though), /uː/ (through), /ɔː/ (thought), /ʌf/ (rough), /aʊ/ (plough)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否正确拼写像“receive”“though”或“co-ordinate”这样的易错词，包括知道何时使用连字符，以及“c”后面何时使用“-ei”拼写模式？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} correctly spell tricky words like "receive," "though," or "co-ordinate," including knowing when to use a hyphen or the "-ei" pattern after "c"?

name.zh: 同音异形词（9岁及以上适用）

description.zh: 区分并正确拼写小学五至六年级（9-10岁）水平的同音异形词与常见易混词，典型词例包括affect/effect、practice/practise、advice/advise、complement/compliment、aisle/isle、led/lead，还涵盖to/too/two、there/their/they're等高频易错词组。
description.en: Distinguish and correctly spell homophones and commonly confused words at Y5-6 level (e.g., affect/effect, practice/practise, advice/advise, complement/compliment, aisle/isle, led/lead), including confused words such as to/too/two and there/their/they're

evidence.zh: 能在语境中辨析词义，从同音词中选出正确拼写，如“医生的建议（名词）是每天练习（动词）”。
evidence.en: Select the correct spelling from a pair of homophones by analysing meaning in context, e.g. 'The doctor's advice (noun) was to practise (verb) daily'

evidence.zh: 能借助词性线索正确拼写常见易混词：advise/advice、practise/practice、licence/license（动词以-ise结尾，名词以-ice结尾）。
evidence.en: Spell commonly confused words accurately by applying word-class clues: advise/advice, practise/practice, licence/license (verb ends in -ise, noun ends in -ice)

evidence.zh: 在较长篇幅写作中识别并纠正同音词错误，包括to/too/two、there/their/they're、whose/who's和its/it's。
evidence.en: Identify and correct homophone errors in extended writing, including to/too/two, there/their/they're, whose/who's, and its/it's

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}写作时，他们能否正确拼写容易混淆的常见单词——比如“affect”和“effect”、“practice”和“practise”，或者“there”、“their”和“they're”？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} writes, do they use the right spelling for commonly mixed-up words — like "affect" vs "effect," "practice" vs "practise," or "there," "their," and "they're"?

description.zh: 能够拼写含有不发音字母的单词——这类字母是单词早期发音或词源演变的遗留痕迹；认识常见的不发音字母规律，能结合单词起源记忆这类单词的拼写。
description.en: Spell words containing silent letters that are remnants of earlier pronunciation or etymology, recognising common silent-letter patterns and using word origins to remember them

evidence.zh: 能识别并拼写含不发音首辅音的单词：knight、know、write、wrap、gnaw、psalm，并能运用这些字母过去曾发音的知识。

evidence.zh: 掌握不发音字母单词的拼写：doubt（b不发音）、island（s不发音）、muscle（c不发音）、solemn（n不发音），并能借助词源关联辅助记忆（如 doubt 源自拉丁语 dubitare）。
evidence.en: Spell words with silent internal letters: doubt (b), island (s), muscle (c), solemn (n), using etymological connections to aid memory (e.g. doubt from Latin dubitare)

evidence.zh: 运用词族和词源知识辅助记忆不发音字母，如sign与signal同族，signal中g发音。
evidence.en: Use word families and etymology to remember silent letters, e.g. sign is related to signal where the g is pronounced

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}书写含有不发音字母的单词时——例如“knight”、“wrap”或“lamb”——他们是否能记得写上那个听不见的不发音字母？

description.zh: 学会拼写以-able、-ible结尾的单词，以及它们对应的以-ably、-ibly结尾的副词形式，能够根据词根运用相关规律判断具体使用哪一种后缀。
description.en: Spell words ending in -able/-ible and the corresponding adverb forms -ably/-ibly, applying patterns to determine which suffix to use based on the root word

evidence.zh: 运用规则：-able通常加在完整词根后（如enjoyable、comfortable），-ible加在不完整词根后（如visible、possible），并注意常见例外。
evidence.en: Apply the guideline that -able is typically used with complete root words (enjoyable, comfortable) while -ible is used with incomplete roots (visible, possible), noting key exceptions

evidence.zh: 掌握：将-able/-ible结尾的形容词变为副词，即把词尾改为-ably/-ibly，如comfortable → comfortably，possible → possibly，terrible → terribly。

evidence.zh: 掌握词根加-able时是否去e的规则，如adorable（去e）与changeable（软g前保留e）。
evidence.en: Determine whether to drop or retain the final -e of the root when adding -able, e.g. adorable (drop e) vs changeable (keep e before soft g)

name.zh: 英语单词后缀（9岁及以上适用）

description.zh: 学习源自拉丁语、法语的英语后缀拼写规律，具体包含三类内容：1. 发音为/ʃəs/的词尾有两种拼写形式：-cious和-tious，例词：precious（珍贵的）、cautious（谨慎的）；2. 发音为/ʃəl/的词尾有两种拼写形式：-cial和-tial，例词：official（官方的）、essential（必要的）；3. 区分-ant/-ance/-ancy与-ent/-ence/-ency这两类不同结尾的单词，例词：observant（观察力敏锐的）/observance（遵守）、confident（自信的）/confidence（信心）
description.en: Spell words with Latin and French suffix patterns: endings sounding like /ʃəs/ spelt -cious or -tious (e.g., precious, cautious), /ʃəl/ spelt -cial or -tial (e.g., official, essential), and words ending in -ant/-ance/-ancy vs -ent/-ence/-ency (e.g., observant/observance, confident/confidence)

evidence.zh: 掌握规律：-cious 前常接元音（如 spacious、gracious），-tious 前常接辅音（如 cautious、ambitious），并注意 anxious 等常见例外。
evidence.en: Apply the pattern that -cious follows a vowel (spacious, gracious) while -tious follows a consonant (cautious, ambitious), noting common exceptions like anxious

evidence.zh: 能根据词尾/ʃəl/前是元音还是辅音，正确拼写-cial（多用于元音后：special, official）或-tial（多用于辅音后：essential, partial）。
evidence.en: Choose between -cial (usually after a vowel: special, official) and -tial (usually after a consonant: essential, partial) when spelling words with the /ʃəl/ ending

evidence.zh: 根据词根末尾是硬音c或g（-ant：significant）还是软音c或g（-ent：innocent），并运用词族策略，选择-ant/-ance或-ent/-ence。
evidence.en: Select -ant/-ance or -ent/-ence by checking whether the root ends in a hard c or g sound (-ant: significant) or a soft c or g sound (-ent: innocent), and by applying word-family strategies

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否正确拼写以“-cious”“-tious”或“-cial”等难拼后缀结尾的单词——例如“precious”“cautious”或“official”——而不出错？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} spell words with tricky endings like "-cious," "-tious," or "-cial" — for example, "precious," "cautious," or "official" — without making mistakes?

name.zh: 复杂单词拼写规则运用
name.en: Applying Spelling Rules to Complex Words

description.zh: 能够正确、稳定地拼写单词，将小学阶段（KS1-2）所学的拼写模式与规则，运用到初中阶段（KS3）阅读及学科专项学习中遇到的复杂度不断提升的词汇上

evidence.zh: 能在新领域遇到学科专业词汇时正确拼写（如“parliament”“photosynthesis”“algorithm”）。

evidence.zh: 运用校对策略，识别并纠正自己长篇写作中的拼写错误。
evidence.en: Use proofreading strategies to identify and correct spelling errors in own extended writing

description.zh: 理解并解读修辞性语言、词语关系与词义的细微差别，涵盖典故、反语、双关语、矛盾修饰法、扩展隐喻等修辞类型；在分析或选用词语时，能够区分词语的字面意义与隐含意义。
description.en: Understand and interpret figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meaning — including allusion, irony, pun, oxymoron, and extended metaphor — and distinguish between connotation and denotation when analysing or choosing words

evidence.zh: 能识别文本中的反讽或典故，并解释其对文本含义的作用。

evidence.zh: 能分析段落或诗歌中的扩展隐喻，并解释其如何深化主题。
evidence.en: Analyse an extended metaphor across a paragraph or poem and explain how it develops an idea

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}阅读诗歌或小说时，如果作者使用了反讽、双关语或出人意料的比喻，他/她能否解释这种手法产生了什么效果，以及作者为什么选择这些词语？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} reads a poem or novel and the author uses irony, a pun, or an unexpected comparison, can they explain what effect it creates and why the author chose those words?

description.zh: 运用多种灵活策略判断生词、多义词及短语的含义，可使用的策略包括借助上下文线索、利用希腊语与拉丁语的词缀和词根、查阅参考资料，以及验证自己推测出的词义

evidence.zh: 能利用上下文线索（如句意、词的位置或语法功能）猜测生词意思

evidence.zh: 借助词典验证或修正推断的词义
evidence.en: Look up a word in a dictionary to verify or refine an inferred meaning

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}在阅读书籍或文章时遇到生词，能否通过上下文线索、词根词缀或词典来推断词义，并随后验证自己的推测是否准确？

description.zh: 在老师的引导下，大声重读自己的习作，检查读起来是否通顺；认真倾听并回应老师或小伙伴提出的问题与建议，以此补充细节、厘清意思、提升习作质量——这是写作自我评价的支架式启蒙阶段，并非需要孩子独立掌握的技能。
description.en: With teacher guidance, re-read own writing aloud to check it sounds right; listen and respond to questions and suggestions from teacher or peers to add detail, clarify meaning, and strengthen writing — this is the scaffolded beginning of writing self-evaluation, not an independent skill

evidence.zh: 通读自己的作文，能发现缺漏字词或表意不清的句子。

evidence.en: Add a detail in response to a question (e.g. 'Can you tell me more about...?')

evidence.zh: 能根据反馈对作品至少完成一处修改。
evidence.en: Make at least one improvement to a piece based on feedback

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}的老师让他们大声朗读自己写的作文，然后问“这一段读起来通顺吗？”时，{{name}}能否听取反馈并做出简单的修改来改进它？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}}'s teacher asks them to read their own writing aloud and then asks "does that bit make sense?", can {{name}} listen to the feedback and make a simple change to improve it?

name.zh: 写句子前先口头说句子

description.zh: 大声说出自己准备书写的内容，动笔写下来之前先口头组织句子，为独立写作做准备。
description.en: Say out loud what is going to be written; compose sentences orally before writing them down as preparation for independent writing

evidence.zh: 先完整口述句子，再动笔书写。
evidence.en: Say a complete sentence aloud before attempting to write it

evidence.zh: 通过反复口头复述句子来强化记忆。
evidence.en: Rehearse a sentence orally more than once to hold it in memory

evidence.zh: 先与同伴进行句子练习，再进行独立写作。
evidence.en: Practise sentences with a partner before writing independently

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在{{name}}动笔写句子之前，他们会先大声说出来——试试听起来怎么样——然后再落笔吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: Before {{name}} starts writing a sentence, do they say it out loud first — testing how it sounds — before putting pen to paper?

description.zh: 参与集体探究与写作项目；既可以回忆自身经历中的相关信息，也可以从各种渠道收集信息，以此解答问题。
description.en: Participate in shared research and writing projects; recall information from experiences or gather information from sources to answer a question

evidence.zh: 为班级写作项目提供想法和素材
evidence.en: Contribute ideas and information to a class writing project

evidence.zh: 针对某一主题，写出或画出基于个人经验的事实。
evidence.en: Draw or write facts learned from personal experience about a topic

evidence.zh: 能围绕小组研究任务，从书籍或成人处收集信息。
evidence.en: Help gather information from books or adults for a group research task

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}接到一个需要了解某事物（如某种动物或某个地方）的写作任务时，他们能否查找信息并利用所找到的内容来撰写有关该主题的文章？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} is given a writing project that involves finding out about something — like an animal or a place — can they look up information and use what they find to write about the topic?
