description.zh: 理解同伴压力——朋友和同龄人可能对你的选择和举止产生的影响——并学会一些策略，用来拒绝那些你知道不对或让你不舒服的事情。
description.en: Understand peer pressure — the influence friends and peers can have on your choices and behaviour — and develop strategies for resisting pressure to do something they know is wrong or that makes them uncomfortable

evidence.zh: 能用自己的话解释同伴压力，并举出一个生活中的例子。
evidence.en: Define peer pressure in their own words and give a real-world example

evidence.zh: 至少描述两种拒绝同伴压力的策略，如离开或运用幽默。
evidence.en: Describe at least two strategies for resisting peer pressure, such as walking away or using humour

evidence.zh: 阐释为何盲从错误行为常致事态恶化
evidence.en: Explain why going along with something wrong to fit in usually makes things worse

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}的朋友怂恿他/她做一些冒险或不友善的事情——比如偷拿糖果或发布别人出丑的照片——他/她能顶住压力并说明自己为什么不做吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}}'s friends dare them to do something risky or unkind — like shoplifting a sweet or posting an embarrassing photo of someone — can they resist the pressure and explain why they won't do it?

name.zh: 风险、不确定性与认知偏差

description.zh: 区分风险（概率已知的决策）和不确定性（结果未知的决策）；识别扭曲风险评估的认知偏差：可得性启发（根据例子容易想到的程度判断可能性）、现时偏差（过度重视眼前而忽视未来）、乐观偏差（低估个人风险）和群体思维；理解青少年大脑在生物学上倾向于更高的风险容忍度；将结构化决策框架应用于真实选择；理解在仅靠事实无法决定答案的决策中个人价值观的作用。
description.en: Distinguish between risk (decisions with known probabilities) and uncertainty (decisions with unknown outcomes); identify cognitive biases that distort risk assessment: availability heuristic (judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind), present bias (overvaluing the immediate over the future), optimism bias (underestimating personal risk), and groupthink; understand why adolescent brains are biologically calibrated toward higher risk tolerance; apply a structured decision-making framework to real choices; understand the role of personal values in decisions where facts alone cannot determine the answer

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么冒险并不总是非理性的——并描述一种导致人们在日常决策中误判风险的认知偏差，例如为什么青少年往往低估某些危险？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why taking a risk isn't always irrational — and describe one cognitive bias that causes people to misjudge risk in their everyday decisions, such as why teenagers tend to underestimate certain dangers?

description.zh: 理解网络身份的伦理，以及线上与线下身份保持一致的重要性；解释推荐算法和过滤气泡如何限制信息接触；评估虚假信息的心理机制：它为何传播、聪明人为何相信，以及如何运用来源评估（横向阅读、核查证据、识别情绪操纵）；理解分享图片或个人信息时的数字同意；探讨人工智能、监控和数据隐私对日常生活的伦理影响；反思负责任的内容创作和网络影响力。
description.en: Understand the ethics of online identity and the importance of consistency between who you are online and offline; explain how recommendation algorithms and filter bubbles narrow information exposure; evaluate the psychology of misinformation: why it spreads, why smart people believe it, and how to apply source evaluation (lateral reading, checking evidence, recognising emotional manipulation); understand digital consent around sharing images or personal information; explore the ethics of AI, surveillance, and data privacy as they affect everyday life; reflect on responsible content creation and online influence

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}在社交媒体上看到一个有说服力的说法时，他们能否描述自己决定是否相信或转发的过程——并解释为什么即使聪明的人也经常在网上被误导？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} sees a convincing claim shared on social media, can they describe their process for deciding whether to believe or share it — and explain why even intelligent people are regularly misled online?

description.zh: 介绍三种主要的伦理框架：后果主义（根据行为的结果和整体福祉来判断行为）、义务论（根据是否遵守规则和义务来判断行为，而不考虑后果）和美德伦理（根据行为所反映的品格来判断行为）；将每种框架应用于现实世界的道德困境：气候责任、人工智能伦理、公民不服从、财富不平等、医疗资源分配；理解每种框架的优势和局限性；培养仔细道德推理的能力——系统思考伦理问题的能力，而不仅仅依赖直觉或群体意见。
description.en: Introduce the three main ethical frameworks: consequentialism (judge actions by outcomes and overall welfare), deontology (judge actions by adherence to rules and duties regardless of consequences), and virtue ethics (judge actions by the character they reflect); apply each framework to real-world moral dilemmas: climate responsibility, AI ethics, civil disobedience, wealth inequality, healthcare rationing; understand the strengths and limitations of each framework; develop the capacity for careful moral reasoning — the ability to think through ethical questions systematically rather than relying only on intuition or group opinion

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否针对一个真实的伦理困境——例如为帮助他人而打破规则是否在任何情况下都正当——说明后果主义者、义务论者和美德伦理学者各自会如何以不同方式思考这一问题，并指出他们认为哪种思路最有说服力？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} take a real ethical dilemma — like whether it's ever right to break a rule to help someone — and explain how a consequentialist, a deontologist, and someone focused on virtue ethics would each think about it differently, and which approach they find most persuasive?

description.zh: 注意自己正在感受什么，并给它起个名字——能够说出一种情绪，是理解和调节它的第一步。
description.en: Notice what you are feeling and put a name to it — being able to label an emotion is the first step to understanding and managing it

evidence.zh: 情绪素养研究
evidence.en: emotional literacy research

evidence.zh: 培养幼儿情绪素养（HeadStart.gov）
evidence.en: Fostering Emotional Literacy in Young Children (HeadStart.gov)

evidence.zh: 情绪词汇发展 4-11岁（掌握标准）
evidence.en: emotion vocabulary development 4-11 years (PMC)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}看起来难过、兴奋或沮丧时，他们能否停下来告诉你他们感受到的是什么情绪——即使他们无法完全解释原因？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} seems upset, excited, or frustrated, can they stop and tell you what emotion they're feeling — even if they can't fully explain why?

description.zh: 认识并使用自我反思的词汇——自我意识、反思、模式、触发、假设、影响、视角和注意——并理解用准确的词语描述这些内心体验，能让我们更容易理解和谈论它们
description.en: Know and use the vocabulary of self-reflection — self-awareness, reflect, pattern, trigger, assumption, impact, perspective, and notice — and understand that having precise words for these inner experiences makes them easier to understand and talk about

evidence.zh: 能准确使用“反思”“模式”“触发”等词语描述自己的行为——例如：“我注意到一个模式：一赶时间我就容易烦躁。”
evidence.en: Use words like 'reflect', 'pattern', and 'trigger' accurately when describing their own behaviour — e.g. 'I notice a pattern: I get frustrated when I rush'

evidence.zh: 能用自己的话解释“自我意识”的含义，并结合自身举例说明。
evidence.en: Explain what 'self-awareness' means in their own words and give a personal example

evidence.zh: 能正确使用“perspective”一词，例如：“从我的角度看，这感觉不公平，但我也能理解他们的角度。”
evidence.en: Use the word 'perspective' correctly — e.g. 'From my perspective it felt unfair, but I can see theirs too'

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在经历了一段艰难时刻之后——比如与朋友闹翻或遇到令人沮丧的任务——{{name}}能否用“触发”或“反思”这样的词来谈论发生了什么，表现出他们在思考自己的反应，而不仅仅是对方做了什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: After a difficult moment — a falling-out with a friend or a frustrating task — can {{name}} talk about what happened using words like 'trigger' or 'reflect', showing they're thinking about their own reactions rather than just what the other person did?

description.zh: 理解感受和行为是分开的——你可以有强烈的感受，但不必马上采取行动。
description.en: Understand that feelings and actions are separate — you can feel something strongly without having to act on it straight away

evidence.zh: 情绪调节发展研究
evidence.en: emotion regulation development research

evidence.zh: 年龄与性别对情绪调节的影响（PMC 2020）
evidence.en: Effects of Age and Gender in Emotion Regulation (PMC 2020)

evidence.zh: 从情绪表达控制到情绪调节（PMC）
evidence.en: expressive control to emotion regulation (PMC)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否明白，感到愤怒、害怕或嫉妒并不意味着必须立刻付诸行动——在情绪和接下来选择怎么做之间，是存在一个缓冲空间的？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} understand that feeling angry, scared, or jealous doesn't mean they have to act on it immediately — that there's a gap between the feeling and what they choose to do next?

description.zh: 留意自己反应中的规律——比如“当我累了、被冷落或突然被提问时，我往往会这样反应”。
description.en: Notice patterns in your own reactions — 'I tend to respond like this when I'm tired, left out, or put on the spot'

evidence.zh: 童年中期情绪调节的自主能力
evidence.en: middle childhood self-reliance in emotion regulation

evidence.zh: 自我认知研究中的7年发展转变
evidence.en: 7-year developmental shift in self-understanding research

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否曾注意到自己的反应存在某种规律——比如，在一天中的某些时段更容易情绪低落，或者某类情境总是会稳定地引发强烈的情绪？
assessmentPrompt.en: Has {{name}} ever noticed a pattern in how they react — for example, that they get more upset at certain times of day, or that a particular type of situation reliably triggers a strong feeling?

description.zh: 反思自己的行为如何影响他人——不仅考虑你的本意，还要考虑对他人实际产生的影响。
description.en: Reflect on how your behaviour lands on others — consider not just what you intended but what the actual impact was on the other person

evidence.zh: 能描述自己的言行对他人的影响——例如：“我没把他算进去，他看起来很难过。”
evidence.en: Describe how something they said or did affected someone else — e.g. 'When I didn't include them, they looked upset'

evidence.zh: 行动前能预判后果——如“如果我不问就拿走最后一个，他们会觉得不公平”
evidence.en: Predict what might happen before acting — e.g. 'If I take the last one without asking, they'll feel it's unfair'

evidence.zh: 冲突后，能说明本可如何应对，以及不同应对方式会带来哪些不同结果。
evidence.en: After a conflict, explain what they could have done differently and what effect that would have had

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否换位思考一下，自己的言行在对方眼里是什么感受——不只是自己想表达什么，而是实际带来了什么影响？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} think about how something they said or did might have felt to the other person — not just what they meant by it, but what the impact actually was?

description.zh: 注意自己对社交情境的第一判断可能有误——你对他人行为原因的假设并不总是事实。
description.en: Notice when your first reading of a social situation might be wrong — your assumptions about why someone acted a certain way are not always facts

evidence.zh: 在回应同学行为前先暂停，考虑其他可能的解释——例如“也许他们是不小心碰到我，不是故意的”
evidence.en: Pause before reacting to a classmate's behaviour and consider an alternative explanation — e.g. 'Maybe they bumped me by accident, not on purpose'

evidence.zh: 描述一次他们曾对他人意图作最坏假设、后来发现判断有误的经历
evidence.en: Describe a time they assumed the worst about someone's intention and later found out they were wrong

evidence.zh: 在模糊的社交情境中，能对他人行为列出至少两种可能的解释，而不是急于下结论。
evidence.en: When told about an ambiguous social situation, suggest at least two possible reasons for the other person's behaviour instead of jumping to one conclusion

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}确信有人受到了不公平或不友善的对待，他们能否先停下来想一想，发生的事情是否可能有其他解释？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} felt sure someone was being unfair or unkind, could they pause and consider whether there might be another explanation for what happened?

description.zh: 反思自己随时间的变化——现在遇到的挑战并非一成不变，注意到自己已经发生的变化能建立真正的自我认识。
description.en: Reflect on your own growth over time — the things that challenge you now are not fixed, and noticing how you have already changed builds genuine self-knowledge

evidence.zh: 情绪词汇的发展持续至11岁（PMC）
evidence.en: emotion vocabulary development continues to age 11 (PMC)

evidence.zh: 儿童研究中自我反思的重要性
evidence.en: self-reflection importance in children research

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否回顾过去一两年，指出某件以前觉得非常困难、现在却处理得更好的事情，并说明发生了什么变化？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} look back over the past year or two and point to something they used to find really difficult that they now handle better — and explain what changed?

description.zh: 理解变化是生活中正常的一部分——比如开始上学、换新老师、家里添了小宝宝或搬家——并学会一些简单的应对策略
description.en: Understand that change is a normal part of life — such as starting school, getting a new teacher, a new baby arriving, or moving house — and identify simple strategies that help them cope with changes

evidence.zh: 能说出至少两种自身经历的变化及当时的感受
evidence.en: Name at least two changes they have experienced and how they felt

evidence.zh: 能识别在困境中可寻求支持的对象
evidence.en: Identify a person they can talk to when a change feels hard

evidence.zh: 描述一种应对变化的策略，如保持熟悉的日常作息。
evidence.en: Describe one strategy that helps them cope with change, such as keeping a familiar routine

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}的生活中发生一些变化时——比如在学校换了新老师——他们能否谈论这给他们带来的感受，并想出帮助自己适应的方法？
assessmentPrompt.en: When something changes in {{name}}'s life — like getting a new teacher at school — can they talk about how it makes them feel and think of ways to help themselves adjust?

description.zh: 理解犯错是学习中正常的一部分，每个人——包括大人——都会犯错，并开始将错误视为学习的机会，而不是放弃的理由。
description.en: Understand that making mistakes is a normal part of learning and that everyone — including adults — makes mistakes, and begin to see mistakes as opportunities to learn rather than reasons to give up

evidence.zh: 描述一次个人犯错经历并总结从中获得的教训
evidence.en: Describe a time they made a mistake and what they learned from it

evidence.zh: 犯错后能重新尝试而不放弃
evidence.en: Respond to a mistake by trying again rather than giving up

evidence.zh: 阐释错误对学习的促进作用
evidence.en: Explain why mistakes help people learn

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在课堂上答错问题或在游戏中失误，他们是能够迅速调整心态继续尝试，还是会情绪低落或说“我做不到”？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} gets an answer wrong in class or messes up during a game, do they bounce back and keep trying rather than shutting down or saying 'I can't do it'?

description.zh: 在等待想要的东西时不会变得非常烦躁——在日常生活中练习耐心和延迟满足，比如排队等待、等待点心或等待帮助
description.en: Wait for things they want without becoming very distressed — practising patience and delayed gratification in everyday situations like waiting their turn, waiting for a treat, or waiting for help

evidence.zh: 在游戏或活动中能轮流等待，不反复抱怨。
evidence.en: Wait for their turn in a game or activity without constant complaints

evidence.zh: 能说出自己在等待时使用的帮助自己等待的方法，例如想别的事情。
evidence.en: Describe what they do to help themselves wait, such as thinking about something else

evidence.zh: 能说出有时需要等待的原因，并指出等待是一种可以通过练习掌握的技能。
evidence.en: Explain why sometimes we have to wait and that it is a skill they can practise

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}必须排队等待他们非常想要的东西——比如玩iPad或让人盛饭——他们能不大吵大闹地等待吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} has to wait their turn for something they really want — like a go on the iPad or being served dinner — can they wait without a big fuss?

description.zh: 在感到难过或不知所措时，使用简单的冷静策略——比如深呼吸、数到十，或者去一个安静的地方——并明白这些方法能帮助身体和心情平静下来。
description.en: Use simple calming strategies when feeling upset or overwhelmed — such as taking deep breaths, counting to ten, or going to a quiet space — and understand that these help the body and mind settle down

evidence.zh: 在提示下能展示至少两种平静策略
evidence.en: Demonstrate at least two calming strategies when prompted

evidence.zh: 能在真实情绪失控情境中主动运用平静策略
evidence.en: Choose to use a calming strategy independently during a real upset

evidence.zh: 用通俗语言解释冷静有助于思考的原因。
evidence.en: Explain in simple terms why calming down helps them think better

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}非常难过时——比如输了比赛或和兄弟姐妹吵架——他能否运用深呼吸等策略让自己平复下来，而不是一直陷入情绪崩溃？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} gets really upset — say they lose a game or argue with a sibling — can they use a strategy like deep breaths to calm themselves down rather than staying in meltdown mode?

description.zh: 认识并使用管理强烈情绪的关键词——平静、策略、应对、平复、耐心、不知所措和深呼吸——并理解拥有这些词是运用它们的第一步
description.en: Know and use the key words for managing big feelings — calm, strategy, cope, settle, patience, overwhelmed, and breathe — and understand that having words for these ideas is the first step to using them

evidence.zh: 能准确运用“沮丧”“焦虑”“不堪重负”“失望”等词语描述自己在困境中的情绪感受
evidence.en: Use words like 'frustrated', 'anxious', 'overwhelmed', and 'disappointed' accurately to describe how they feel in difficult moments

evidence.zh: 能用自己的话解释“冷静下来”的策略，并列举至少两种自己用过的具体方法（如深呼吸、数数、暂时离开）。
evidence.en: Explain what 'calm down' strategies are in their own words and name at least two they have tried (e.g. deep breaths, counting, walking away)

evidence.zh: 区分相似情绪——例如，解释生气与失望的区别
evidence.en: Distinguish between similar feelings — e.g. explain the difference between being angry and being disappointed

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}感到非常难过或沮丧时，他/她能否用“我需要冷静一下”或“我觉得有点招架不住了”这样的话来表达，而不是直接发脾气？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} is feeling really upset or frustrated, can they use words like 'I need to calm down' or 'I'm feeling overwhelmed' instead of just acting out?

description.zh: 把有挑战的任务拆分成更小、更容易完成的步骤，而不是被整个任务吓倒——并在过程中庆祝每一个进步。
description.en: Break a challenging task into smaller, manageable steps rather than feeling overwhelmed by the whole thing — and celebrate progress along the way

evidence.zh: 面对一项有挑战性的任务，能将其拆解为至少三个更小的步骤来完成。
evidence.en: Take a challenging task and list at least three smaller steps to complete it

evidence.zh: 从第一步开始行动，而不是拖延整个任务。
evidence.en: Start with the first step rather than procrastinating on the whole task

evidence.zh: 每完成一步即给予正向反馈
evidence.en: Acknowledge progress after completing each step

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}有一个繁重的学校项目让他感到压力很大，他能否把它分解成更小的步骤——比如“我先做研究，然后写引言”——而不是因为整个任务而惊慌失措？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} has a big school project that feels overwhelming, can they break it down into smaller steps — like 'first I'll research, then I'll write the introduction' — rather than panicking about the whole thing?

description.zh: 理解不同情况需要不同的应对策略——对生气有效的方法可能对悲伤无效，在学校有帮助的方法可能和在家有帮助的方法不同。
description.en: Understand that different situations require different coping strategies — what works for anger might not work for sadness, and what helps at school might be different from what helps at home

evidence.zh: 能列举至少两种应对策略，并说明各自最适用的情境。
evidence.en: Name at least two different coping strategies and explain when each one is most useful

evidence.zh: 能根据具体情境和情绪选择恰当的策略
evidence.en: Choose an appropriate strategy based on the specific situation and emotion

evidence.zh: 反思一次策略失败的经历，并提出可尝试的替代方案
evidence.en: Reflect on a time a strategy didn't work and explain what they might try instead

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否意识到，当他们感到愤怒时，需要通过一些身体活动来调节，比如走一走；而当他们感到担忧时，则需要把内心的想法说出来——而不是对所有不舒服的情绪都采用同一种应对方式？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} recognise that when they're angry they need to do something physical like walk around, but when they're worried they need to talk it through — rather than using the same approach for every difficult feeling?

description.zh: 理解成长型思维的概念——能力与智力可以通过努力、练习和好方法不断提升，而不是固定型思维所认为的要么擅长、要么不擅长。
description.en: Understand the concept of a growth mindset — that abilities and intelligence can grow with effort, practice, and good strategies — as opposed to a fixed mindset where you believe you're either good at something or you're not

evidence.zh: 用自己的话解释成长型思维与固定型思维的区别
evidence.en: Explain the difference between growth mindset and fixed mindset in their own words

evidence.zh: 描述困难时使用“尚未”式表达
evidence.en: Use 'yet' language when describing something they find difficult

evidence.zh: 能举例说明自己通过练习和努力在哪方面取得了进步
evidence.en: Give an example of something they got better at through practice and effort

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}面对像学骑自行车或掌握乘法表这类困难任务时，他们会说“我还做不到”，而不是“我就是不擅长这个”吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} finds something difficult like learning to ride a bike or mastering times tables, do they say 'I can't do it YET' rather than 'I'm just not good at this'?

description.zh: 用积极的自我对话来应对困难情境——把“我真笨”或“我永远做不到”这类没用的想法，换成“这很难，但我可以继续努力”或“我以前也做成过难事”这类鼓励自己的想法。
description.en: Use positive self-talk to manage difficult situations — replacing unhelpful thoughts like 'I'm stupid' or 'I'll never be able to do this' with encouraging ones like 'This is hard but I can keep trying' or 'I've done hard things before'

evidence.zh: 能举例说明一个无益想法，并将其改写为有益想法。
evidence.en: Give an example of an unhelpful thought and rephrase it as a helpful one

evidence.zh: 在遇到挑战时，能够通过口头或书面形式进行积极的自我对话。
evidence.en: Use positive self-talk aloud or in writing when facing a challenge

evidence.zh: 解释自我对话如何影响自身感受与表现
evidence.en: Explain how the words we say to ourselves affect how we feel and perform

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}做作业遇到困难并开始说“我太笨了，这我根本做不好”时，他/她能否觉察到这种想法，并用更有帮助的想法来替代，比如“我只是需要换个方法试试”？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} is struggling with homework and starts saying 'I'm rubbish at this', can they catch that thought and replace it with something more helpful like 'I just need to try a different approach'?

description.zh: 认识并使用关于韧性和自我管理的词汇——包括调节、韧性、成长型思维、固定型思维、自我对话、触发点、挫折、坚持和痛苦——并理解每个词在实际中的含义。
description.en: Know and use the vocabulary of resilience and self-management — including regulate, resilience, growth mindset, fixed mindset, self-talk, trigger, setback, persevere, and distress — and understand what each word means in practice

evidence.zh: 能用自己的话解释“韧性”的含义，并举出一次面对困难仍坚持不放弃的经历。
evidence.en: Explain what 'resilience' means in their own words and give an example of a time they kept going when something was hard

evidence.zh: 正确运用“成长型思维”——例如：“我暂时还做不到，但通过练习我可以进步。”
evidence.en: Use 'growth mindset' correctly — e.g. 'I can't do it yet, but I can improve with practice'

evidence.zh: 定义“自我调节”并描述一种应对挫败感或挫折的策略
evidence.en: Define 'self-regulation' and describe a strategy they use to manage frustration or setbacks

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}的团队输了一场比赛，或者他们考试没考好，他们能否用“韧性”或“成长型思维”这样的词来谈论发生了什么——表明他们理解放弃和重新振作之间的区别？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}}'s team loses a match or they fail a test, can they talk about what happened using words like 'resilience' or 'growth mindset' — showing they understand the difference between giving up and bouncing back?

description.zh: 反思哪些自我调节和应对策略最适合自己，建立一个可以在不同情况下使用的“工具箱”，并与他人分享有效的方法。
description.en: Reflect on which self-regulation and coping strategies work best for them personally, building a 'toolkit' of approaches they can draw on in different situations and sharing what works with others

evidence.zh: 描述至少三种个人应对策略，并说明每种策略最适用的情境。
evidence.en: Describe at least three personal coping strategies and when each is most effective

evidence.zh: 能针对朋友的特定情况推荐相应策略
evidence.en: Recommend a strategy to a friend based on the friend's specific situation

evidence.zh: 评估所尝试策略的有效性并说明理由
evidence.en: Evaluate whether a strategy they tried worked well and explain their reasoning

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否说出“考试压力大时我会去散步，这对我有帮助，但难过时我需要找人聊聊”——这是否表明他们了解自己的应对策略工具箱？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} tell you 'When I'm stressed about exams I go for a walk and that helps, but when I'm sad I need to talk to someone' — showing they know their own coping toolkit?

description.zh: 设定切合实际的个人目标，制定简单的实现计划，监控自己的进度，并在方法不奏效时调整策略
description.en: Set realistic personal goals, create a simple plan to achieve them, monitor their own progress, and adjust their approach when things aren't working

evidence.zh: 能制定或表述一个具体、可实现且有截止期限的个人目标
evidence.en: Write or state a specific, achievable personal goal with a timeframe

evidence.zh: 描述他们将采取哪些步骤来实现目标
evidence.en: Describe the steps they will take to reach the goal

evidence.zh: 定期回顾进展，方法无效时及时调整计划。
evidence.en: Review their progress and adjust their plan when something isn't working

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否为自己设定一个目标——比如提高游泳水平或读完一套书——并真正一步步朝着它努力，必要时调整计划？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} set themselves a goal — like improving their swimming or finishing a book series — and actually work towards it step by step, adjusting their plan if needed?

description.zh: 理解心理韧性是指从挫折中恢复、适应困难环境并继续前进的能力——认识到心理韧性是一种通过经历培养出来的技能，而不是天生就有或没有的特质。
description.en: Understand resilience as the ability to recover from setbacks, adapt to difficult circumstances, and keep going — recognising that resilience is a skill that develops through experience, not a trait you either have or don't

evidence.zh: 能用自己的话解释心理韧性的含义，并说明其重要性。
evidence.en: Define resilience in their own words and explain why it matters

evidence.zh: 描述一次从挫折中恢复的经历，并说明是什么帮助他们走出来的。
evidence.en: Describe a time they bounced back from a setback and what helped them recover

evidence.zh: 说明韧性可以通过经历培养，遇到困难并不等于软弱。
evidence.en: Explain that resilience grows through experience and that struggling doesn't mean you're weak

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在一次真正的失望之后——比如没被选上学校戏剧的角色，或者认真复习了却没考好——{{name}}会不会先感到难过，但随后能振作起来，并想办法接下来该怎么做？
assessmentPrompt.en: After a real disappointment — like not getting a part in the school play or failing a test they studied for — can {{name}} feel upset but then pick themselves up and figure out what to do next?

description.zh: 有效管理自己的时间和注意力——优先处理任务，减少干扰，即使任务不那么有趣也能保持专注
description.en: Manage their own time and attention effectively — prioritising tasks, minimising distractions, and maintaining focus on important work even when it's not the most exciting option

evidence.zh: 能对多项任务制定简单计划，并按合理顺序完成。
evidence.en: Create a simple plan for completing multiple tasks in a sensible order

evidence.zh: 能识别自身常见的分心因素，并说出相应的应对策略。
evidence.en: Identify their own common distractions and describe strategies to manage them

evidence.zh: 在无需反复提醒的情况下，先完成较不喜欢的任务，再完成较喜欢的任务。
evidence.en: Complete a less enjoyable task before a more enjoyable one without constant reminders

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}既有作业要完成、又想玩游戏时，他/她能自己管理好时间吗——比如先做作业或设个定时器——而不是总需要你来督促？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} has homework to finish but also wants to play a game, can they manage their time — doing the homework first or setting a timer — rather than always needing you to enforce it?

description.zh: 区分良性压力（能激发动力、有成效的压力）和不良压力（有害的、令人不堪重负的压力）；解释生理压力反应（战斗-逃跑-僵住反应、HPA轴）以及长期压力如何影响身心；识别青少年常见的压力源（学业压力、社会比较、身体变化、对未来的不确定感）；评估基于证据的应对策略（运动、睡眠、正念、社会支持、表达性写作）；识别压力已演变为焦虑或抑郁的警告信号，并知道去哪里寻求帮助。
description.en: Distinguish between eustress (the productive, motivating kind of stress) and distress (harmful, overwhelming stress); explain the physiological stress response (fight-flight-freeze, HPA axis) and how chronic stress affects the body and mind; identify common adolescent stressors (academic pressure, social comparison, physical change, uncertainty about the future); evaluate evidence-based coping strategies (exercise, sleep, mindfulness, social support, expressive writing); recognise warning signs that stress has crossed into anxiety or depression and know where to get help

assessmentPrompt.zh: 当{{name}}面临考试或社交压力时，能否说出两到三种真正帮助自己管理压力的策略——并解释每种策略为什么有效，而不只是说“让自己感觉好一点”？
assessmentPrompt.en: When {{name}} is under pressure from exams or social situations, can they name two or three strategies that genuinely help them manage the stress — and explain why each one actually works, not just that it 'makes them feel better'?

description.zh: 理解习惯形成的提示-惯例-奖励循环，以及如何有意识地设计新习惯；区分内在动机（因为事情本身的价值而做）和外在动机（奖励/惩罚），并理解各自何时更有效；理解拖延主要是一个情绪调节问题（逃避不适），而不是时间管理失败；应用自我决定理论（自主性、胜任感、归属感）来增强内在动机；设计减少期望行为阻力的环境。
description.en: Understand habit formation through the cue-routine-reward loop and how to design new habits intentionally; distinguish intrinsic motivation (doing something for its own value) from extrinsic motivation (rewards/punishments) and understand when each is more effective; understand procrastination as primarily an emotion regulation problem (avoiding discomfort) rather than a time management failure; apply self-determination theory (autonomy, competence, relatedness) to boost intrinsic motivation; design environments that reduce friction for desired behaviours

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}一直想做某件重要的事却总是拖延，他能否解释人们拖延的真正原因——并不是因为懒——并说出一个可以实际调整环境、让开始变得更容易的具体做法？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} keeps meaning to do something important but finds themselves putting it off, can they explain the real reason people procrastinate — it's not laziness — and describe one practical change they could make to their environment to make starting easier?

description.zh: 理解面对严重挑战可以在三个方面带来真正的成长：对生活的新视角、改善的人际关系以及增强的个人能力感（创伤后成长）；区分真正的成长与有毒的积极（“一切事情的发生都是有原因的”）和否认；理解韧性并不意味着不受逆境影响，而是通过逆境恢复和成长；基于意义建构发展处理挫折的个人哲学；探索如何在不轻视他人经历的情况下支持他们度过严重困难。
description.en: Understand that facing serious challenges can lead to genuine growth in three domains: new perspectives on life, improved relationships, and a strengthened sense of personal capability (post-traumatic growth); distinguish genuine growth from toxic positivity ('everything happens for a reason') and from denial; understand that resilience does not mean being unaffected by adversity but recovering and growing through it; develop a personal philosophy for handling setbacks based on meaning-making; explore how to support others going through serious difficulty without minimising their experience

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否经历过真正艰难的事情，并发现这件事以有意义的方式改变了他们？他们能否解释什么是创伤后成长，以及它与仅仅“走出来”或假装某件艰难的事情没事有何不同？
assessmentPrompt.en: Has {{name}} ever come through something genuinely hard and found it changed them in a meaningful way? Can they explain what post-traumatic growth means and how it differs from just 'getting over it' or pretending something difficult was fine?

description.zh: 知道许多动物会使用伪装——即帮助它们融入周围环境的颜色和花纹——来躲避捕食者或悄悄接近猎物，比如看起来像树叶的叶虫，或者冬天会变白的北极兔。
description.en: Know that many animals use camouflage — colours and patterns that help them blend into their surroundings — to hide from predators or to sneak up on prey, like a leaf insect that looks like a leaf or an Arctic hare that turns white in winter

evidence.zh: 能解释保护色是指生物体色与周围环境相融合的现象。
evidence.en: Explains that camouflage means blending in with surroundings

evidence.zh: 至少列举出3种具有保护色的动物。
evidence.en: Gives at least 3 examples of camouflaged animals

evidence.zh: 能说明保护色的作用：帮助动物躲避天敌或隐蔽接近猎物。
evidence.en: Explains that camouflage helps animals hide from predators or sneak up on food

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}尝试在花园里找一只蚱蜢，他们能否解释蚱蜢很难被发现是因为它的绿色有助于它隐藏在草丛中——并举出其他使用保护色的动物例子？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} tries to spot a grasshopper in the garden, can they explain that it's hard to see because its green colour helps it hide in the grass — and give other examples of animals that use camouflage?

description.zh: 知道动物会建造或寻找许多不同种类的家——鸟儿筑巢，兔子挖洞，蜜蜂住在蜂巢里，寄居蟹用空壳，蜘蛛结网——这些庇护所保护它们和它们的宝宝
description.en: Know that animals make or find many different kinds of homes — birds build nests, rabbits dig burrows, bees live in hives, hermit crabs use empty shells, spiders spin webs — and that these shelters protect them and their young

evidence.zh: 能列举至少4种不同动物的住所（如巢、洞穴、蜂巢、网、壳、兽穴、窝）。
evidence.en: Names at least 4 different types of animal homes (nest, burrow, hive, web, shell, den, lodge)

evidence.zh: 能说出动物需要住所来遮风挡雨、保护幼崽。
evidence.en: Explains that animals need homes for shelter and to keep their babies safe

evidence.zh: 能匹配常见动物与其栖息地
evidence.en: Matches common animals to their homes

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果你问{{name}}不同动物住在哪里，他们能否描述几种动物的家——比如鸟巢、兔子洞或蜂巢——并说出动物为什么需要住所？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you ask {{name}} where different animals live, can they describe several animal homes — like a bird's nest, a rabbit's burrow, or a bee's hive — and say why animals need shelter?

description.zh: 认识一些世界动物纪录保持者——蓝鲸是史上最大的动物，猎豹是最快的陆地动物，吸蜜蜂鸟是最小的鸟，长颈鹿是最高的——并把它们的体型与熟悉的东西做比较。
description.en: Know some of the world's animal record-holders — the blue whale is the largest animal ever, the cheetah is the fastest land animal, the bee hummingbird is the smallest bird, the giraffe is the tallest — and compare their sizes to familiar objects

evidence.zh: 能说出至少4种动物之最及其纪录（如最快、最大、最高、最小等）。
evidence.en: Names at least 4 animal record-holders with their record (fastest, biggest, tallest, smallest, etc.)

evidence.zh: 能将动物的体型或能力与常见参照物进行比较
evidence.en: Compares an animal's size or ability to a familiar reference

evidence.zh: 表现出对动物之最知识的兴趣
evidence.en: Shows enthusiasm for superlative animal facts

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果你问{{name}}世界上哪种动物最快或最大，他们能否说出猎豹或蓝鲸等纪录保持者，并能将其大小与熟悉的事物进行比较，比如“蓝鲸有三辆公交车那么长”？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you ask {{name}} which animal is the fastest or the biggest in the world, can they name some record-holders like the cheetah or blue whale and compare their size to something familiar, like 'a blue whale is as long as three buses'?

description.zh: 知道动物生活在世界各地——在陆地上、水中和空中——每个大洲，甚至冰冷的南极洲，都是动物的家园，每种动物都适应它们所生活的环境。
description.en: Know that animals live all over the world — on land, in water, and in the air — and that every continent, even icy Antarctica, is home to animals, each suited to the conditions where they live

evidence.zh: 至少列举3种来自不同栖息地（如森林、海洋、沙漠）的动物。
evidence.en: Names at least 3 animals from different environments (e.g., forest, ocean, desert)

evidence.zh: 能说出动物的生存环境各不相同，有的生活在陆地上，有的生活在水里，有的会飞。
evidence.en: States that animals live on land, in water, and some can fly

evidence.zh: 掌握各洲动物的分布。
evidence.en: Recognises that animals live on every continent

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果你给{{name}}看北极熊、鹦鹉、骆驼和企鹅的图片，他们能说出这些动物生活在世界上不同的地方吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you show {{name}} pictures of a polar bear, a parrot, a camel, and a penguin, can they tell you that animals live in all sorts of different places around the world?

description.zh: 知道不同的动物生宝宝的方式不一样——有些动物会下蛋（比如鸟类、爬行动物、鱼类、昆虫），有些动物会直接生出小宝宝（大多数哺乳动物）——而且动物宝宝有的长得像缩小版的大人，有的和爸爸妈妈长得完全不一样。
description.en: Know that different animals have their babies in different ways — some lay eggs (birds, reptiles, fish, insects), some give birth to live young (most mammals) — and that babies may look like miniature adults or look very different from their parents

evidence.zh: 能举例说明卵生动物和胎生动物。
evidence.en: Gives examples of animals that lay eggs and animals that give birth to live young

evidence.zh: 能举例说明至少一种幼体与成体形态不同的生物（如蝌蚪/青蛙、毛毛虫/蝴蝶）。
evidence.en: Describes at least one example of a baby that looks different from its parent (e.g., tadpole/frog, caterpillar/butterfly)

evidence.zh: 对动物的繁殖方式感到好奇
evidence.en: Shows curiosity about how different animals have their babies

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在自然节目中看到一个有蛋的鸟巢，他/她能解释鸟类是卵生、幼鸟从蛋中孵化出来，而狗和猫的宝宝是胎生直接生出来的吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a nest with eggs in a nature programme, can they explain that birds lay eggs and the babies hatch out, but dogs and cats have their babies born alive?

description.zh: 知道有些动物是夜行动物——它们在夜间活动，白天睡觉——而且夜行动物通常有特殊的特征，比如大眼睛（猫头鹰、眼镜猴）、大耳朵（蝙蝠、耳廓狐）或敏感的胡须，帮助它们在黑暗中寻找食物。
description.en: Know that some animals are nocturnal — active at night and sleeping during the day — and that nocturnal animals often have special features like big eyes (owls, tarsiers), large ears (bats, fennec foxes), or sensitive whiskers to help them find food in the dark

evidence.zh: 能解释“夜行性”的含义
evidence.en: Explains what 'nocturnal' means

evidence.zh: 能列举至少3种夜行动物（如猫头鹰、蝙蝠、狐狸、刺猬、飞蛾）
evidence.en: Names at least 3 nocturnal animals (e.g., owl, bat, fox, hedgehog, moth)

evidence.zh: 描述夜行动物的一项特征（如大眼睛、回声定位、触须）
evidence.en: Describes one feature that helps a nocturnal animal (e.g., big eyes, echolocation, whiskers)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在睡前听到猫头鹰叫，他/她能解释猫头鹰是夜行动物——也就是白天睡觉、晚上出来活动——并且它们的大眼睛能帮助它们在黑暗中看清东西吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} hears an owl hooting at bedtime, can they explain that owls are nocturnal — meaning they sleep during the day and come out at night — and that their big eyes help them see in the dark?

name.zh: 野生动物、农场动物和宠物

description.zh: 了解野生动物、农场动物和宠物之间的区别——野生动物在自然界中自己寻找食物和住所；农场动物由人们饲养，用来获取食物、羊毛或鸡蛋；宠物是人们为了陪伴而饲养的动物——并知道应该与野生动物保持距离观察
description.en: Understand the difference between wild animals, farm animals, and pets — wild animals find their own food and shelter in nature; farm animals are kept by people for food, wool, or eggs; pets are animals people keep for companionship — and know that wild animals should be observed from a distance

evidence.zh: 能够对动物进行分类（野生动物、农场动物、宠物）并举例说明。
evidence.en: Sorts animals into wild, farm, and pet categories with examples

evidence.zh: 能说出各类别间的一项关键区别
evidence.en: Explains one key difference between each category

evidence.zh: 掌握安全观察野生动物的方法，做到不靠近、不打扰。
evidence.en: Understands that wild animals should be observed, not approached

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在花园里看到一只狐狸，他们能否解释狐狸是野生动物——不同于家里的宠物猫或农场的绵羊——并且野生动物会自己照顾自己，不应该去触摸？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a fox in the garden, can they explain that it's a wild animal — different from their pet cat or a farm sheep — and that wild animals look after themselves and shouldn't be touched?

description.zh: 了解动物会用许多不同的方式交流——鸟儿唱歌是为了吸引伴侣和保卫领地，鲸鱼能隔着广阔的海洋互相呼唤，蜜蜂用舞蹈告诉其他蜜蜂食物在哪里，狼用嚎叫让狼群保持团结，萤火虫则用闪光发信号——交流对动物的生存来说非常重要。
description.en: Understand that animals communicate in many different ways — birds sing to attract mates and defend territory, whales call across vast ocean distances, bees dance to show other bees where food is, wolves howl to keep the pack together, and fireflies flash light signals — and that communication is essential for survival

evidence.zh: 至少能说出4种动物交流方式（声音、舞蹈、发光、气味、肢体语言）。
evidence.en: Describes at least 4 different methods of animal communication (sound, dance, light, scent, body language)

evidence.zh: 能为每种方法举出具体的动物实例
evidence.en: Gives a specific animal example for each method

evidence.zh: 能举例说明动物通过交流进行求偶、警报或指示食物位置。
evidence.en: Explains that animals communicate to find mates, warn of danger, or share food locations

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在早晨听到鸟鸣，能否解释鸟鸣是一种交流方式——并至少描述两种其他动物相互传递信息的方式？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} hears birds singing in the morning, can they explain that birdsong is a way of communicating — and describe at least two other ways different animals send messages to each other?

description.zh: 了解许多动物会进行令人惊叹的长途旅行，称为迁徙——北极燕鸥从一极飞到另一极，黑脉金斑蝶穿越北美飞行数千英里，角马跟随降雨穿越塞伦盖蒂，座头鲸在极地觅食地和热带繁殖水域之间游动——这些旅行与食物、繁殖和季节有关。
description.en: Know that many animals make incredible journeys called migrations — Arctic terns fly from pole to pole, monarch butterflies travel thousands of miles across North America, wildebeest cross the Serengeti following rain, and humpback whales swim between polar feeding grounds and tropical breeding waters — and that these journeys are linked to food, breeding, and seasons

evidence.zh: 能准确将迁徙定义为动物周期性的长距离移动。
evidence.en: Defines migration as a regular long journey animals make

evidence.zh: 能说出至少3种迁徙动物及其迁徙路线或目的地。
evidence.en: Names at least 3 migratory animals with their routes or destinations

evidence.zh: 能说明迁徙是由食物来源、繁殖或季节变化驱动的。
evidence.en: Explains that migration is driven by food availability, breeding, or seasonal changes

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}学习了黑脉金斑蝶的迁徙旅程，他们能否解释迁徙的含义，并说出至少两种其他进行长途迁徙的动物——还能说明它们迁徙的原因？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} learns about the monarch butterfly's journey, can they explain what migration means and name at least two other animals that make long journeys — and say why they travel?

description.zh: 探索沙漠中的动物——骆驼、耳廓狐、蝎子、响尾蛇、狐獴——了解沙漠动物如何通过夜间活动、储存水分或脂肪、白天在地下打洞以及长着大耳朵散热来在极端炎热和缺水的环境中生存。
description.en: Explore animals of the desert — camels, fennec foxes, scorpions, rattlesnakes, meerkats — and understand how desert animals survive extreme heat and lack of water through being active at night, storing water or fat, burrowing underground during the day, and having large ears to lose heat

evidence.zh: 至少列举出4种沙漠动物
evidence.en: Names at least 4 desert animals

evidence.zh: 能说明至少两种沙漠生存适应方式（夜行、储水、穴居、大耳散热）
evidence.en: Explains at least two desert survival adaptations (nocturnal behaviour, water storage, burrowing, large ears for cooling)

evidence.zh: 了解沙漠有冷热类型之分，但均具有干燥少雨的特征
evidence.en: Knows deserts can be hot or cold but are always dry

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}阅读了关于沙漠中骆驼的内容，他们能否至少说出沙漠动物应对高温和缺水的两种方式——比如夜间活动或具有特殊的身体特征？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} reads about camels in a desert, can they explain at least two ways desert animals cope with the heat and lack of water — like being active at night or having special body features?

description.zh: 探索北极和南极的动物——北方的北极熊、北极狐和海象；南方的企鹅、海豹和信天翁——并了解极地动物如何通过厚厚的皮毛或鲸脂、抱团取暖以及像冬季白毛这样的季节性变化来在极端寒冷中生存。
description.en: Explore animals of the Arctic and Antarctic — polar bears, Arctic foxes, and walruses in the north; penguins, seals, and albatrosses in the south — and understand how polar animals survive extreme cold through thick fur or blubber, huddling behaviour, and seasonal changes like white winter coats

evidence.zh: 能分别列举北极和南极至少3种动物。
evidence.en: Names at least 3 animals each from the Arctic and Antarctic

evidence.zh: 能说出至少两种御寒适应特征（鲸脂、厚毛皮、集群取暖、白色伪装）。
evidence.en: Explains at least two adaptations for surviving cold (blubber, thick fur, huddling, white camouflage)

evidence.zh: 能说出北极熊仅分布于北极，企鹅仅分布于南极/南半球。
evidence.en: Knows polar bears live only in the Arctic and penguins only in the Antarctic/Southern Hemisphere

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}观看了一部关于北极的自然节目，他们能否解释北极熊如何在严寒中保持温暖，并说出北极动物（北方）与南极动物（南方）之间的至少两点不同？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a nature programme about the Arctic, can they explain how polar bears stay warm in freezing temperatures and name at least two differences between Arctic animals (north) and Antarctic animals (south)?

description.zh: 了解捕食者进化出了捕猎策略——狼群集体捕猎，变色龙用长舌头，蜘蛛结网，鳄鱼在水边伏击——而猎物也进化出了防御机制——豪猪的尖刺，臭鼬的喷雾，箭毒蛙的毒素，斑马的条纹迷惑捕食者，装死
description.en: Understand that predators have evolved hunting strategies — wolves hunt in packs, chameleons use their long tongues, spiders build webs, crocodiles ambush at water's edge — and prey animals have evolved defences — porcupine spines, skunk spray, poison dart frog toxins, zebra stripes confusing predators, playing dead

evidence.zh: 能举例说明至少3种捕食者的捕猎策略
evidence.en: Describes at least 3 predator hunting strategies with examples

evidence.zh: 至少列举并说明3种猎物的防御机制。
evidence.en: Describes at least 3 prey defence mechanisms with examples

evidence.zh: 理解捕食者与猎物之间的“协同进化”概念
evidence.en: Understands the concept of an 'arms race' between predators and prey

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}观看一个展示狮子捕猎的自然节目，他能否描述至少两种捕食者捕捉猎物的方式，以及两种猎物自我防御的方式？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} watches a nature programme showing a lion hunting, can they describe at least two different ways predators catch food and two ways prey animals defend themselves?

description.zh: 探索热带雨林中的动物——地球上物种最丰富的栖息地。了解雨林分为不同层次（树冠层、林下层、森林地面），每层生活着不同的动物：树冠层里有巨嘴鸟和猴子，地面上有美洲豹和青蛙。同时知道雨林位于赤道附近。
description.en: Explore animals of the tropical rainforest — the most species-rich habitat on Earth — learning that the forest has layers (canopy, understory, forest floor) with different animals at each level: toucans and monkeys in the canopy, jaguars and frogs on the floor, and that rainforests are found near the equator

evidence.zh: 能说出至少4种来自不同雨林层的动物
evidence.en: Names at least 4 rainforest animals from different layers

evidence.zh: 描述雨林的分层结构（林冠层、林下层、林地层）
evidence.en: Describes the rainforest as having layers (canopy, understory, forest floor)

evidence.zh: 能说出热带雨林分布在赤道附近，气候炎热潮湿。
evidence.en: Explains that rainforests are near the equator and are hot and wet

evidence.zh: 了解雨林中的物种数量几乎超过其他任何栖息地
evidence.en: Recognises that rainforests have more species than almost any other habitat

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}观看了一部关于雨林的纪录片，他们能否描述至少三种生活在其中的动物，并说明不同动物分别栖息在森林的不同层次——有些在树冠层，有些在地面？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} watches a documentary about rainforests, can they describe at least three animals that live there and explain that different animals live at different heights in the forest — some in the treetops and some on the ground?

description.zh: 探索草原和稀树草原上的动物——非洲稀树草原上的狮子、斑马、角马、大象、猎豹；美洲草原上的野牛和草原犬鼠——了解为什么开阔的草原上会形成大群动物，以及捕食者和猎物在这些广阔空间里如何互动。
description.en: Explore animals of the grasslands and savanna — lions, zebras, wildebeest, elephants, cheetahs in African savanna; bison and prairie dogs in American grasslands — understanding why large herds form on open grasslands and how predators and prey interact in these wide-open spaces

evidence.zh: 能列举至少5种草原/稀树草原动物
evidence.en: Names at least 5 grassland/savanna animals

evidence.zh: 能说明群居可通过数量优势抵御捕食者。
evidence.en: Explains that herding provides safety in numbers against predators

evidence.zh: 描述捕食者与被捕食者的关系（如狮子捕猎斑马）
evidence.en: Describes the predator-prey relationship (e.g., lions hunt zebras)

evidence.zh: 理解草原/稀树草原为树木稀疏的开阔栖息地。
evidence.en: Knows grasslands/savannas are wide-open habitats with few trees

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到非洲大草原的图片，他们能否说出至少四种生活在那里的动物，并解释为什么像斑马这样的动物会成群结队地生活？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees pictures of the African savanna, can they name at least four animals that live there and explain why some animals like zebras live in large herds?

description.zh: 知道昆虫和其他微小生物（蜘蛛、蚯蚓、蜗牛、蜈蚣）是地球上数量最多、种类最丰富的动物群体——甲虫的种类比其他任何动物都多——并且它们在传粉（蜜蜂、蝴蝶）、分解（潮虫、蚯蚓）和作为其他动物的食物方面发挥着重要作用。
description.en: Know that insects and other minibeasts (spiders, worms, snails, centipedes) are the most numerous and diverse group of animals on Earth — there are more species of beetle than any other animal — and that they play vital roles as pollinators (bees, butterflies), decomposers (woodlice, worms), and food for other animals

evidence.zh: 知道昆虫等小型动物是动物界中种类最多的类群。
evidence.en: Knows that insects/minibeasts are the most numerous animal group

evidence.zh: 能列举微生物的至少3种作用：传粉、分解、作为食物来源。
evidence.en: Names at least 3 roles minibeasts play: pollinators, decomposers, food source

evidence.zh: 能区分昆虫（6条腿）、蜘蛛（8条腿）及其他小型无脊椎动物。
evidence.en: Distinguishes insects (6 legs) from spiders (8 legs) from other minibeasts

evidence.zh: 认识到无脊椎动物的重要性
evidence.en: Shows appreciation for the importance of invertebrates

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在花园里看到一只蜜蜂，他们能否解释蜜蜂为什么重要——并说出至少两种其他昆虫和小型生物为帮助自然界所做的工作？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} spots a bee in the garden, can they explain why bees are important — and name at least two other jobs that insects and minibeasts do that help the natural world?

description.zh: 探索动物的智慧和复杂行为——黑猩猩和乌鸦会使用工具，海豚能在镜子里认出自己，章鱼能解开谜题并逃出围栏，大象会哀悼死去的同伴，猫鼬会教幼崽对付蝎子——了解许多动物会思考、学习，并且拥有比人们过去认为的更复杂的社交生活。
description.en: Explore animal intelligence and complex behaviour — chimpanzees and crows use tools, dolphins recognise themselves in mirrors, octopuses solve puzzles and escape enclosures, elephants mourn their dead, meerkats teach their young to handle scorpions — understanding that many animals think, learn, and have social lives more complex than once believed

evidence.zh: 至少列举4个动物智慧或复杂行为的实例
evidence.en: Gives at least 4 examples of animal intelligence or complex behaviour

evidence.zh: 能解释“工具使用”的含义，并至少列举2种会使用工具的动物。
evidence.en: Explains what 'tool use' means and names at least 2 tool-using animals

evidence.zh: 能说明科学家如何测试动物智力（镜像测试、谜题箱、观察法）
evidence.en: Discusses how scientists test animal intelligence (mirror test, puzzle boxes, observation)

evidence.zh: 能理解不同物种在智力表现形式上的差异
evidence.en: Shows understanding that intelligence takes different forms in different species

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}观看了一段乌鸦用树枝从管子里取食的视频，他们能否解释这说明动物具有智力，并举出其他动物使用工具、解决问题或表现出复杂行为的例子？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} watches a video of a crow using a stick to get food from a tube, can they explain that this shows animal intelligence and give other examples of animals that use tools, solve problems, or show complex behaviour?

description.zh: 理解生物多样性——生态系统中不同物种的多样性——对健康的生态系统至关重要，并且关键物种（如黄石公园的狼、海带林中的海獭或作为传粉者的蜜蜂）对其生态系统有着巨大的影响，因此失去一个关键物种可能引发连锁变化，影响许多其他物种。
description.en: Understand that biodiversity — the variety of different species in an ecosystem — is essential for healthy ecosystems, and that keystone species (like wolves in Yellowstone, sea otters in kelp forests, or bees as pollinators) have an outsized impact on their ecosystem, so that losing one key species can cause a cascade of changes affecting many others

evidence.zh: 能将生物多样性定义为生态系统中的物种多样性
evidence.en: Defines biodiversity as the variety of species in an ecosystem

evidence.zh: 解释生物多样性的重要性（稳定性、恢复力、生态系统服务）
evidence.en: Explains why biodiversity matters (stability, resilience, ecosystem services)

evidence.zh: 能定义关键物种，并至少举出2个例子。
evidence.en: Defines keystone species and gives at least 2 examples

evidence.zh: 描述因移除或引入某一物种而引发的营养级联或连锁反应。
evidence.en: Describes a trophic cascade or chain reaction from removing/adding a species

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}学习了狼是如何被重新引入黄石公园并改变整个生态系统的，他/她能否解释什么是“关键物种”，以及为什么一个地区拥有许多不同物种很重要？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} learns about how wolves were brought back to Yellowstone and the whole ecosystem changed, can they explain what a 'keystone species' is and why having many different species in an area matters?

description.zh: 了解为什么有些动物物种会濒危或灭绝——栖息地破坏、狩猎/偷猎、污染、气候变化和入侵物种——并认识大熊猫、山地大猩猩、远东豹等例子，以及已经灭绝的渡渡鸟和袋狼，同时知道世界自然保护联盟红色名录是科学家用来追踪受威胁物种的系统。
description.en: Understand why some animal species become endangered or go extinct — habitat destruction, hunting/poaching, pollution, climate change, and invasive species — and know examples like the giant panda, mountain gorilla, Amur leopard, and the now-extinct dodo and thylacine, using the IUCN Red List as the system scientists use to track threatened species

evidence.zh: 能准确说出濒危物种是指面临灭绝风险的物种。
evidence.en: Defines endangered as a species at risk of extinction

evidence.zh: 至少说出物种濒危的3个原因
evidence.en: Names at least 3 causes of species becoming endangered

evidence.zh: 至少列举出3种濒危或已灭绝的动物。
evidence.en: Gives at least 3 examples of endangered or extinct animals

evidence.zh: 了解IUCN红色名录作为追踪系统的功能。
evidence.en: Knows the IUCN Red List exists as a tracking system

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到一则关于濒危动物的新闻，他/她能解释“濒危”是什么意思，并至少说出三个导致某些动物面临永远消失风险的原因吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a news story about an endangered animal, can they explain what 'endangered' means and describe at least three reasons why some animals are at risk of disappearing forever?

description.zh: 理解入侵物种是指被引入到它们原本不属于的地方的动物（或植物）——比如英国的灰松鼠排挤红松鼠、澳大利亚的甘蔗蟾蜍毒害本地捕食者、或者兔子破坏澳大利亚的生态系统——它们会通过争夺食物、传播疾病或因为没有天敌而对本地野生动物造成严重伤害。
description.en: Understand that invasive species are animals (or plants) that have been introduced to a place where they don't naturally belong — like grey squirrels outcompeting red squirrels in the UK, cane toads poisoning native predators in Australia, or rabbits devastating ecosystems in Australia — and that they can cause serious harm to native wildlife by competing for food, spreading disease, or having no natural predators

evidence.zh: 能将入侵物种定义为被引入新环境的非本地动物
evidence.en: Defines invasive species as non-native animals introduced to a new environment

evidence.zh: 至少列举2个入侵物种及其影响的例子
evidence.en: Names at least 2 examples of invasive species and their impacts

evidence.zh: 能说明入侵物种有害的至少两个原因（缺少天敌、竞争排斥本地物种、传播疾病）
evidence.en: Explains at least 2 reasons invasive species are harmful (no predators, outcompete natives, spread disease)

evidence.zh: 理解自然扩散与人为引入在物种分布范围上的区别
evidence.en: Understands the difference between a species naturally expanding its range and being introduced by humans

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}知道灰松鼠是从美国被带到英国的，他们能否解释为什么外来动物会给原本生活在那里的动物带来问题？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} learns that grey squirrels were brought to the UK from America, can they explain why introduced animals can be a problem for the animals that were already living there?

description.zh: 了解人们如何努力保护濒危动物——通过国家公园和海洋保护区、圈养繁殖计划（如拯救加州神鹫和阿拉伯剑羚的计划）、反偷猎巡逻、连接栖息地的野生动物走廊，以及禁止濒危物种贸易的法律——并理解孩子们可以通过对栖息地友好的选择做出贡献。
description.en: Know how people work to protect endangered animals — through national parks and marine reserves, captive breeding programmes (like those that saved the California condor and Arabian oryx), anti-poaching patrols, wildlife corridors connecting habitats, and laws banning trade in endangered species — and understand that children can contribute through habitat-friendly choices

evidence.zh: 能列举至少3种保护策略并举例说明
evidence.en: Describes at least 3 conservation strategies with specific examples

evidence.zh: 能举例说出一种因保护措施而免于灭绝的动物。
evidence.en: Names an animal saved from near-extinction by conservation efforts

evidence.zh: 能列举至少一项儿童或家庭可参与的野生动物保护行动。
evidence.en: Suggests at least one action children or families can take to help wildlife

evidence.zh: 理解生物多样性保护需兼顾栖息地保护与物种个体保护。
evidence.en: Understands that conservation requires both protecting habitats and helping individual species

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}参观一个有繁育项目的动物园，他们能否解释动物园如何帮助拯救濒危物种，并描述至少两种人们保护野生动物的其他方式？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} visits a zoo with a breeding programme, can they explain how zoos help save endangered species and describe at least two other ways people protect wildlife?

description.zh: 理解动物具有结构适应性（身体特征，如长颈鹿的长脖子、鹰的利爪、海豚的流线型身体）、行为适应性（迁徙、冬眠、使用工具）和生理适应性（北极鱼血液中的抗冻物质、蝙蝠的回声定位）——并且这些适应性是通过自然选择经过许多代发展而来的
description.en: Understand that animals have structural adaptations (body features like the giraffe's long neck, eagle's talons, dolphin's streamlined shape), behavioural adaptations (migration, hibernation, tool use), and physiological adaptations (antifreeze in Arctic fish blood, echolocation in bats) — and that these developed over many generations through natural selection

evidence.zh: 能将适应定义为有助于动物在其环境中生存的特征或行为。
evidence.en: Defines adaptation as a feature or behaviour that helps an animal survive in its environment

evidence.zh: 能举例说明结构适应、行为适应和生理适应。
evidence.en: Gives examples of structural, behavioural, and physiological adaptations

evidence.zh: 解释适应是经过许多世代逐渐形成的，而非在动物个体的一生中发生。
evidence.en: Explains that adaptations develop over many generations, not during one animal's lifetime

evidence.zh: 能初步建立适应与自然选择的联系
evidence.en: Connects adaptations to the concept of natural selection at a basic level

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到啄木鸟啄树，能否解释其坚硬的喙、长长的舌头和减震的头骨都是适应性特征，并能举出其他例子来说明“适应性”一词的含义？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a woodpecker pecking a tree, can they explain that its strong beak, long tongue, and shock-absorbing skull are all adaptations — and describe what the word 'adaptation' means with other examples?

description.zh: 理解共生关系——不同物种之间的紧密联系——包括互利共生（双方都受益，比如小丑鱼和海葵）、偏利共生（一方受益而不伤害另一方，比如䲟鱼搭乘鲨鱼）和寄生（一方受益而另一方受损，比如鹿身上的蜱虫）——并能在自然界中识别这些关系。
description.en: Understand symbiosis — close relationships between different species — including mutualism (both benefit, like clownfish and anemones), commensalism (one benefits without harming the other, like remora fish riding sharks), and parasitism (one benefits at the other's expense, like ticks on deer) — and recognise these relationships in nature

evidence.zh: 能将共生定义为不同物种之间的密切关系
evidence.en: Defines symbiosis as a close relationship between different species

evidence.zh: 能区分互利共生、偏利共生和寄生，并能分别举例。
evidence.en: Distinguishes mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism with an example of each

evidence.zh: 能在新情境中识别共生关系
evidence.en: Identifies symbiotic relationships when presented with new scenarios

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到一档自然节目，展示一只小鸟在水牛背上啄食昆虫，他/她能否解释这两种动物都从这种关系中受益，并说出这种共生关系的类型？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a nature programme showing a small bird picking insects off a buffalo's back, can they explain that both animals benefit from this relationship and name the type of symbiosis?

description.zh: 介绍红皇后假说——物种必须不断进化，才能在与共同进化的伙伴的竞争中保持适应度；描述捕食者与猎物之间的军备竞赛（猎豹的速度与瞪羚的速度、蝙蝠的回声定位与飞蛾的听觉干扰）以及寄生虫与宿主的共同进化（兔子的黏液瘤病）；解释达尔文的鹰蛾与兰花作为互利共生共同进化的经典例子，并预测了一个未知物种；理解共同进化是生物多样性的主要驱动力。
description.en: Introduce the Red Queen hypothesis — species must keep evolving just to maintain fitness relative to co-evolving partners; describe predator-prey arms races (cheetah speed vs gazelle speed, bat echolocation vs moth hearing jamming) and parasite-host co-evolution (myxomatosis in rabbits); explain Darwin's hawk moth and orchid as a classic example of mutualistic co-evolution predicting an unknown species; understand that co-evolution is a major driver of biological diversification

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释“进化军备竞赛”的概念——即捕食者与其猎物如何针对彼此不断进化出更强的攻击和防御策略，却始终难分高下？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain the idea of an evolutionary arms race — how a predator and its prey keep evolving better attack and defence strategies in response to each other, never quite getting ahead?

description.zh: 解释深海动物如何应对巨大的压力（没有充气空间、柔性蛋白质、适应压力的酶）；描述体温调节的极端情况——南极鱼类的抗冻糖蛋白、木蛙的过冷现象；介绍缓步动物和隐生现象（在干燥、极端温度、辐射、真空中存活）；调查其他极端微生物（热液喷口处的嗜热菌、盐滩中的嗜盐菌）；思考这些生物告诉我们生命的极限是什么。
description.en: Explain how deep-sea animals cope with crushing pressure (no gas-filled spaces, flexible proteins, pressure-adapted enzymes); describe thermoregulation extremes — antifreeze glycoproteins in Antarctic fish, supercooling in wood frogs; introduce tardigrades and cryptobiosis (surviving desiccation, extreme temperatures, radiation, vacuum); survey other extremophiles (thermophiles at hydrothermal vents, halophiles in salt flats); consider what these organisms tell us about the limits of life

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否描述一种能在被冻成冰、完全脱水或暴露于太空真空中存活下来的动物，并大致解释它如何能在几乎任何其他生物都无法存活的条件下生存？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} describe an animal that can survive being frozen solid, completely dried out, or exposed to the vacuum of space — and explain roughly how it manages to survive conditions that would kill almost any other living thing?

description.zh: 解释性选择作为自然选择的一种形式：孔雀尾巴的失控选择、极乐鸟的炫耀、青蛙的叫声；解释亲缘选择和利他行为——为什么工蜂会为保护蜂巢而死，为什么猫鼬会冒着个人风险站岗（汉密尔顿法则、广义适合度）；使用鹰鸽模型介绍动物行为中的博弈论；定义认知动物行为学，并综述动物情感、玩耍和文化的证据。
description.en: Explain sexual selection as a form of natural selection: runaway selection for peacock tails, bird of paradise displays, and frog calls; explain kin selection and altruistic behaviour — why worker bees die to protect the hive, why meerkats stand guard at personal risk (Hamilton's rule, inclusive fitness); introduce game theory in animal behaviour using the hawk-dove model; define cognitive ethology and survey evidence for animal emotions, play, and culture

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么工蜂为保护蜂巢而牺牲在进化上是合理的——尽管这只蜜蜂从未有自己的后代？使这成为一种成功策略的逻辑是什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why a worker bee dying to protect the hive actually makes evolutionary sense — even though the bee never has its own offspring? What's the logic that makes this a successful strategy?

description.zh: 量化当前的生物多样性危机：物种灭绝速率是背景灭绝速率的100到1000倍；解释衡量生物多样性丧失的方法（物种-面积关系、种群生存力分析、世界自然保护联盟红色名录等级）；评估野化案例研究——黄石公园狼群重新引入引发营养级联，改变了河道；伊比利亚猞猁恢复；描述最小可存活种群理论和保护分类；探讨决定优先保护哪些物种时的伦理争论。
description.en: Quantify the current biodiversity crisis: extinction rates 100-1000x the background rate; explain methods for measuring biodiversity loss (species-area relationship, population viability analysis, IUCN Red List categories); evaluate rewilding case studies — Yellowstone wolf reintroduction triggering a trophic cascade that changed river courses; Iberian lynx recovery; describe minimum viable population theory and conservation triage; examine ethical debates in deciding which species to prioritise

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否描述狼群被重新引入后黄石国家公园发生的变化——即一种顶级捕食者的回归如何在整个生态系统中引发连锁反应，包括对河流产生的意外影响？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} describe what happened to Yellowstone National Park after wolves were reintroduced — what unexpected changes rippled through the whole ecosystem, including effects on rivers, as a result of one predator coming back?

description.zh: 解释分支系统学：生物根据共享的衍生特征分组，而不仅仅是相似性；如何利用分子数据（DNA序列比对）和分子钟构建系统发育树；解释为什么鸟类在技术上属于恐龙类群（冠部鸟跖类）；区分趋同进化（不相关的物种进化出相似特征）和平行进化；介绍水平基因转移以及为什么生命之树更准确地说是生命之网；解释为什么随着新数据的出现分类系统不断变化。
description.en: Explain cladistics: organisms are grouped by shared derived characters, not just similarity; how phylogenetic trees are built using molecular data (DNA sequence alignment) and the molecular clock; explain why birds are technically a group within dinosaurs (crown Avemetatarsalia); distinguish convergent evolution (unrelated species evolving similar traits) from parallel evolution; introduce horizontal gene transfer and why the tree of life is more accurately a web; explain why classification systems keep changing as new data emerge

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么生物学家现在认为鸟类就是恐龙的一类——不只是恐龙的后裔，而是真正属于恐龙演化支中的一员？这对我们理解科学家如何对动物进行分类有什么启示？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why biologists now say that birds ARE a type of dinosaur — not just their descendants but literally within the dinosaur family tree? What does that tell us about how scientists classify animals?

description.zh: 把恐龙的体型和孩子们熟悉的东西比一比——有些恐龙像房子一样高，有些像小鸡一样小——了解恐龙的体型有大有小，差别很大。
description.en: Compare dinosaur sizes to familiar things — some dinosaurs were as tall as a house, others were as small as a chicken — and understand that dinosaurs came in a huge range of sizes

evidence.zh: 能将大型恐龙的大小与公交车、房子等常见物体进行比较。
evidence.en: Compare the size of a large dinosaur to a familiar object like a bus or house

evidence.zh: 能说出一种大型恐龙（如腕龙）和一种小型恐龙（如美颌龙）。
evidence.en: Name a very large dinosaur (e.g. Brachiosaurus) and a small one (e.g. Compsognathus)

evidence.zh: 能运用“比……高”“比……长”“比……重”等词语进行比较。
evidence.en: Use words like 'taller than', 'longer than', 'heavier than' when comparing

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否说出有些恐龙非常巨大，而有些却非常小巧——也许会用“像楼房一样高”或“像猫一样小”这样的比较来描述？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} tell you that some dinosaurs were enormous and others were tiny — maybe using comparisons like 'as tall as a building' or 'as small as a cat'?

description.zh: 理解恐龙是真实存在过的动物，很久很久以前生活在地球上，现在已经灭绝了——今天没有一只活着。
description.en: Understand that dinosaurs were real animals that lived on Earth a very long time ago and are now extinct — none are alive today

evidence.zh: 能说出恐龙是真实存在的动物，而非虚构。
evidence.en: State that dinosaurs were real animals, not made up

evidence.zh: 能解释“灭绝”是指任何地方都不再有存活的个体。
evidence.en: Explain that 'extinct' means no living ones are left anywhere

evidence.zh: 能区分“很久以前”与“去年”等近期事件
evidence.en: Distinguish between 'a long time ago' and recent events like last year

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到恐龙玩具，能否说出真正的恐龙很久以前生活过，但现在已经灭绝了？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a dinosaur toy, can they tell you that real dinosaurs lived long ago but aren't alive any more?

description.zh: 认识并说出常见的著名恐龙种类：霸王龙、三角龙、剑龙和腕龙/梁龙，并描述每种恐龙的一个基本特征。
description.en: Recognise and name common well-known dinosaur species: Tyrannosaurus rex, Triceratops, Stegosaurus, and Brachiosaurus/Diplodocus, describing a basic feature of each

evidence.zh: 能借助图片或模型说出至少四种常见恐龙的名称。
evidence.en: Name at least four common dinosaur species from pictures or models

evidence.zh: 能说出每种恐龙的一个显著特征（如：霸王龙前肢短小，三角龙有三只角）。
evidence.en: Describe one visible feature of each (e.g. T. rex has tiny arms, Triceratops has three horns)

evidence.zh: 能独立将恐龙名称与图片或模型配对。
evidence.en: Match a dinosaur name to a picture or model without help

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到不同恐龙的图片，他们能说出至少三种恐龙的名字吗——比如霸王龙、三角龙和剑龙？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees pictures of different dinosaurs, can they name at least three — like T. rex, Triceratops, and Stegosaurus?

description.zh: 理解化石是保存在岩石中的古代生物遗骸，而被称为古生物学家的科学家通过研究化石来了解恐龙。
description.en: Understand that fossils are the remains of ancient living things preserved in rock, and that scientists called palaeontologists study fossils to learn about dinosaurs

evidence.zh: 将化石描述为保存在岩石中的生物遗骸
evidence.en: Describe a fossil as the remains of a living thing preserved in rock

evidence.zh: 能说出古生物学家的职责是研究化石。
evidence.en: Name the job of a palaeontologist as someone who studies fossils

evidence.zh: 识别化石的实例：岩石中的骨骼、牙齿、足迹。
evidence.en: Identify examples of fossils: bones, teeth, footprints in rock

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在海滩或博物馆发现了一块化石形状的石头，他们能解释什么是化石以及谁研究化石吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} found a fossil-shaped rock on a beach or at a museum, could they explain what a fossil is and who studies them?

description.zh: 通过观察牙齿形状等线索，将恐龙分为植食恐龙（吃植物的恐龙）和肉食恐龙（吃肉的恐龙）——平坦的牙齿用来吃植物，尖利的牙齿用来吃肉。
description.en: Sort dinosaurs into plant-eaters (herbivores) and meat-eaters (carnivores) by looking at clues like tooth shape — flat teeth for plants, sharp teeth for meat

evidence.zh: 能根据植食性、肉食性特征对恐龙图片或模型进行分类。
evidence.en: Sort a set of dinosaur pictures or models into herbivore and carnivore groups

evidence.zh: 说出尖锐牙齿用于撕咬肉类，扁平牙齿用于磨碎植物。
evidence.en: Explain that sharp pointed teeth are for tearing meat and flat teeth are for grinding plants

evidence.zh: 能分别举例说出一种植食性恐龙和一种肉食性恐龙。
evidence.en: Give an example of one herbivore and one carnivore dinosaur

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果给{{name}}看一张恐龙牙齿的图片，他们能推断出这只恐龙是植食性还是肉食性吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you showed {{name}} a picture of a dinosaur's teeth, could they guess whether it ate plants or meat?

name.zh: 真正的恐龙与虚构恐龙

description.zh: 区分真正的恐龙和虚构或容易混淆的生物——翼龙（会飞的爬行动物）和蛇颈龙（海洋爬行动物）不是恐龙，电影里的恐龙也不总是准确的。
description.en: Distinguish real dinosaurs from fictional or commonly confused creatures — pterosaurs (flying reptiles) and plesiosaurs (marine reptiles) were not dinosaurs, and movie dinosaurs are not always accurate

evidence.zh: 能说明翼龙会飞，但不属于恐龙。
evidence.en: State that pterosaurs could fly but were not dinosaurs

evidence.zh: 能说出蛇颈龙生活在海洋中，但不属于恐龙。
evidence.en: State that plesiosaurs lived in the sea but were not dinosaurs

evidence.zh: 能说出电影或卡通中的恐龙与真实恐龙的至少一处不同。
evidence.en: Identify at least one way a movie or cartoon dinosaur differs from the real animal

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在恐龙书里看到一种会飞的爬行动物，他们能不能告诉你，那其实不是恐龙，而是另一种史前动物？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a flying reptile in a dinosaur book, can they tell you it's actually not a dinosaur but a different kind of prehistoric animal?

description.zh: 了解不同的恐龙生活在不同的大陆上，世界各地的化石发现表明恐龙曾遍布全球，有些物种只出现在特定地区。
description.en: Understand that different dinosaurs lived on different continents and that fossil discoveries around the world show dinosaurs were a global phenomenon, with some species found only in certain regions

evidence.zh: 能说出恐龙化石已在包括南极洲在内的各大洲被发现。
evidence.en: State that dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent including Antarctica

evidence.zh: 能举例说明至少一处恐龙化石的发现地（如霸王龙发现于北美，迅猛龙发现于蒙古）。
evidence.en: Name at least one dinosaur discovery location (e.g. T. rex in North America, Velociraptor in Mongolia)

evidence.zh: 能解释同类恐龙为何会出现在如今相隔遥远的大陆上。
evidence.en: Suggest a reason why the same type of dinosaur is sometimes found on continents now far apart

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果给{{name}}看一张世界地图，他们能说出各大洲都发现过恐龙化石吗？也许还能说出某个著名恐龙的发现地点？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you showed {{name}} a world map, could they tell you that dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent — and maybe name a place where a famous dinosaur was discovered?

description.zh: 解释什么是粪化石（恐龙粪便形成的化石），以及古生物学家如何通过分析粪化石来了解恐龙吃什么，包括植物碎片、骨头和种子。
description.en: Describe what coprolites are (fossilised dinosaur dung) and how palaeontologists analyse them to discover what dinosaurs ate, including plant fragments, bones, and seeds

evidence.zh: 将粪化石定义为化石化的粪便（动物粪便保存为岩石）
evidence.en: Define a coprolite as fossilised dung (animal droppings preserved as rock)

evidence.zh: 解释科学家切割粪化石的原因——寻找其中的植物种子、骨骼碎片或鱼鳞。
evidence.en: Explain that scientists cut coprolites open to find plant seeds, bone fragments, or fish scales inside

evidence.zh: 能举例说明粪化石内容物如何揭示恐龙的食性。
evidence.en: State one example of what coprolite contents reveal about a dinosaur's diet

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}知道什么是粪化石吗？他们能不能一边咯咯笑，一边解释粪化石如何帮助科学家推断恐龙吃了什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know what a coprolite is? Can they explain — with a giggle — how fossilised poo helps scientists figure out what a dinosaur ate?

description.zh: 理解化石不仅告诉我们古代动物的信息，还能告诉我们古代环境的信息——例如，在山顶上发现的海洋化石表明该地区曾经在水下。
description.en: Understand that fossils tell us not only about ancient animals but also about ancient environments — for example, marine fossils found on a mountaintop show that area was once underwater

evidence.zh: 能举例说明化石反映的过去环境与现在不同。
evidence.en: Give an example of a fossil that reveals a past environment different from today's

evidence.zh: 能解释在内陆发现海洋化石说明该地区曾被海洋覆盖。
evidence.en: Explain that finding marine fossils inland means that area was once covered by sea

evidence.zh: 能说出植物化石可以指示一个地区曾是森林、沙漠还是沼泽。
evidence.en: State that plant fossils can show whether an area was once a forest, desert, or swamp

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}听说山上发现了贝壳化石，他们能解释这说明该地区过去是什么样的吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} heard that seashell fossils were found on a mountain, could they explain what that tells us about what the area used to be like?

description.zh: 用简单的话解释化石是怎么形成的：生物死后很快被泥沙埋起来；经过几百万年，矿物质替换了生物遗体，泥沙变成岩石，把形状保留下来。
description.en: Explain in simple terms how fossils form: an organism dies and is quickly buried in sediment; over millions of years minerals replace the remains and the sediment turns to rock, preserving the shape

evidence.zh: 描述基本顺序：生物死亡、被沉积物掩埋、矿物质随时间置换遗骸。
evidence.en: Describe the basic sequence: organism dies, buried in sediment, minerals replace remains over time

evidence.zh: 解释化石记录稀少的原因——多数生物在未被掩埋前即已分解。
evidence.en: Explain why fossilisation is rare — most organisms decompose before being buried

evidence.zh: 能在解释中正确使用“沉积物”“矿物”和“岩石”三个术语。
evidence.en: Use the words 'sediment', 'minerals', and 'rock' correctly when explaining

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在学校用盐面团做了一个化石模型，他们能解释真正的化石是如何在地下历经数百万年形成的吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} made a salt-dough fossil at school, could they explain how real fossils form underground over millions of years?

description.zh: 了解玛丽·安宁是谁——一位来自英国莱姆里吉斯的先驱化石猎人，她在19世纪初发现了鱼龙和蛇颈龙的骨架，为我们理解史前生命做出了贡献。
description.en: Know who Mary Anning was — a pioneering fossil hunter from Lyme Regis, England, who discovered ichthyosaur and plesiosaur skeletons in the early 1800s and contributed to our understanding of prehistoric life

evidence.zh: 能说出玛丽·安宁生活在19世纪初的英格兰，并在海岸边寻找化石。
evidence.en: State that Mary Anning lived in England in the early 1800s and hunted for fossils along the coast

evidence.zh: 至少说出她的一项主要发现（鱼龙或蛇颈龙）
evidence.en: Name at least one of her major discoveries (ichthyosaur or plesiosaur)

evidence.zh: 解释其工作的重要性——她帮助科学家认识到灭绝生物曾在地球上生存。
evidence.en: Explain why her work was important — she helped scientists understand that extinct creatures once lived on Earth

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}听说过玛丽·安宁吗？他们能说出她是谁，以及她对化石研究的重要性吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: Has {{name}} heard of Mary Anning? Can they tell you who she was and why she was important to the study of fossils?

description.zh: 利用恐龙足迹（脚印化石）来推断恐龙的大小、速度和行为——脚印间距大表示奔跑，间距小表示行走。
description.en: Use dinosaur trackways (fossilised footprints) to make inferences about a dinosaur's size, speed, and behaviour — widely spaced prints suggest running, closely spaced suggest walking

evidence.zh: 能说出脚印越大通常意味着恐龙体型越大。
evidence.en: Explain that larger footprints generally mean a larger dinosaur

evidence.zh: 通过比较脚印间距判断是走还是跑
evidence.en: Compare spacing between prints to infer walking versus running

evidence.zh: 推断一组平行足迹的可能含义（如恐龙成群行进）
evidence.en: Suggest what a set of parallel trackways might mean (e.g. dinosaurs travelling in a group)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在博物馆看到一排恐龙脚印，他们能根据脚印之间的间距判断出那只恐龙是在走路还是在奔跑吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} saw a line of dinosaur footprints at a museum, could they figure out whether the dinosaur was walking or running based on how far apart the prints are?

description.zh: 按顺序排列中生代的三个时期——三叠纪、侏罗纪和白垩纪，并理解不同的恐龙生活在不同的时期，而不是同时存在
description.en: Place the three periods of the Mesozoic Era — Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous — in order and understand that different dinosaurs lived in different periods, not all at the same time

evidence.zh: 能按正确时间顺序排列三叠纪、侏罗纪和白垩纪。
evidence.en: List Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous in the correct chronological order

evidence.zh: 至少能正确说出一种著名恐龙所处的地质时期。
evidence.en: Assign at least one well-known dinosaur to the correct period

evidence.zh: 能说出这些时期相隔数百万年，且不同时期生存着不同物种。
evidence.en: Explain that millions of years separated these periods and different species lived in each

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否知道霸王龙和剑龙实际上并非生活在同一时期——并且他们能否按顺序说出三个恐龙时代？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know that T. rex and Stegosaurus didn't actually live at the same time — and can they name the three dinosaur time periods in order?

description.zh: 区分遗体化石（保存下来的骨骼、牙齿、贝壳）和遗迹化石（脚印、行迹、蛋、洞穴、粪化石），并解释每种类型能告诉科学家什么信息。
description.en: Distinguish body fossils (preserved bones, teeth, shells) from trace fossils (footprints, trackways, eggs, burrows, coprolites) and explain what each type can tell scientists

evidence.zh: 能将实例归为遗体化石（骨骼、牙齿、贝壳）和遗迹化石（足迹、蛋、粪便）两类。
evidence.en: Sort examples into body fossils (bones, teeth, shells) and trace fossils (footprints, eggs, dung)

evidence.zh: 能说出实体化石能反映动物的外形特征。
evidence.en: Explain that body fossils show what an animal looked like physically

evidence.zh: 解释遗迹化石如何反映动物的行为——如何移动、吃什么、在哪里筑巢
evidence.en: Explain that trace fossils show how an animal behaved — how it moved, what it ate, where it nested

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在博物馆的岩石上看到一个恐龙足迹，他们能否解释它和化石骨骼有什么不同，以及科学家能从中了解到什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} saw a dinosaur footprint in rock at a museum, could they explain how it's different from a fossil bone and what scientists can learn from it?

description.zh: 分析和解读化石中的数据，为很久以前存在的生物和环境提供证据
description.en: Analyse and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of organisms and environments that existed long ago

evidence.zh: 能说明化石是远古生物遗留下来的、保存完好的遗体或遗迹。
evidence.en: Explain that fossils are preserved remains or traces of organisms that lived long ago

evidence.zh: 运用化石证据推断古生物及其生存环境
evidence.en: Use fossil evidence to make inferences about past organisms and their environments

evidence.zh: 描述化石与现存生物的比较如何帮助我们理解生命演化。
evidence.en: Describe how comparing fossils with living organisms helps us understand how life has changed

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}在山坡的岩石中发现了鱼类化石，他们能否解释这表明该地区在数百万年前必定曾位于水下？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees a fossil of a fish in a rock on a hillside, can they explain that the area must have been underwater millions of years ago?
