description.zh: 观察并描述月亮在大约一个月内形状的变化，认识到月亮会经历一个重复的月相周期，从新月（看不见）到满月（完整的圆形）再回到新月。
description.en: Observe and describe the Moon's changing shape over about a month, recognising that it goes through a repeating cycle of phases from new moon (invisible) to full moon (complete circle) and back again

evidence.zh: 描述月相在一个月周期内的变化。
evidence.en: Describe that the Moon appears to change shape over about a month

evidence.zh: 能说出或画出至少三个月相：新月（暗）、半月和满月。
evidence.en: Name or draw at least three phases: new moon (dark), half moon, and full moon

evidence.zh: 能说出规律具有重复性——月相变化周而复始。
evidence.en: State that the pattern repeats — the Moon goes through the same shapes again and again

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果你让{{name}}连续几个晚上观察月亮，他们能注意到月亮形状的变化并描述出这个规律吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you asked {{name}} to look at the Moon several nights in a row, could they notice that it changes shape and describe the pattern?

description.zh: 知道除了地球以外还有其他行星，围绕太阳运行的行星群体被称为太阳系——太空是地球天空之外的广阔区域。
description.en: Know that there are other planets besides Earth and that our group of planets orbiting the Sun is called the solar system — and that space is the vast area beyond Earth's sky

evidence.zh: 能说出地球是一颗行星，并知道还有其他行星。
evidence.en: State that Earth is a planet and there are other planets too

evidence.zh: 能使用“太阳系”这一术语描述太阳及其轨道上的行星。
evidence.en: Use the term 'solar system' to describe the Sun and the planets that orbit it

evidence.zh: 解释太空是地球大气层以外的区域，行星和恒星存在于其中。
evidence.en: Explain that space is the area beyond the Earth's sky, where the planets and stars are

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否知道地球是围绕太阳运行的几颗行星之一，并且这一群体被称为太阳系？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know that Earth is one of several planets that go around the Sun, and that this group is called the solar system?

description.zh: 在夜空中认出一些星星的图案（星座），从北斗七星开始，并知道可以用北斗七星找到北极星。
description.en: Recognise a few star patterns (constellations) in the night sky, starting with the Big Dipper (the Plough), and understand that the North Star (Polaris) can be found using the Big Dipper

evidence.zh: 识别或绘制北斗七星图案
evidence.en: Identify or draw the Big Dipper (the Plough) as a pattern of seven stars

evidence.zh: 能指出北斗七星斗口两颗指极星指向北极星。
evidence.en: Explain that the two end stars of the Big Dipper's bowl point towards the North Star

evidence.zh: 能说出星座是人们为恒星排列模式所起的命名。
evidence.en: State that constellations are patterns of stars that people have named

assessmentPrompt.zh: 在一个晴朗的夜晚，{{name}}能否在天空中辨认出北斗七星——或者凭记忆画出它的形状？
assessmentPrompt.en: On a clear night, could {{name}} find the Big Dipper in the sky — or draw its shape from memory?

description.zh: 能识别天空中的太阳、月亮和星星，并描述它们的基本区别：太阳在白天提供光和热，星星在夜晚是小小的光点，月亮在白天和夜晚都可能出现在天空中。
description.en: Identify the Sun, Moon, and stars as objects in the sky and describe basic differences: the Sun gives light and heat during the day, stars are tiny points of light at night, and the Moon can appear in both the day and night sky

evidence.zh: 说出天空中太阳、月亮和星星的名称
evidence.en: Name the Sun, Moon, and stars as objects in the sky

evidence.zh: 能说出太阳在白天出现，并给我们带来光和热。
evidence.en: State that the Sun appears during the day and gives us light and heat

evidence.zh: 能说出星星在夜晚可见，月亮有时白天也能看到。
evidence.en: State that stars appear at night and the Moon can sometimes be seen during the day too

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否指出太阳、月亮和星星，并简单说出它们各自的特点——比如太阳给我们带来光和热？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} point out the Sun, Moon, and stars and tell you something simple about each one — like that the Sun gives us light and heat?

description.zh: 知道宇航员是乘坐火箭去太空的人，人类已经登上过月球（阿波罗任务），现在的宇航员在国际空间站上生活和工作。
description.en: Know that astronauts are people who travel to space in rockets, that humans have walked on the Moon (Apollo missions), and that astronauts today live and work on the International Space Station

evidence.zh: 将宇航员定义为太空旅行者
evidence.en: Define an astronaut as a person who travels to space

evidence.zh: 能说出人类在阿波罗任务期间登上了月球
evidence.en: State that humans landed on the Moon during the Apollo missions

evidence.zh: 能说出国际空间站是宇航员在地球轨道上生活和工作的地方。
evidence.en: Describe the International Space Station as a place where astronauts live and work in orbit around Earth

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否说出宇航员是什么，并知道人类确实已在月球上行走，且生活在空间站里？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} tell you what an astronaut is, and that people have actually walked on the Moon and live on a space station?

description.zh: 认识太阳系中除行星以外的其他天体：小行星（岩石天体，大多位于火星和木星之间）、彗星（冰质天体，靠近太阳时会出现尾巴）以及流星体/流星/陨石（进入地球大气层的太空岩石）
description.en: Identify other objects in the solar system beyond planets: asteroids (rocky bodies mostly between Mars and Jupiter), comets (icy bodies with tails when near the Sun), and meteoroids/meteors/meteorites (space rocks that enter Earth’s atmosphere)

evidence.zh: 描述小行星是主要分布在火星与木星之间小行星带中的岩石天体。
evidence.en: Describe asteroids as rocky bodies mostly found in the belt between Mars and Jupiter

evidence.zh: 能将彗星描述为接近太阳时形成发光尾巴的冰质天体
evidence.en: Describe comets as icy bodies that develop a glowing tail when they approach the Sun

evidence.zh: 解释流星体（太空中的）、流星（大气层中的光迹）和陨石（落到地球上的）之间的区别
evidence.en: Explain the difference between a meteoroid (in space), meteor (streak of light in atmosphere), and meteorite (lands on Earth)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到一颗流星，他们能否解释这其实是一小块太空岩石在地球大气层中燃烧，并告诉你它和彗星的区别？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} saw a shooting star, could they explain that it’s actually a tiny space rock burning up in our atmosphere — and tell you the difference between that and a comet?

description.zh: 了解地球有两种运动方式：它绕地轴自转，每24小时转一圈，形成白天和黑夜；它绕太阳公转，每365天转一圈，也就是一年。
description.en: Understand that Earth moves in two ways: it rotates (spins) on its axis once every 24 hours causing day and night, and it orbits (travels around) the Sun once every 365 days, which is one year

evidence.zh: 借助地球仪或球体演示：地球自转导致向阳面为白昼，背阳面为黑夜。
evidence.en: Demonstrate with a globe or ball that Earth's rotation causes day on the Sun-facing side and night on the opposite side

evidence.zh: 能说出地球自转一周约需24小时（一天）。
evidence.en: State that one full rotation takes about 24 hours (one day)

evidence.zh: 能说出地球公转周期约为365天（即一年）。
evidence.en: State that one full orbit around the Sun takes about 365 days (one year)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释：我们有白天和黑夜是因为地球自转，而一年是地球绕太阳公转一圈所需的时间？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain that we have day and night because the Earth spins, and that a year is the time it takes Earth to go all the way around the Sun?

description.zh: 知道望远镜是帮助我们观察太空中遥远物体的仪器，而像哈勃和詹姆斯·韦伯这样的太空望远镜在地球大气层上方运行，以获得更清晰的宇宙视图。
description.en: Know that telescopes are instruments that help us see distant objects in space, and that space telescopes like Hubble and James Webb orbit above Earth’s atmosphere to get clearer views of the universe

evidence.zh: 能说出望远镜能放大远处物体，帮助我们看清更多细节。
evidence.en: Explain that a telescope magnifies distant objects so we can see them in more detail

evidence.zh: 能说出地球大气层会模糊视野，因此太空望远镜能获得更清晰的图像。
evidence.en: State that Earth's atmosphere blurs the view, so space telescopes get clearer pictures

evidence.zh: 能说出至少一台太空望远镜（哈勃或詹姆斯·韦布）并描述其功能。
evidence.en: Name at least one space telescope (Hubble or James Webb) and describe what it does

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否理解望远镜的功能，以及为什么有些望远镜会被送入太空——例如哈勃或詹姆斯·韦布望远镜？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know what a telescope does and why some telescopes are sent into space — like the Hubble or James Webb telescopes?

description.zh: 描述每颗行星的一个主要特征：水星最小且离太阳最近，金星最热，火星因生锈而呈红色，木星最大且有巨大的红斑，土星有光环，天王星侧躺着自转，海王星最远且非常寒冷。
description.en: Describe a key feature of each planet: Mercury is smallest and closest, Venus is the hottest, Mars is red with rust, Jupiter is the largest with a Great Red Spot, Saturn has rings, Uranus tilts on its side, Neptune is the farthest and very cold

evidence.zh: 能说出八大行星中至少六颗的任一显著特征
evidence.en: State one distinctive feature for at least six of the eight planets

evidence.zh: 能比较至少两颗行星的特征（如木星比地球大得多，金星比水星更热）
evidence.en: Compare at least two planets (e.g. Jupiter is much bigger than Earth, Venus is hotter than Mercury)

evidence.zh: 解释火星呈红色的原因（其岩石中的氧化铁/铁锈）
evidence.en: Explain why Mars appears red (iron oxide/rust in its rocks)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果让你说出一颗行星，{{name}}能讲出关于它的一条有趣事实吗——比如土星环或木星大红斑？
assessmentPrompt.en: If you named a planet, could {{name}} tell you one interesting fact about it — like Saturn's rings or Jupiter's Great Red Spot?

description.zh: 描述机器人和漫游车如何探索人类难以到达的地方——像好奇号和毅力号这样的火星漫游车在火星上行驶，拍摄照片、采集岩石样本，并寻找过去存在水的迹象。
description.en: Describe how robots and rovers have explored places humans cannot easily go — Mars rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance drive across Mars taking photos, collecting rock samples, and searching for signs of past water

evidence.zh: 能说出至少一辆火星车（好奇号或毅力号），并说明其在火星表面行驶。
evidence.en: Name at least one Mars rover (Curiosity or Perseverance) and state it drives on Mars's surface

evidence.zh: 解释巡视器如何拍摄图像、分析岩石并寻找水存在的证据。
evidence.en: Explain that rovers take photos, analyse rocks, and look for evidence of water

evidence.zh: 能说出用机器人代替人类前往火星的原因：火星距离极其遥远，且没有可供呼吸的空气。
evidence.en: State why we send robots instead of people: Mars is very far away and has no breathable air

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}了解火星车吗？他们能说出“好奇号”或“毅力号”在火星上做什么吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know about the Mars rovers? Can they tell you what Curiosity or Perseverance does on Mars?

description.zh: 按离太阳从近到远的顺序说出八大行星（水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星），知道冥王星是矮行星，并能区分岩石质的类地行星和气体巨行星
description.en: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), know that Pluto is a dwarf planet, and distinguish rocky inner planets from gas giant outer planets

evidence.zh: 能按离太阳由近及远的顺序说出八大行星。
evidence.en: List all eight planets in order from the Sun

evidence.zh: 能说出冥王星于2006年被重新归类为矮行星。
evidence.en: State that Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006

evidence.zh: 描述内行星的四颗行星体积小、由岩石构成，而外行星的四颗行星则是巨大的气态巨行星。
evidence.en: Explain that the four inner planets are small and rocky while the four outer planets are large gas giants

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否按离太阳从近到远的顺序列出八大行星——也许可以借助“水金地火木土天海”这类记忆口诀？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} list all eight planets in order from the Sun — maybe using a memory trick like 'My Very Eager Mother Just Served Us Nachos'?

description.zh: 知道月球大约每个月绕地球一圈，它自己不发光，而是反射太阳光，我们看到的月相变化是因为从地球上能看到月球被太阳照亮部分的大小不同。
description.en: Know that the Moon orbits Earth approximately once a month, that it does not make its own light but reflects sunlight, and that its changing appearance (phases) is caused by how much of the sunlit side we can see from Earth

evidence.zh: 能说出月球绕地球公转一周大约需要28-30天。
evidence.en: State that the Moon orbits Earth roughly once every 28-30 days

evidence.zh: 能说出月球本身不发光，是反射太阳光。
evidence.en: Explain that the Moon reflects sunlight rather than producing its own light

evidence.zh: 描述月相成因：月球绕地球公转过程中，地球上观测到的月球被照亮部分的比例发生变化。
evidence.en: Describe how Moon phases happen: we see different amounts of the lit-up side as the Moon orbits Earth

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么月亮看起来会改变形状——即它始终是圆的，我们只是看到了被太阳照亮的那部分？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why the Moon seems to change shape — that it’s always round but we only see the part lit up by the Sun?

description.zh: 知道太阳是一颗恒星——离地球最近的恒星——并且它位于太阳系的中心，所有八颗行星都围绕它运行。
description.en: Know that the Sun is a star — the closest star to Earth — and that it is at the centre of our solar system, with all eight planets orbiting around it

evidence.zh: 说明太阳是一颗恒星，而非特殊类型的天体。
evidence.en: State that the Sun is a star, not a unique type of object

evidence.zh: 能解释太阳看起来比其他恒星更大更亮，是因为它离地球近得多。
evidence.en: Explain that the Sun appears bigger and brighter than other stars because it is much closer

evidence.zh: 将太阳系描述为以太阳为中心、行星围绕其运行的系统。
evidence.en: Describe the solar system as the Sun at the centre with planets orbiting around it

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否知道太阳实际上是一颗恒星——只是离我们非常近——并且行星都围绕它公转？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know that the Sun is actually a star — just a very close one — and that the planets go around it?

description.zh: 了解人们对太阳系的看法是如何随时间改变的：古代人认为地球在中心（地心说，托勒密），直到哥白尼提出太阳在中心（日心说），后来由伽利略的望远镜观测所证实。
description.en: Understand that ideas about the solar system changed over time: ancient people believed Earth was at the centre (geocentric model, Ptolemy), until Copernicus proposed the Sun was at the centre (heliocentric model), later confirmed by Galileo’s telescope observations

evidence.zh: 描述地心模型（地球位于中心），并指出托勒密为其主要倡导者。
evidence.en: Describe the geocentric model (Earth at the centre) and name Ptolemy as its main proponent

evidence.zh: 描述日心模型（太阳位于中心），并指出哥白尼是其提出者。
evidence.en: Describe the heliocentric model (Sun at the centre) and name Copernicus as the person who proposed it

evidence.zh: 解释伽利略如何借助望远镜发现支持日心说的证据（如木星的卫星）。
evidence.en: Explain that Galileo used a telescope to find evidence supporting the heliocentric model (e.g. moons orbiting Jupiter)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否说出人们过去认为太阳绕着地球转，并解释像哥白尼和伽利略这样的科学家是如何改变我们的认识的？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} tell you that people used to think the Sun went around the Earth, and explain how scientists like Copernicus and Galileo changed our understanding?

description.zh: 理解重力是一种将物体拉向地心的力，无论你站在球体上的哪个位置，“下”都指向地心，并且重力使月球绕地球运行、行星绕太阳运行。
description.en: Understand gravity as a force that pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth, that 'down' means towards Earth’s centre regardless of where you stand on the sphere, and that gravity keeps the Moon orbiting Earth and planets orbiting the Sun

evidence.zh: 将重力定义为物体受到地球吸引而指向地心的力
evidence.en: Define gravity as a pulling force that attracts objects towards the centre of the Earth

evidence.zh: 能解释“向下”即指向地心，因此地球两端的人均感觉自己被拉向“下方”。
evidence.en: Explain that 'down' points towards Earth's centre, so people on opposite sides of the globe both feel pulled 'down'

evidence.zh: 能说出重力使月球绕地球运动、行星绕太阳运动。
evidence.en: State that gravity keeps the Moon orbiting Earth and planets orbiting the Sun

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么物体会“向下”落，以及引力同样是使月球绕地球运行的力？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why things fall 'down' and that gravity is the same force keeping the Moon going around the Earth?

description.zh: 了解恒星生命周期的基本知识：恒星诞生于气体和尘埃云（星云）中，通过核聚变将氢转化为氦，发光数百万或数十亿年，最终死亡——大质量恒星爆炸成为超新星，而较小的恒星则逐渐冷却变成白矮星。
description.en: Understand the basics of a star’s life cycle: stars are born in clouds of gas and dust (nebulae), shine for millions or billions of years by fusing hydrogen, and eventually die — massive stars explode as supernovae while smaller stars fade into white dwarfs

evidence.zh: 描述恒星如何由称为星云的气体和尘埃云形成。
evidence.en: Describe that stars form from clouds of gas and dust called nebulae

evidence.zh: 描述恒星核心通过氢聚变为氦释放能量的过程。
evidence.en: State that stars produce energy by fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores

evidence.zh: 解释大质量恒星以超新星爆发终结，而较小恒星则坍缩为白矮星。
evidence.en: Explain that massive stars end in a supernova explosion while smaller stars shrink to become white dwarfs

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释恒星会诞生、存活极长时间并最终消亡——而且超大质量恒星在生命末期会发生爆炸？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain that stars are born, live for a very long time, and eventually die — and that really big stars can explode at the end?

description.zh: 使用比例模型、示意图或计算来表示太阳系中天体的相对大小和距离，理解行星之间的距离比行星本身大得多。
description.en: Use scale models, diagrams, or calculations to represent the relative sizes and distances of objects in the solar system, understanding that the distances between planets are enormously larger than the planets themselves

evidence.zh: 举例说明：若太阳为沙滩球大小，则地球仅有豌豆大小，两者相距约26米。
evidence.en: Explain that if the Sun were the size of a beach ball, Earth would be a pea about 26 metres away

evidence.zh: 能说出行星间距离远大于行星自身尺寸。
evidence.en: State that the distances between planets are much greater than the sizes of the planets themselves

evidence.zh: 能构建或解读同时体现相对大小与距离的比例模型。
evidence.en: Create or interpret a scale model showing both relative sizes and distances

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否曾制作或观察过太阳系的等比例模型？他们能否解释为什么行星之间要保持正确的距离，就需要分布在整个操场上？
assessmentPrompt.en: Has {{name}} ever built or looked at a scale model of the solar system? Can they explain why the planets would need to be spread across a whole playing field to be the right distance apart?

description.zh: 认识不同季节可见的命名星座，并理解为什么一年中不同时间看到的星座不同——因为地球绕太阳公转，改变了我们夜晚面向天空的方向。
description.en: Recognise named constellations visible in different seasons and understand why we see different constellations at different times of year — because Earth’s orbit around the Sun changes which part of the sky we face at night

evidence.zh: 能说出至少三个星座的名称（如猎户座、大熊座/北斗七星、狮子座、仙后座）。
evidence.en: Name at least three constellations (e.g. Orion, Ursa Major/Big Dipper, Leo, Cassiopeia)

evidence.zh: 说出不同季节可见的星座不同。
evidence.en: State that different constellations are visible in different seasons

evidence.zh: 能解释该现象的原因：地球公转轨道使我们在一年中不同时期朝向宇宙的不同方向。
evidence.en: Explain that this happens because Earth's orbit means we face different directions in space at different times of year

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否知道冬季和夏季可见的星座不同，并能解释其原因？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} know that you can see different constellations in winter than in summer, and can they explain why?

description.zh: 描述人类太空探索的关键里程碑：太空竞赛（斯普特尼克号、尤里·加加林、阿波罗11号登月）、航天飞机时代、国际空间站以及当前任务（阿尔忒弥斯计划、火星探索计划、商业太空飞行）
description.en: Describe key milestones in human space exploration: the Space Race (Sputnik, Yuri Gagarin, Apollo 11 Moon landing), the Space Shuttle era, the International Space Station, and current missions (Artemis programme, Mars exploration plans, commercial spaceflight)

evidence.zh: 能说出斯普特尼克号是第一颗人造卫星（1957年），加加林是第一位进入太空的人（1961年）。
evidence.en: Name Sputnik as the first satellite (1957) and Yuri Gagarin as the first person in space (1961)

evidence.zh: 描述1969年阿波罗11号登月及尼尔·阿姆斯特朗和巴兹·奥尔德林。
evidence.en: Describe the Apollo 11 Moon landing (1969) with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin

evidence.zh: 能列举至少一个当前太空计划（如阿尔忒弥斯计划、SpaceX、国际空间站），并说明其目标。
evidence.en: Name at least one current space programme (Artemis, SpaceX, ISS) and describe its goal

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能不能给你讲讲太空探索的历史——从第一颗人造卫星到登月，再到现在的进展？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} tell you about the history of space exploration — from the first satellite to the Moon landing to what’s happening now?

description.zh: 用层层嵌套的方式描述宇宙的尺度：地球是太阳系中的一颗行星，太阳是银河系中数十亿颗恒星中的一颗，而银河系又是宇宙中数十亿个星系中的一个。
description.en: Describe the scale of the universe in nested layers: Earth is one planet in our solar system, the Sun is one star among billions in the Milky Way galaxy, and the Milky Way is one galaxy among billions in the universe

evidence.zh: 能说出银河系是我们的星系，包含数十亿颗恒星。
evidence.en: State that the Milky Way is our galaxy and it contains billions of stars

evidence.zh: 解释层级关系：行星→太阳系→星系→宇宙
evidence.en: Explain the hierarchy: planet → solar system → galaxy → universe

evidence.zh: 能通过类比说明宇宙尺度（如：若太阳是足球，地球则是26米外的一粒胡椒）。
evidence.en: Use a comparison to convey cosmic scale (e.g. if the Sun were a football, Earth would be a peppercorn 26 metres away)

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否描述我们在宇宙中的位置是如何运作的——即我们身处一个星系中太阳系里的一颗行星上，而这样的星系有数十亿个？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} describe how our place in the universe works — that we’re on a planet in a solar system in a galaxy among billions of galaxies?

name.zh: 为什么太阳看起来最亮

description.zh: 解释为什么太阳看起来比其他恒星亮得多：它是离地球最近的恒星，而不是宇宙中最大或最亮的恒星——理解视觉亮度（看起来有多亮）和实际亮度之间的区别。
description.en: Explain why the Sun appears much brighter than other stars: it is the nearest star to Earth, not the biggest or brightest star in the universe — understanding the difference between apparent brightness (how bright something looks) and actual brightness

evidence.zh: 能说出太阳是一颗中等大小的恒星，看起来最亮是因为它是离地球最近的恒星。
evidence.en: State that the Sun is a medium-sized star that appears brightest because it is the closest star to Earth

evidence.zh: 解释视亮度（看起来有多亮）与实际亮度（发出多少光）的区别
evidence.en: Explain the difference between apparent brightness (how bright it looks) and actual brightness (how much light it gives off)

evidence.zh: 举例说明：近处的手电筒看起来比远处的泛光灯更亮，尽管泛光灯的功率更大。
evidence.en: Give an example: a torch held close looks brighter than a distant floodlight, even though the floodlight is more powerful

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否理解太阳看起来这么亮是因为它离我们近，而不是因为它是最大的恒星——并且有些遥远的恒星实际上要大得多？
assessmentPrompt.en: Does {{name}} understand that the Sun looks so bright because it’s close, not because it’s the biggest star — and that some faraway stars are actually much larger?

description.zh: 描述天文学家如何利用凌星测光法（行星经过恒星前方时星光出现的微弱下降）和径向速度法（恒星的 Doppler 摆动）来探测其他恒星周围的行星，解释宜居带的概念，并讨论大气生物特征——例如同时探测到氧气、甲烷和水蒸气——对行星意味着什么。
description.en: Describe how astronomers detect planets around other stars using transit photometry (dip in starlight as a planet crosses) and radial velocity (Doppler wobble of the star), explain the habitable zone concept, and discuss what atmospheric biosignatures — such as oxygen, methane, and water vapour detected together — would suggest about a planet

evidence.zh: 掌握凌星法：行星从恒星前方经过时，恒星亮度会出现微小且周期性的下降。
evidence.en: Explains transit photometry: the small, periodic dip in a star's brightness when a planet passes in front of it

evidence.zh: 将宜居带解释为恒星周围允许行星表面存在液态水的距离范围
evidence.en: Explains the habitable zone as the range of distances from a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface

evidence.zh: 描述至少两种大气生物标志物，并解释其同时存在的重要意义（如氧气与甲烷共存，表明有活跃生命持续补充二者）。
evidence.en: Describes two or more atmospheric biosignatures and explains why their co-presence is significant (e.g. oxygen + methane together suggests active life replenishing both)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}听说在附近恒星的宜居带中发现了一颗地球大小的行星，他们能否解释天文学家是如何探测到它的、宜居带意味着什么，以及他们会在大气中寻找哪些特征来判断那里是否可能存在生命？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} heard that a planet the size of Earth had been found in the habitable zone of a nearby star, could they explain how astronomers detected it, what the habitable zone means, and what they'd look for in its atmosphere to decide if life might exist there?

description.zh: 解释电磁波谱如何成为现代天文学的主要工具——不同波长（无线电波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X射线、伽马射线）揭示不同的现象，为什么有些望远镜必须放在太空，以及每个波长范围带来了哪些具体发现（例如微波中的宇宙微波背景辐射、X射线中的黑洞喷流、无线电波中的冷气体云）。
description.en: Explain how the electromagnetic spectrum is the primary tool of modern astronomy — different wavelengths (radio, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma-ray) reveal different phenomena, why some telescopes must be in space, and what specific discoveries each wavelength range has enabled (e.g. CMB in microwave, black hole jets in X-ray, cold gas clouds in radio)

evidence.zh: 能列举电磁波谱中至少四个波段，并各举一个天文观测实例。
evidence.en: Lists at least four regions of the EM spectrum and gives a specific astronomical object or phenomenon observed in each

evidence.zh: 解释为何某些望远镜必须置于太空（地球大气层会吸收X射线、伽马射线及大部分红外辐射）。
evidence.en: Explains why some telescopes must be placed in space (Earth's atmosphere blocks X-ray, gamma-ray, and much infrared radiation)

evidence.zh: 描述詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜或哈勃望远镜，并解释各自主要观测的波谱范围及其选择原因。
evidence.en: Describes the James Webb Space Telescope or Hubble and explains which part of the spectrum each primarily observes and why that was chosen

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果告诉{{name}}我们用肉眼看不到宇宙的大部分，他们能否解释原因——并描述两种探测可见光以外信号的望远镜，说出它们帮助我们发现了什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was told that we can't see most of the universe with our eyes, could they explain why — and describe two types of telescope that detect something other than visible light, naming what they've helped us discover?

description.zh: 运用牛顿定律解释轨道运动：为什么轨道是持续向侧方下落而不是漂浮；引力助推（弹弓机动）如何将行星的动量传递给航天器；以及为什么火箭需要达到特定速度才能进入轨道——用概念性（而非代数）的方式讲解齐奥尔科夫斯基火箭方程
description.en: Apply Newton's laws to explain orbital motion: why orbit is continuously falling sideways rather than floating; how a gravity assist (slingshot manoeuvre) transfers momentum from a planet to a spacecraft; and why rockets need to reach a specific speed to enter orbit — with a conceptual (not algebraic) treatment of the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation

evidence.zh: 解释轨道为持续自由落体：航天器不断落向地球，但因水平速度极快而始终“错过”地球。
evidence.en: Explains that orbit is a state of continuous freefall — the spacecraft is falling towards Earth but moving so fast horizontally that it keeps missing

evidence.zh: 描述引力弹弓效应的工作原理：航天器飞掠行星时，通过“借用”行星的轨道动量来获得加速。
evidence.en: Describes how a gravity assist works: a spacecraft flying past a planet gains speed by 'borrowing' from the planet's orbital momentum

evidence.zh: 解释火箭方程的核心结论：所需Δv越大，燃料与航天器最终质量之比呈指数增长，这解释了为什么大型火箭大部分都是燃料。
evidence.en: Explains the key insight of the rocket equation: the ratio of fuel to final spacecraft mass grows exponentially with required Δv, explaining why large rockets are mostly fuel

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果问{{name}}：为什么国际空间站里的宇航员明明离地球还很近、引力也没有消失，却会飘起来？他们能否解释宇航员其实处于自由落体状态，并从物理学角度说明“在轨道上运行”到底意味着什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was asked why astronauts in the ISS float even though they're still close to Earth and gravity hasn't disappeared, could they explain that they're actually in freefall and describe what 'being in orbit' really means physically?

description.zh: 解释恒星核合成：宇宙大爆炸主要产生了氢和氦；主序星内部的核聚变反应能合成直到铁的元素；而比铁更重的元素则需要在超新星爆发中产生，并被抛洒到太空中——这意味着我们身体里的原子，都是在远古恒星中锻造出来的。
description.en: Explain stellar nucleosynthesis: the Big Bang produced mainly hydrogen and helium; main-sequence fusion builds elements up to iron; and supernovae produce elements heavier than iron and scatter them into space — meaning the atoms in our bodies were forged in ancient stars

evidence.zh: 能说出大爆炸主要产生了氢和氦，所有更重的元素都是后来在恒星中形成的。
evidence.en: States that the Big Bang produced primarily hydrogen and helium, and that all heavier elements were made later in stars

evidence.zh: 能说明主序星内部的核聚变过程：氢核聚变为氦，并可继续聚变生成更重元素直至铁。
evidence.en: Explains that nuclear fusion in main-sequence stars converts hydrogen to helium and can continue building heavier elements up to iron

evidence.zh: 解释比铁重的元素为何需通过超新星爆发形成，并描述超新星如何将这些元素散布至星际空间，成为新恒星、行星及生命的原材料。
evidence.en: Explains why elements heavier than iron require supernova explosions to form, and describes how supernovae distribute these elements into interstellar space where they become the raw material for new stars, planets, and life

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果告诉{{name}}，他们骨骼中的钙和血液中的铁是在数十亿年前爆炸的古老恒星内部形成的，他们能否解释从大爆炸到这些原子形成，再到它们最终如何来到地球的这一系列事件？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was told that the calcium in their bones and the iron in their blood were made inside ancient stars that exploded billions of years ago, could they explain the chain of events from the Big Bang to the formation of those atoms to how they ended up on Earth?

description.zh: 评估前往火星的长期太空飞行所面临的工程和人类挑战——辐射暴露、肌肉和骨骼流失、心理孤立、通信延迟——并评估SETI计划的现状：使用了哪些方法，迄今探测到了什么，以及什么是费米悖论。
description.en: Evaluate the engineering and human challenges of long-duration spaceflight to Mars — radiation exposure, muscle and bone loss, psychological isolation, communication delays — and assess the current state of the SETI programme: what methods are used, what has been detected so far, and what the Fermi Paradox is

evidence.zh: 能识别并解释火星任务的至少三大挑战：辐射（无磁层保护）、低重力导致的骨骼与肌肉流失、心理隔离，以及通信延迟。
evidence.en: Identifies and explains at least three major challenges of a Mars mission: radiation (no magnetosphere), bone/muscle loss from low gravity, psychological isolation, and delayed communications

evidence.zh: 描述SETI如何搜寻智慧生命（射电信号、激光脉冲、技术特征），并解释为何迄今未探测到并不等于其不存在。
evidence.en: Describes how SETI searches for intelligent life (radio signals, laser pulses, technosignatures) and explains why the lack of detection so far is not proof of absence

evidence.zh: 能阐述费米悖论（“大家都在哪儿？”），并讨论两种对立的可能解释。
evidence.en: States the Fermi Paradox ('Where is everybody?') and discusses two contrasting proposed resolutions

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果问{{name}}是否愿意志愿参加为期3年的火星任务，他们能否至少描述出三个必须先解决的重大科学或工程挑战——并解释为什么仅20分钟的通信延迟这一点，就会几乎彻底改变任务的运作方式？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was asked whether they'd volunteer for a 3-year mission to Mars, could they describe at least three serious scientific or engineering challenges that would need to be solved first — and explain why the 20-minute communication delay alone changes almost everything about how the mission would operate?

description.zh: 按照离太阳从近到远的顺序说出太阳系中的行星，并使用太空词汇——行星、恒星、太阳、月球、卫星、轨道、太阳系、星系、宇宙、小行星、彗星——在描述太阳系结构和我们天空中看到的物体时正确运用这些词汇。
description.en: Name the planets in our solar system in order from the Sun and use vocabulary for space — planet, star, sun, moon, satellite, orbit, solar system, galaxy, universe, asteroid, comet — applying these correctly when describing the structure of the solar system and objects we see in the sky

evidence.zh: 无需提示，能按离太阳由近及远的顺序说出八大行星。
evidence.en: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun without prompting

evidence.zh: 能正确运用“orbit”描述行星绕太阳、卫星绕行星的运动。
evidence.en: Use 'orbit' correctly to describe the movement of planets around the Sun and moons around planets

evidence.zh: 能正确运用相关词汇区分行星、卫星、恒星和小行星。
evidence.en: Distinguish between a planet, a moon, a star, and an asteroid using the correct vocabulary

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否按离太阳由近及远的顺序说出八大行星的名称，并解释恒星、行星和卫星之间的区别？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} name the planets in order from the Sun — and explain the difference between a star, a planet, and a moon?

description.zh: 在不同季节进行观察，将日照时间与一年中的时间联系起来，注意夏天白天更长，冬天白天更短
description.en: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year, noticing longer days in summer and shorter days in winter

evidence.zh: 描述规律：夏季昼长夜短，冬季昼短夜长。
evidence.en: Describe the pattern: more daylight hours in summer, fewer in winter

evidence.zh: 比较一年中不同时间的日出/日落时间
evidence.en: Compare sunrise/sunset times at different points in the year

evidence.zh: 能建立日照时长与天气及自然界季节变化的联系
evidence.en: Relate amount of daylight to seasonal changes in weather and nature

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}是否观察到夏天睡觉时天还亮着，而冬天则天黑得早得多，并能对此现象作出解释？
assessmentPrompt.en: Has {{name}} noticed that it's still light at bedtime in summer but dark much earlier in winter, and can they explain this pattern?

description.zh: 通过观察太阳、月亮和星星，描述可预测的规律，例如太阳升起和落下、月亮形状的变化以及星星在夜晚出现
description.en: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe predictable patterns such as the sun rising and setting, the moon changing shape, and stars appearing at night

evidence.zh: 描述日出与日落的每日规律
evidence.en: Describe the daily pattern of sunrise and sunset

evidence.zh: 描述月相在一个月左右的变化规律
evidence.en: Describe the pattern of the moon's shape changing over about a month

evidence.zh: 描述夜空中可见的星星，并解释所观察到的季节性变化规律。
evidence.en: Explain that stars are visible at night and describe any seasonal patterns observed

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否描述他们在天空中观察到的规律——比如太阳从东边升起、月亮在几周内形状变化，以及星星在夜晚出现？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} describe patterns they've noticed in the sky — like the sun rising in the east, the moon changing shape over weeks, and stars coming out at night?

description.zh: 利用多个来源的信息来证明地球事件可以发生得很快（地震、火山喷发），也可以发生得很慢（侵蚀、造山运动）。
description.en: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly (earthquakes, volcanic eruptions) or slowly (erosion, mountain building)

evidence.zh: 至少举出两个快速地球事件的例子（地震、火山喷发、滑坡、洪水）。
evidence.en: Give at least two examples of rapid Earth events (earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, flood)

evidence.zh: 至少列举两个缓慢地球过程的实例（侵蚀、造山运动、峡谷切割）
evidence.en: Give at least two examples of slow Earth processes (erosion, mountain formation, canyon carving)

evidence.zh: 能借助文本、图像或视频中的证据，支持区分快变与慢变。
evidence.en: Use evidence from text, images, or video to support the distinction between fast and slow changes

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能举例说明哪些事物会迅速改变地球（如地震），哪些事物会非常缓慢地改变地球（如河流切割出山谷）吗？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} give examples of things that change the Earth quickly, like an earthquake, and things that change it very slowly, like a river carving a valley?

description.zh: 使用专业词汇来描述地球的运动和更广阔的宇宙——自转、公转、地轴、倾斜、轨道、光年、引力、大气层、月相、盈、亏、至点、分点、食——并运用这些词汇解释昼夜、季节和月相的形成
description.en: Use technical vocabulary for Earth's motion and the wider universe — rotation, revolution, axis, tilt, orbit, light year, gravitational force, atmosphere, lunar phases, waxing, waning, solstice, equinox, eclipse — and apply these when explaining day and night, the seasons, and the Moon's phases

evidence.zh: 能正确运用“自转”和“公转”描述地球的两种运动形式，并解释各自产生的结果。
evidence.en: Use 'rotation' and 'revolution' correctly to describe Earth's two distinct types of movement and explain what each causes

evidence.zh: 能描述月相的盈亏变化，并解释月相的成因
evidence.en: Use 'waxing' and 'waning' to describe the Moon's phases and explain what causes them

evidence.zh: 能运用“至日”和“分日”的概念解释四季成因和昼夜长短变化。
evidence.en: Apply 'solstice' and 'equinox' correctly when explaining why seasons exist and why day length varies

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否使用科学术语“自转”和“公转”来解释地球自转与地球绕太阳公转的区别？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain the difference between the Earth rotating and the Earth orbiting the Sun — using the actual science words 'rotation' and 'revolution'?

description.zh: 用地球自转的概念解释昼夜以及太阳在天空中看起来的移动
description.en: Use the idea of the Earth's rotation to explain day and night and the apparent movement of the sun across the sky

evidence.zh: 描述地球绕地轴每24小时自转一周。
evidence.en: Explain that the Earth rotates (spins) on its axis once every 24 hours

evidence.zh: 描述自转如何导致白天（面向太阳）和黑夜（背向太阳）。
evidence.en: Describe how this rotation causes day (facing the sun) and night (facing away)

evidence.zh: 解释太阳视运动由地球自转引起，而非太阳本身运动。
evidence.en: Explain that the sun appears to move across the sky because we are rotating, not the sun

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释清楚，太阳其实并不是在天空中移动——是地球自转让我们看起来像是太阳在动，而这也是昼夜交替的原因？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain that the sun doesn't actually move across the sky — it's the Earth spinning that makes it look like it does, and that's what causes day and night?

description.zh: 从岩层中的岩石构造和化石规律中找出证据，来支持对地貌随时间变化的解释。
description.en: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time

evidence.zh: 能解释岩层（地层）随时间形成，越往下年代越久远。
evidence.en: Explain that rock layers (strata) form over time, with the oldest at the bottom

evidence.zh: 描述不同地层中的化石如何为不同时期存在的生物提供证据
evidence.en: Describe how fossils in different layers provide evidence of organisms that lived at different times

evidence.zh: 运用岩层规律解释地貌在数百万年间的演变过程
evidence.en: Use patterns in rock formations to explain how a landscape has changed over millions of years

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}看到悬崖面上有多层岩石，他们能否解释最底下的岩层最古老，并且任何化石都能告诉我们很久以前那里生活着什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} sees layers of rock in a cliff face, can they explain that the bottom layers are oldest and any fossils tell us what lived there long ago?

description.zh: 描述太阳、地球和月球近似为球体，并描述太阳系中地球和其他行星绕太阳运动的情况。
description.en: Describe the sun, Earth, and moon as approximately spherical bodies, and describe the movement of the Earth and other planets orbiting the sun in the solar system

evidence.zh: 说出太阳、地球和月球大致呈球形。
evidence.en: State that the sun, Earth, and moon are approximately spherical

evidence.zh: 能按离太阳由近及远的顺序说出八大行星，并说明它们都绕太阳公转。
evidence.en: Name the planets in order from the sun and explain they all orbit the sun

evidence.zh: 描述月球绕地球公转，同时二者共同绕太阳公转。
evidence.en: Describe the moon orbiting the Earth while both orbit the sun

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否描述太阳系——地球和其他行星如何绕太阳公转，月球如何绕地球公转，以及它们大致都是球形的？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} describe the solar system — how Earth and the other planets orbit the sun, and how the moon orbits Earth, and that they're all roughly ball-shaped?

description.zh: 用图表展示数据，揭示影子长度和方向每日变化、昼夜循环以及季节性星空图案的规律
description.en: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in shadow length and direction, day and night cycles, and seasonal star patterns

evidence.zh: 测量并记录一天中不同时段的影长和影子方向
evidence.en: Measure and record shadow length and direction at different times of day

evidence.zh: 绘制图表，表示一天中影长的变化。
evidence.en: Create a graph showing how shadow length changes throughout the day

evidence.zh: 能将影子模式与太阳视位置及地球自转建立联系
evidence.en: Connect shadow patterns to the sun's apparent position and Earth's rotation

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否测量一天中不同时间的影子长度，将其绘制在图表上，并解释为什么影子在早晨和傍晚最长，而在正午最短？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} measure their shadow at different times of day, plot it on a chart, and explain why it's longest in the morning and evening but shortest at midday?

description.zh: 支持太阳和星星看起来的亮度是由它们与地球的相对距离决定的观点，理解太阳是一颗相对较近的恒星。
description.en: Support an argument that the apparent brightness of the sun and stars is due to their relative distances from Earth, understanding the sun is a relatively close star

evidence.zh: 能说出太阳是一颗恒星，它看起来更亮是因为离地球近得多。
evidence.en: Explain that the sun is a star, and it appears much brighter because it is much closer to Earth

evidence.zh: 能解释手电筒近亮远暗的类比。
evidence.en: Describe how a torch looks brighter close up and dimmer far away as an analogy

evidence.zh: 论证恒星视亮度差异主要源于其与地球距离的不同。
evidence.en: Argue that differences in apparent brightness of stars are mainly due to their different distances from Earth

assessmentPrompt.zh: {{name}}能否解释为什么太阳看起来比其他恒星亮得多，尽管很多恒星实际上更大——这是因为太阳离我们近得多？
assessmentPrompt.en: Can {{name}} explain why the sun looks so much brighter than other stars, even though many stars are actually bigger — it's because the sun is much closer to us?

description.zh: 解释从地球上看到的月球表面阳光角度变化所形成的月相，并描述日食和月食是如何发生的。
description.en: Explain the phases of the Moon as the changing angle of sunlight on the lunar surface as seen from Earth, and describe how solar and lunar eclipses occur

evidence.zh: 解释月相成因是日、地、月三者相对位置变化，而非地球阴影。
evidence.en: Explains that the phases of the Moon arise from the changing geometry of Sun, Earth, and Moon, not Earth's shadow

evidence.zh: 描述月相在约28天周期内的变化顺序。
evidence.en: Describes the sequence of Moon phases over approximately 28 days

evidence.zh: 区分日食（月球位于太阳和地球之间）和月食（地球位于太阳和月球之间）。
evidence.en: Distinguishes between a solar eclipse (Moon between Sun and Earth) and a lunar eclipse (Earth between Sun and Moon)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}注意到某天晚上月亮看起来像一弯细月牙，而两周后却变成了一个完整的圆，他们能否解释发生了什么变化、为什么会这样，并描述月食期间会发生什么？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} noticed the Moon looking like a thin crescent one night and a full circle two weeks later, could they explain what has changed and why — and describe what happens during a lunar eclipse?

description.zh: 描述太阳系的详细结构，包括卫星、小行星和彗星，比较行星的公转周期和距离，并区分行星、矮行星和其他天体。
description.en: Describe the detailed structure of the solar system, including moons, asteroids, and comets, compare orbital periods and distances of the planets, and distinguish between planets, dwarf planets, and other bodies

evidence.zh: 能按顺序说出八大行星，并各说出一个主要特征。
evidence.en: Names the eight planets in order and gives one distinguishing fact about each

evidence.zh: 描述行星、矮行星、小行星和彗星之间的区别
evidence.en: Describes the difference between a planet, a dwarf planet, an asteroid, and a comet

evidence.zh: 解释行星距日远近与公转周期的关系（距日越远，公转周期越长）
evidence.en: Explains the relationship between distance from the Sun and orbital period (planets further out take longer)

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}正在制作太阳系模型，他们能否描述行星、卫星、小行星和彗星之间的区别，并解释为什么离太阳最近的行星完成轨道运行所需的时间更短？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was making a model of the solar system, could they describe the difference between a planet, a moon, an asteroid, and a comet — and explain why planets closest to the Sun take less time to complete an orbit?

description.zh: 解释四季是由地球绕太阳公转时地轴的倾斜造成的，并区分常见的误解——即四季是由地球与太阳距离的变化造成的。
description.en: Explain that the seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis during its orbit around the Sun, distinguishing this from the common misconception that seasons are caused by changing distance from the Sun

evidence.zh: 解释地轴与公转轨道面呈约23.5°的倾斜角。
evidence.en: Explains that Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5° relative to its orbit

evidence.zh: 描述地轴倾斜如何导致夏季半球接收更多直射阳光，冬季则接收较少。
evidence.en: Describes how the tilted axis causes one hemisphere to receive more direct sunlight in summer and less in winter

evidence.zh: 能指出地球在1月实际离太阳略近，以此反驳“日地距离导致四季变化”的错误概念。
evidence.en: Refutes the misconception that distance from the Sun causes seasons by noting Earth is actually slightly closer to the Sun in January

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果问{{name}}为什么英国是夏天而澳大利亚同时却是冬天，他们能否解释这并不是因为离太阳更近，而是因为地球的哪一半朝向太阳倾斜？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was asked why the UK is hot in summer but Australia is cold at the same time, could they explain that it's not about being closer to the Sun but about which half of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun?

description.zh: 描述宇宙的尺度，包括星系的结构、太阳在银河系中的位置，以及使用光年作为距离单位，并理解为什么太空探索需要极其漫长的时间。
description.en: Describe the scale of the universe, including the structure of galaxies, the position of the Sun in the Milky Way, and the use of light years as a unit of distance, and appreciate why space exploration requires enormous timescales

evidence.zh: 将光年定义为光在一年内传播的距离
evidence.en: Defines a light year as the distance light travels in one year

evidence.zh: 描述星系的结构，并指出太阳是银河系中的一颗恒星。
evidence.en: Describes the structure of a galaxy and states that the Sun is a star in the Milky Way galaxy

evidence.zh: 比较太阳系内天体间距离、恒星间距离与星系间距离，并选用恰当的单位表示。
evidence.en: Compares the distances within the solar system with the distances between stars and between galaxies, expressing them in appropriate units

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果{{name}}听说一颗恒星距离地球400光年，他们能否解释光年的含义、这大致有多远，以及为什么以目前的航天器我们永远无法到达那里？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} heard that a star is 400 light years away, could they explain what a light year means, roughly how far that is, and why we will never be able to visit it with current spacecraft?

description.zh: 把引力描述为所有有质量的物体之间普遍存在的吸引力，解释轨道运动之所以产生是因为引力提供了使物体保持在轨道上的向心力，并比较不同行星上的引力场强度。
description.en: Describe gravity as a universal attractive force between all masses, explain that orbital motion arises because gravity provides the centripetal force keeping objects in orbit, and compare gravitational field strengths on different planets

evidence.zh: 能说出重力是任何两个有质量的物体之间普遍存在的相互吸引力。
evidence.en: States that gravity is a universal attractive force acting between all objects with mass

evidence.zh: 解释轨道运动是因为引力持续改变绕行物体的运动方向。
evidence.en: Explains that orbital motion occurs because gravity continuously deflects the path of the orbiting object

evidence.zh: 比较不同行星的重力场强度，并解释其对重量的影响。
evidence.en: Compares gravitational field strength on different planets and explains how this affects weight

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果问{{name}}，为什么月球既不会飞向太空，也不会撞上地球，他们能否解释这是因为引力不断把它拉入一条弯曲的轨道——就像用绳子抡球一样？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was asked why the Moon doesn't fly off into space but also doesn't crash into Earth, could they explain that gravity is constantly pulling it into a curved path — like swinging a ball on a string?

description.zh: 描述恒星从星云到主序星，再到最终状态（根据质量不同，可能是白矮星、中子星或黑洞）的生命周期，并将恒星的生命周期与比氢更重的元素的起源联系起来。
description.en: Describe the life cycle of a star from nebula through main sequence to its end state (white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole depending on mass), and relate the life cycle to the origin of elements heavier than hydrogen

evidence.zh: 描述类太阳恒星生命周期的各个主要阶段：星云→原恒星→主序星→红巨星→行星状星云→白矮星
evidence.en: Describes the main stages in the life cycle of a star similar to the Sun: nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf

evidence.zh: 解释大质量恒星以超新星爆发终结，进而形成中子星或黑洞。
evidence.en: Explains that more massive stars end as a supernova followed by a neutron star or black hole

evidence.zh: 描述恒星内部通过氢核聚变和氦核聚变生成更重元素的过程。
evidence.en: States that nuclear fusion inside stars produces heavier elements from hydrogen and helium

assessmentPrompt.zh: 如果告诉{{name}}，他们血液中的铁是在数十亿年前一颗爆炸的恒星内部锻造而成的，他们能否解释恒星的生命周期以及元素是如何在恒星内部形成的？
assessmentPrompt.en: If {{name}} was told that the iron in their blood was forged inside a star that exploded billions of years ago, could they explain the life cycle of a star and how elements are made inside stars?
